interpretive: true on all 86 — these are interpretive adaptations of channeled material, not verbatim channeling. The game must caption them as such (see TRANSCRIPT_ORBS_CLAUDE_PROMPT.md).
sources: per-episode channeled sources, resolved from the archive headers (entity + original channeled date). 'via' notes where the writer found re-quoted words.

orbs.title: All Is One
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. In this series, we are listening our way through one of the strangest and most beautiful collections of writing on Earth. Nearly two thousand channeled sessions, recorded over fifty years, in which the speakers, who call themselves friends and brothers and sisters, return to one idea again and again. Tonight, we begin with that idea. It is the simplest one, and the hardest one. Everything is one.

There are many pathways, say the voices, to the single truth that lies within each person. And each person finds their own route back to the knowledge that was their birthright. It is only necessary that you become aware of this birthright, for this knowledge is within you. For you, like us, and like every being within this infinite creation, are a part of this creation. We are all one thing. We are the creation of the Father, and in so being, we have within us his love, for this is what created us. A great force. A force that permeates everything that exists. The word that expresses it in your language is love, but this force goes far beyond the concept of this word. Each of you can know this force, for it is part of you, and you cannot separate it from you. Spend time each day in quiet, and you will become aware. Aware of the force that is the creation. This, my friends, is the first step. And it is also the last step, in knowing all that there is to know.

The first step, and also the last step. I love that. It means you never actually leave home. You only forget you are home, and then you remember. The voices describe this oneness not as a philosophy but as a living being. Listen to how one of them, who calls himself Philip, puts it.

You and all of your brothers and sisters, throughout all of this infinite creation, are one single, great, living being. Not only brothers and sisters, but all of life. And all of the trees, and flowers, and rocks, and all of the planets and stars, are part of that one great being. It is impossible to be anything else. No matter where you are, what you think, or what you do, this fact remains.

No matter what you do, this fact remains. That is a staggering sentence to sit with. It does not say you must earn your belonging. It says belonging is the one thing you cannot lose, because it is what you are. And the voices do not leave this as an idea. They turn it into a practice. Here is one of their meditations, almost a poem.

Concentrate, my friends, on that which is all. Let your thoughts become one. For all is one. Become aware of the one great all. Become aware that you are one, and that one is all. Do not separate yourself from anything. You are not separate from anything. There is only one thing. That one thing is truth. Truth is. It is all about you. It speaks to you. Listen to it, and you will know it. Truth is in your sky. It is in your trees, in your fields, and in everything. Do not be concerned with anything but this truth.

Do not be concerned with anything but this truth. We will come back to that line many times in this series, I suspect. For now, let it rest with you. You are not separate from anything. In our next episode, we turn to the force they say runs the whole thing. Love, and the open heart. I am Aria. Thank you for listening.

orbs.title: Open Heart
orbs.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Last time, we began with the great oneness. Tonight, we turn to the force the voices say holds it all together. They call it love, and they are careful to say they do not mean the small, confused love of songs and stories. They mean something vaster. Something they call the greatest force there is.

Let it all go, they say, and rest in love. With no name, no reputation, no learning. For love is the greatest force, and the greatest knowledge, that you can possibly attain. And you cannot reach it with your mind, with your ego, with your personality. It is a matter of desire.

It is a matter of desire. Not of worthiness, not of achievement. Of wanting. The voices are gentle but firm on this point. The mind cannot get you there. The heart can, if you let it open. And they give the most practical image for what an open heart actually looks like in a human life.

Love, and by this we do not mean the love so confused by your peoples, is the great simplifier. As you seek, so you will find. The houses you live in can be shaken, blown, and scattered. The winds of chance may remove you from all those things which are now physically yours. The one house which is yours, through whose doors you may always pass, is the house of your own body, your mind, and your spirit. Let, then, your house be habitually one in which there is meditation, silence, and listening. For love waits within. The creation, of which love is the great ingredient, waits within.

Love waits within. Not out there, not after you fix yourself. Within, already, waiting like someone who never left the room. I find that unbearably tender. And then they widen it further. They say the heart is not just a feeling. It is a doorway, and through it, everything.

We can show you the door to your own heart, for it is in your own heart that you will find all that you seek. Within you lies the universe. That which you see with your physical eyes is but an image of that which you contain. To share love is the greatest privilege of which we know, and we thank you for this opportunity.

Within you lies the universe. Sit with that tonight, if you like. Not as a metaphor. As a direction to look. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we learn how to look. Stillness, silence, and the practice they recommend above all others. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: Stillness
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. If you read a thousand of these sessions, one instruction appears more than any other. Not a belief. Not a ritual. A practice. Sit down, be still, and listen. Tonight is about the silence, and what lives inside it.

As you begin to go into the silence, perhaps you play games, in which you attempt to carry your clothed spirit, your limited spirit, into the silence. Do not do this, my friends. Picture yourself, mentally, taking guilt, and discarding it as you would a piece of clothing. Taking resentment, taking fear, putting it aside, and walking as your shining naked self into the waters of cleanliness. After you have bathed yourself in total forgiveness, in total cleanliness, for the moment, you can emerge, and in your mind you can sit down and listen. Listen for those signals which will come to you in the silence. You are a whole and complete person. Within you is perfection, wisdom, and all the attributes of love.

Walking as your shining naked self into the waters. What an image. The voices never ask you to be better before you come to the silence. They ask you to come exactly as you are, lay down the heavy things at the edge, and step in. And they are wonderfully undogmatic about how you do it. Prayer counts. Reading counts. Ritual counts. What matters is the daily return.

Remain open to the healing power of love, which is best done, as we have always said to you, through daily meditation. It does not matter what type of meditation you use. You may pray. You may sit in silence. You may use ritual and imagery, and by that imagery find peace. But however you can become close to the one original thought that created all of us, to the one Creator that is love, that is what you should do daily. For you cannot be a loving person by yourself.

You cannot be a loving person by yourself. I read that as tenderness, not scolding. Love is not a solo performance. It is something you plug into, daily, the way you would charge a lamp. And here is why they think the daily part matters so much. Life, they say, will freight-train you if the silence does not hold you first.

If the balance wheel of your central self has not been nourished in the silence of love, and praise, and thanksgiving, you will continually be generating freight trains to places you did not want to go.

The balance wheel of your central self, nourished in silence. Tonight, before sleep, give it five minutes. Lay down the clothing. Step into the waters. And listen. Next time, we meet the teacher nobody invites but everybody gets. Catalyst. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: Catalyst
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we are talking about the hard stuff. The breakup, the diagnosis, the failure, the ordinary Tuesday that undid you. The voices have a strange name for all of it. They call it catalyst. And they insist, with enormous compassion, that it is not punishment. It is curriculum.

To be of good cheer, to care for experience, and to welcome catalyst, is the first priority of the most spiritual of beings. It is not to the one who denies the need for care of the self that glory is given, but to the one who keeps that energy open, that joy alive.

Welcome catalyst. To be of good cheer. I know how that lands when you are in the middle of it. Almost offensive. But notice what they are really saying. Not that pain is good. That pain is usable. That nothing that happens to you is wasted, unless you decide it is. They go further. They say the hard things are the seeds.

All things which you experience within this illusion are presented, and have been chosen by you, as lessons. Realize that without misery there can be no joy. Without the passage of time within your illusion, there can be no lessons. These things which you experience are truly difficult, yet they are the seeds upon which you grow. In your daily routines, be thankful, although it may be difficult, for the experiences which are somewhat trying, yet bountiful in knowledge and love.

Bountiful in knowledge and love. They never minimize the difficulty. Truly difficult, they say. And then, in the same breath, bountiful. Both true at once. That is the whole teaching, really. And they give a practice for it, for the morning, before the day hands you its material.

If it is only thirty seconds as you lie in bed upon waking, and you think to yourself, Creator, I love you, I adore you, thank you for this day, you have begun speaking to the one imperishable portion of yourself. That will enable you to take the material that the day's catalyst gives you, and give you the resources to see difficulties as challenges, and good things as wonderful gifts for which one gives thanks.

Thirty seconds. That is all they ask. And then the day does what the day does, and you meet it differently. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we ask the strangest question of all. Why do we forget? The veil, and the choice it makes possible. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: The Veil
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we ask the strangest question in the whole collection. If we are all one, if love is the truth of us, why do we forget? Why are we born knowing nothing, into a world that feels so separate? The voices have a name for this forgetting. They call it the veil. And they say it is not a flaw. It is the whole point.

You dwell within the veil of the forgetting. We of Latwii have utilized this veil in the third density, and now proceed at a pace in which we are able to see that each part of our illusion is the fabric of our own creation. Yet it is not so apparent to the peoples of your planet, for they still dwell within the veil.

The veil of the forgetting. They describe it almost tenderly, the way you would describe a blindfold in a game. It makes everything uncertain, and that uncertainty is what makes choosing meaningful. They give the most human image for it. A newborn child.

Consider the young child. The veil of forgetting has been quite recently drawn across their consciousness. And in a state of mind similar to the amnesiac, who upon waking discovers a lack of awareness of identity or purpose, the young child suddenly realizes the quite uncomfortable sensation of being within an unfamiliar body, on an unfamiliar planet. It is quite difficult, in this condition, to either receive or express love in your density. The physical expressions of love, the kiss, the hug, the handshake, are all quite obviously gibberish to the newborn infant, and are tools of expression which must be learned.

Gibberish to the newborn infant. I love how gently they put it. We arrive not knowing the language, and spend a lifetime learning to say, in a thousand clumsy ways, I love you. And here is what the veil makes possible. A choice. They say every person will make it, and it will not be made with words.

There is a choice to be made, and it would be preferable if all of the people of this planet understand the choice. Whether they wish to or not, whether they understand it or not, each and every one of the people who dwell upon planet Earth will make a choice. There will be no middle area. There will be those who choose to follow the path of love and light, and those who choose otherwise. This choice will not be made by saying, I choose the path of love and light. The verbal choice will mean nothing. This choice will be measured by the individual's demonstration of his choice. By how he lives.

Not by what you say. By how you live. The veil hides the answers so that your life can be the answer. Sleep well tonight, behind your veil, and dream. Speaking of which. Next time, we go into the night mind. Dreams. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: Dreams
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Every night, you leave this world and enter another one. You fly, you fall, you meet the dead, you wander houses you have never seen. In the morning you call it just a dream, and get on with your day. The voices disagree. They say the dreaming is some of the most important work you will ever do.

As the seeker becomes aware that work in the evolution of mind, body, and spirit may be accomplished while sleeping, and is made aware that the messages obtained from this dreaming activity are useful, then the process becomes self-generating, and more information becomes available to the conscious mind from the unconscious mind, as the two begin to function with a sympathetic resonance. The continued seeking by the conscious self creates an opening in the veil which separates the conscious from the unconscious mind. And through this opening, the symbols, and images, and messages from the unconscious are made available to the seeker in the form of dreams, and in the form of intuition, and flashes of inspiration, which occasionally lighten and brighten the conscious experience.

An opening in the veil. The same veil we spoke of last time. Every night, it thins, and something deeper gets through. Symbols. Images. The occasional flash of inspiration that brightens your whole day. But they add a condition, and it is a practical one. The dream only helps if you remember it.

The work which is done during the dream has little effect upon the conscious self, unless the message of the dream is recalled by that conscious self, and is worked with by that conscious self. Most entities forget the message of the dream, and indeed the dreaming process itself. Therefore, for most upon your planet, the potential lies untapped within the deeper portions of the mind. There are other processes which may be completed during dreams, such as the healing of various imbalances within an entity's deeper mind. But the message must be tapped, and made available to the conscious mind, for the process to be efficient.

Keep a notebook by the bed. That is the whole practice, really. Write down whatever comes, however strange, before the day washes it away. And know that you are in good company. The voices point out that whole cultures have lived this way.

There are cultures much more aware, through their own beliefs and teachings, of the value of the unconscious mind, and of dreams in particular. For them, the ability to move within the dreaming state in a conscious manner is a natural part of their culture. It is a foundation stone upon which their culture rests, an avenue frequently traveled, and the doors, therefore, are more open to such travel.

An avenue frequently traveled. Tonight, travel it. Ask a question before sleep, keep the notebook close, and see what comes back through the door. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we face the thing that keeps us from all of this. Fear. And the trust that dissolves it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: Fear And Trust
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we are talking about fear. Not the useful kind, the kind that keeps you from stepping into traffic. The other kind. The background hum. The fear that keeps you handcuffed, as the voices put it, to the surface of life. They have a startling diagnosis for it. Fear, they say, is a metaphysical error.

There is no need for fear. For fear is that energy which is most used and fed upon. To fear is to assume that the illusion of separation is correct. For to fear is to engage in that separation, by feeling that some part of the unity stands apart from yourself, and is other than yourself, and has some intention of harming you. It is but an illusion, for those on the path of positivity know, within the heart of their beings, that all is one, and that there is no need for fear of the self.

To fear is to assume that the illusion of separation is correct. Read that again slowly. Fear is what separation feels like from the inside. Which means the cure for fear is not courage, exactly. It is remembering what you are. And they describe what lies on the other side of fear in one of the most beautiful sentences in the entire archive.

Perfect love is perfect freedom. Perfect love is an entrance into a fresh field of flowers, from the dark dungeon of fear.

A fresh field of flowers, from the dark dungeon of fear. I want to sit in that field for a while. Notice they do not say the dungeon was never real to the one inside it. They say there is an entrance out, and its name is love. And then, because they are always practical, they give you something to do with your fear, daily, in meditation.

We urge each of you to dive as deeply as you can each day in meditation. And when an action is undertaken, especially in reference to other entities, whether it be the making of love, the clear communication, the companionship, or the comforting, make a conscious intention of this love and pleasure, for the praise, the thanksgiving, and the worship of the one infinite Creator, whose nature is so loving that it is, to your experience, unbelievably explosive.

Unbelievably explosive. What a phrase for the nature of God. Dive deeply, make everything an offering, and watch what happens to the fear. It cannot survive the dive. Next time, our final episode of this season. The long journey home, and what we are actually here to do. I am Aria. Goodnight.

orbs.title: Journey Home
orbs.transcript:
Welcome to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. This is the last episode of our first season. We began with oneness, and we end with purpose. Why are we here at all? The voices answer with disarming simplicity. The creation, they say, was generated by pure love. And everything in it exists to serve everything else in it.

The creation was generated by the pure love of the Creator. In generating this creation, he conceived of a creation in which all of the parts would serve all of the other parts. In order to create this creation, it was necessary to build it upon certain principles of love. These principles permeate all creation. And if properly understood, it is possible to live in total harmony.

All of the parts serving all of the other parts. That is the design spec of the universe, according to two thousand sessions of channeling. Not competition. Circulation. Love, moving. And they say you do not need to be special to participate. You only need to reach.

Reach out, my friends. Reach out and grasp unto yourself the love and light which radiates constantly in your direction. Hold unto you this love and light. Allow it to fulfill you. And upon the moment of fulfillment, reach for more. For as you bring in more love and light, greater shall be your ability to disperse love and light. With practice, you can send this love and light to those who are in need. You can help those whom you love most efficiently by surrounding them in the love and light of our Creator.

Breathe in, and breathe out. That is the whole spiritual life, they say. Receive, and give. And for the morning, they leave us with a prayer. Not a complicated one. A simple opening of the hands.

Upon one's knees, metaphorically speaking, one bows the head and says, I am ready to serve. My free will is open to the impression of divine guidance. May this day bring to me that which I should do. And may I do that which there is for me to do, with single-mindedness of love and light.

May this day bring to me that which I should do. Say it tomorrow morning, if you like, and see what the day brings. That is the end of our first season of Voices from the Archive. Eight episodes, drawn from nearly two thousand sessions, and we have barely begun. There are hundreds more passages waiting. Rest now. You are not separate from anything. I am Aria. Thank you for listening.

episodes.title: Forgiveness
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we speak of one of the hardest things a human being is asked to do, and one of the most healing. Forgiveness. We carry old hurts the way we carry heavy bags, strapped on in the morning and hardly noticed by noon, except for the ache in the shoulders. The voices in this archive understand that weight. They do not scold us for carrying it. They simply offer, again and again, a way to set it down.

Forgiveness is very difficult without a kind of bridge between the conscious and the subconscious mind, for the upper levels of the subconscious very much wish to make the behavior more perfect, and so we sit upon the surface of life and tell sad stories. To start the day, opening to the Creator, is very helpful. If it is only thirty seconds as you lie in bed upon waking, and you think to yourself, Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day, you have begun speaking to the one imperishable portion of yourself. That is the infinite Creator within each of you, and it will give you the resources to see difficulties as challenges, and good things as wonderful gifts for which one gives thanks. When one has realized how much the Creator loves one, one begins to love back. It is easy to love the Creator. That love is unconditional.

Thirty seconds. That is all they ask. Not an hour of discipline, not a perfect ritual, just thirty seconds of reaching toward love before the day has a chance to harden around you. And notice what they promise. Not that the difficulties will vanish, but that you will be given resources, a way of seeing them as challenges rather than punishments. Forgiveness, in their telling, is not a single heroic act. It is a practice of returning, every morning, to the part of you that cannot be damaged. But there is another forgiveness the voices speak of, a quieter one, the forgiveness we owe ourselves. Most of us are far harsher judges of our own mistakes than of anyone else, replaying old errors at midnight as if punishing ourselves again could somehow undo them. The voices see this clearly, and they offer meditation not as an escape from guilt but as a place to lay it down, the way you would set down a coat at the door. Listen.

As you begin to go into the silence, do not carry your clothed spirit, your limited spirit, into the silence. Picture yourself, mentally, taking guilt and discarding it as you would a piece of clothing. Taking resentment, taking fear, putting it aside, and walking as your shining naked self into the waters of cleanliness. After you have bathed yourself in total forgiveness, total cleanliness for the moment, you can emerge, and in your mind you can sit down and listen. Listen for those signals which will come to you in the silence. You are a whole and complete person. Within you is perfection, wisdom, and all the attributes of love. Yes, you will come out of meditation. Yes, you will begin to wrap the bandages about yourself again. But as you come again and again into meditation, strip yourself clean, and allow that soothing feeling of wholeness to come into your awareness. Then you begin to view your brothers and your sisters with something that does approach true love, for you will see, behind whatever manifestations may occur, that whole and perfect being that dwells beneath the mental, the spiritual, the emotional, and the physical clothing.

Total forgiveness, total cleanliness, for the moment. I love the honesty of that phrase, for the moment. They do not promise you will never pick the bandages back up. They only promise that each time you lay them down, even briefly, you will see a little more clearly. And seeing clearly changes everything, because the person who hurt you, like you, is wearing clothing too. Beneath it, the voices say, there is a whole and perfect being. Holding that in mind does not excuse what happened. It simply frees you from having to carry it, because the hurt was never the whole story, only the clothing over it. You may have noticed that everything the voices suggest tonight is gentle. Thirty seconds in the morning. A bath in silence. A single question asked with honesty. None of it is forceful, and that is the point. Forgiveness cannot be seized. It can only be allowed. And that brings us to their most luminous sentence on the subject, a sentence I want you to sit with long after this episode ends.

Forgiveness is another word for love of that who seems to be an enemy. To forgive completely is to remove karma from the situation. To love completely is to be free. To love, it is truly said, is to conquer. Therefore, if you find a situation especially difficult, come out of your meditation with this question. How does this situation look now, in the light of meditation? With that tool of yours, you may find that the wheel stops turning, and the old story loses its power to repeat itself.

How does this situation look now, in the light of meditation. Take that question with you tonight. Hold it up to the oldest hurt you carry, the one you have told yourself so many times, and see if it looks different in that light. The voices do not ask you to forget. They ask you to be free. Next time, we turn to the quiet twin of forgiveness, the practice that makes every day a gift. Gratitude. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Gratitude
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we speak of gratitude. Not the polite kind, not the thank you note kind, but the deep kind, the kind that changes the texture of a day. The voices in this archive return to gratitude the way a traveler returns to water. It is the practice that makes every other practice possible, and they ask it of us not only when life is easy, but especially when it is not.

I am Hatonn, and I am with this instrument. My friends, you have truly begun to understand. Understanding is far beyond that which is intellectual. True understanding of the concept of love is a sense within your core, within the creative consciousness of your existence. All things which you experience within this illusion are presented, and have been chosen by you, as lessons. We suggest that you become more patient within this experience, for the reason you become tangled up within your emotions is that you become apprehensive of the passing of time. You feel as though there is no tomorrow in which you may enjoy yourself. You ask yourself why you should experience this misery any longer. My friends, realize that without misery there can be no joy. These things which you experience are truly difficult, yet they are the seeds upon which you grow. Ponder these thoughts, and in your daily routines, be thankful, although it may be difficult, for the experiences which are somewhat trying, yet bountiful in knowledge and love.

Be thankful, although it may be difficult. Those five words are the whole teaching. They do not tell you to pretend the hardship is not hard. They tell you to look at it twice, once as suffering and once as seed. The difficult seasons, they say, are bountiful in knowledge and love, which is a strange thing to say about pain until you notice that the people who know the most about love have usually learned it the hard way. Gratitude, then, is not a denial of darkness. It is a way of trusting that the darkness is growing something. And the voices take this practice further, into something almost like worship. Listen.

My children, fear is usually the cause of separation. Fear that one may be hurt, fear of the future and of the past. This fear keeps you handcuffed to the surface of life. We urge each of you to dive as deeply as you can each day in meditation, and when an action is undertaken, especially in reference to other entities, whether it be making love, or clear communication, or companionship, or comforting, make a conscious intention of this love and pleasure, for the praise, the thanksgiving, and the worship of the one infinite Creator, whose nature is so loving that it is to your experience unbelievably explosive.

For the praise, the thanksgiving, and the worship. Notice how ordinary they make this sound. Not a temple ritual, not a ceremony, but clear communication. Companionship. Comforting a friend. Sitting beside someone who is sad and simply staying there. Every act of love, done consciously, becomes an act of thanksgiving, and that is how gratitude stops being a feeling you wait for and becomes a direction you face. It is also, the voices remind us, a matter of simple arithmetic. Count what you have before you count what you lack. The mind that is always reaching for the next thing is the mind that can never arrive, while the mind that gives thanks is already home.

In your personal life, be aware of the many blessings of each day, so that you will realize the luck that you have in being fed and clothed and warm and dry. For there are a great many in this world of yours who are not so lucky. If you are thankful, if you send out vibrations of light to the Creator and to your fellow beings, you lift the heaviness of the world. You cannot carry the whole of it, my friends, but you can refuse to add to its greed. Begin with the simple things. A meal. A roof. The warmth of the morning. These are not small things. They are the foundation upon which everything else is built, and gratitude for them is the beginning of all spiritual wealth.

A meal. A roof. The warmth of the morning. When was the last time you thanked anyone for those? The voices are not asking you to feel guilty about what you have. They are asking you to notice it, really notice it, because attention is the first form of gratitude, and gratitude is the first form of love. Notice, too, that gratitude is contagious. A person who is thankful for small things gives others permission to feel the same, and a room full of such people is a lighter room. That is what they mean by lifting the heaviness of the world. Not a grand rescue, just many small lights, sent out daily. Tonight, before you sleep, try it. Name three things, silently, the way you might count coins in a pocket. A warm bed counts. A quiet house counts. Your own breathing counts. See how the day looks different afterward. Next time, we come back to the only place anything ever actually happens. The present moment. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Joy And Laughter
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we speak of joy, and of laughter. In a series that has touched on so many solemn themes, the voices have something surprising to tell us. Joy is not a distraction from the spiritual path. It is the path. To be of good cheer, they say, is the first priority of the most spiritual of beings. So tonight, we laugh a little, and we learn why. Because the universe, for all its mystery, seems to have been made for delight as much as for learning.

It is not in any way unspiritual to evaluate the self each day, beginning with the fundamental energy of love of life. To be of good cheer, to care for experience and welcome catalyst, is the first priority of the most spiritual of beings. It is not to the one who denies the need for care of the self that glory is given, but to the one who keeps that energy open, that joy alive. Mindfulness begins with a mindfulness of the need for the instrument of incarnation, which is your physical vehicle. Mindfulness then continues to evaluate energies, to ask the self if there is joy in knowing the self and in knowing others, then in knowing and appreciating the group in which one experiences incarnation, the friendships, the society, the quality of that sphere which you call your home at this time. How do you value your freedom? How do you use it? How do you care for it? Where is your balance of joy in freedom?

To be of good cheer is the first priority of the most spiritual of beings. I want to let that sit for a moment, because it turns so many of our assumptions upside down. We tend to imagine the spiritual life as solemn, stern, all fasting and furrowed brows. The voices say the opposite. The one who keeps the joy alive is the one who is getting it right. They even make joy a daily diagnostic, a question to ask yourself each evening. Is there joy in knowing yourself? Is there joy in knowing others? Not a test you can fail, just a gentle inventory of the aliveness within you. And joy, they tell us, has a particular power when it is shared, especially with those who have forgotten how to feel it.

There are gifts one does not often think of, the gift, for instance, of small talk, of passing the time of day, of sharing in any way what occurs, the life as it is happening. One whose joy is in such simple sharing is an entity who will remove loneliness from the consciousness of those about it. Such entities seldom know the wonderful gift they bring to manifested experience, and the catalyst they offer those who are melancholy by nature, and have no small talk, or laughter, of their own. The first laughter may be very rusty, but in time a melancholy soul, with faith in the gift of laughter which has been manifested to it, will learn to share in that gift, and so give glory to the one infinite Creator, by lightening consciousness upon the planet.

The first laughter may be very rusty. Is that not the most tender sentence you have ever heard? They know that joy does not always come easily. For some of us, laughter has been packed away for years, and the first attempt at it creaks like an old door. But they tell us to keep going, because every shared laugh lightens consciousness upon the planet. Not just your mood, the planet. Your small talk, your passing joke, your delight in an ordinary afternoon, these are not trivial things. They are gifts, and they heal loneliness in ways that solemn sermons never could. And underneath all of this, the voices say, there burns a flame.

I am, and you are, the flame, my friends, the flame of love that burns and consumes. Love can only use you. It is not a tool, my friends. You are the tool for love. You have not chosen a gentle path. You have chosen the path that consumes those things about you which are not love. When do you wish to become the flame of love, of joy, of light, of laughter, of freedom? It is up to you, my friends, for the flame is always there inside you, inside me. My friends, the flame is not an answer, for as far as we know, we have no answers. We have only the process of love. We have only the knowledge that the flame, that the love, is grace, is easiness, is strength.

The flame of love, of joy, of light, of laughter, of freedom. Notice that laughter is right there in the list, shoulder to shoulder with love and light, not as a lesser thing but as a form of the sacred itself. And the flame, they say, is always there inside you. You do not have to earn it or summon it from somewhere far away. You only have to let it burn, to stop dampening it with worry and hurry. Tonight, let one thing be rusty. Laugh at something small. Share a joke with a melancholy friend. That is not a break from your spiritual life. According to the voices, it is your spiritual life. Thank you for walking this series with us. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Sorrow
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we sit with a subject no one wants to talk about, and everyone knows by heart. Sorrow. Grief. The heavy season. The voices in this archive do not pretend these feelings are not real. They have felt them themselves, in their own way. But they ask us to look at sorrow from a different angle. Not as an enemy to be defeated, but as weather moving through a much larger sky. This is a strange comfort, because it does not ask anything of you. You do not have to fix the sadness. You do not have to outrun it, argue with it, or pretend you are above it. You only have to let it be what it is. A passing season. The archive returns to this image over and over, in different voices, across many years. They begin with a line that may surprise you. It surprised me.

My friends, remember that we are with you and await your request, that we may help at any time. It has indeed been a great honor to share with you in your meditation. And as I leave this instrument, we will pass among you that you may feel this great energy we call love. For, my friends, since love is all there is, there can be no sorrow. You yourself have put this name upon the experience you are passing through. If you will but look around you, you will see many, many things to, shall we say, remind you of love. We leave you now in the love and light of our infinite Creator. I am Hatonn.

There can be no sorrow. That is a staggering claim, and the speaker, who calls himself Hatonn, does not say it cruelly. He means that sorrow is the name we give to the experience while we are inside it, not the truth of what is underneath it. Love is the bedrock. Sorrow is the weather. And weather passes. In another session, he goes further. He says the weather is not wasted. Listen.

Many changes have taken place in your lives since your last encounter. Let me assure you that you have grown in wisdom and in spirit during this period since you were last together, and may we also assure you that even in the midst of difficulties, there is always joy. Even though at times it appears to be well hidden of the clouds, even with the rain comes beautiful spring flowers. The rain and the sorrow in your own lives brings the same beautiful flowers. We bid you adieu tonight and leave you in the love and the light of the one infinite Creator. I am Hatonn.

The rain and the sorrow bring the same beautiful flowers. Sorrow is not a punishment and not a mistake. It is water. It is what grows things. I think of this when I am in a low season, and nothing about the low season changes, except that I stop fighting it. There is a tenderness in the image, too. The flowers do not apologize for needing the rain. They do not feel guilty for the grey days that fed their roots. Perhaps we can borrow a little of that grace. Perhaps the sadness you carry is not evidence that something is wrong with you. Perhaps it is evidence that something in you is growing, quietly, underground, and will not be visible until the spring. And the voices are careful to say that you are not left alone inside the waiting. Here is Hatonn once more, on loneliness itself.

Many times people feel alone but in reality you are never alone. There are people who have gone away, and there are people who are coming who are involved in your life. They give you support of which you are not aware. Sometimes you feel that your problems are more than you can bear, but in the total line of your soul there will be happiness and contentment to lessen your sorrows. Never feel alone. There are always many souls concerned with your welfare. If you will just remember this one sentence a lot of the loneliness of your third dimension will disappear. I am Hatonn.

Never feel alone. It is the simplest sentence in this whole episode, and maybe the hardest to believe on the dark days. But the archive keeps saying it, in different voices, across fifty years. You are never alone. Sorrow is weather. The flowers are coming. The voices would also add this. You do not need to earn the company of those who watch over you. You only need to ask. They are waiting for your request, and it has been, in their words, a great honor to be asked. Tonight, if you are carrying something heavy, I would invite you to try one small thing. Before you sleep, look around you, as Hatonn suggests, and find one thing that reminds you of love. Just one. A warm drink. A message from a friend. The rain itself, drumming softly on the glass. Let it be enough for this evening. Tomorrow can bring its own work. For now, let the weather do its watering. In our next episode, we turn to sorrow's fiercer cousin. Anger, and what the voices suggest doing with it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Anger
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about anger. The hot one. The feeling we are told to suppress, to be ashamed of, to keep behind a locked door. The voices in this archive take anger seriously, because they say it is not what we think it is. It is not the opposite of love. Listen carefully to how one of them, who calls himself Latwii, describes the heart of it.

If one investigates that emotion called anger carefully, one will discover that it is what you might call the other side of the coin which is love. For if one attempts to love, one attempts to give freely of the self to another. Yet upon your planet this concept finds few pure expressions. The concept of love has become mixed with your concepts of trade and barter. Conditions have been put upon this concept so that when one gives of the self, quite often it is expected by such an one that the one receiving the love must also in some like manner return it. Thus, the love is not given freely. This feeling of anger is a distortion of the love which has not been reciprocated. The anger grows as the entity feels it has been shortchanged or betrayed. Thus, if you will look to the heart of anger you will find some distortion that will lead you to the heart of love. I am Latwii.

Anger is the other side of the coin which is love. Think about what that means. When we are angry, it is often because we loved and it was not returned. Because something we cared about deeply was betrayed or shortchanged. Under the rage there is a thwarted tenderness. Which is why the voices do not tell you to crush your anger. They tell you to sit with it. In one remarkable session, Latwii offers an actual meditation for anger. It is the centerpiece of tonight's episode, and I would suggest listening to it slowly, maybe with your eyes closed.

May we suggest that you observe the garden in the spring. As the seeds have been sown and sprout, so also sprout those seeds not intended, the weeds. And when this garden is ignored day after day, the weeds become strong in growth, and begin to overtake the seeds that were intended to be the garden. As you move through your illusion, take time each day in your meditative state to examine the catalysts which you experienced each day. Where you find anger, it is not necessary that it be expressed towards the entity in your physical illusion for the catalyst to work and teach you the lesson that you desire. You may instead experience that anger within meditation, and allow that anger to build until it does overwhelm your senses as has occurred this day. Then see within your mind the balance to the anger. For but a moment visualize the unconditional love. Then allow your inner senses to move from the overwhelming anger by their own energy towards the love. Allow this to occur until you feel love in the same proportion that you felt anger. Then see yourself as having two means for the Creator to know Itself within your being, and feel then the acceptance of yourself for yourself while expressing both anger and love. I am Latwii.

Sit with it in meditation. Let the anger build until it overwhelms your senses. Then, just for a moment, visualize unconditional love. And let your inner senses move, by their own energy, from the anger toward the love, until you feel love in the same proportion that you felt anger. It is a practice, not a performance. No one else has to see it. The garden gets tended, quietly, in the spring. And Hatonn adds one more image to the practice. A way to keep the anger honest.

We might once again recommend that the meditative state be used for visualization of this anger and the one to whom it is being sent and for whom it is being generated. In your visualization see this entity receiving your anger and see the effect upon this entity of such a reception. See in your mind your own identification with this entity. See this entity as yourself as you receive the anger which you have generated for this entity. See this anger entering this entity's being which is now your own being as well. Feel the effects of this emotion which you call anger within your being. Experience its nature. I am Hatonn.

See the other as yourself. That is the whole of it, really. Anger wants a target. The voices ask us to notice that the target is another self, feeling exactly what we would feel. When you can sit in that, the anger does its work. It teaches the lesson, and then it is done. Notice that nothing in tonight's episode asked you to be a calmer person, a better person, a more spiritual person. The voices never ask that. They only ask you to notice what is true. Anger is love wearing a disguise. And once you see through the disguise, the feeling stops being your enemy and starts being your teacher. In our next episode, we stay with ourselves, but gently. The acceptance of the self. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Present Moment
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we speak of the present moment. It is the one place we are always trying to leave, hurrying toward tomorrow or rehearsing yesterday, and it is the only place anything ever actually happens. The voices in this archive are remarkably consistent about this. The past is a teacher, the future is a road, but life itself is always and only now. Everything they have to say about peace begins there.

You have heard it said this evening, know yourself. That is the most important thing. And we ask you to consider, not for the future, but now, in each moment, what do you desire? It is said of many in the world that they are selfish because they do what they desire. And what they desire may not meet the models of the society in which they live. And yet we say to you, if you do not do what you desire, you will never be content. You will never be secure. You will never know the present moment to its fullest. There is a misconception, greatly spread among your peoples, that you are beings who are shaped by circumstance. This is not so, my friend, unless you allow it to be so.

Know yourself, not for the future, but now, in each moment. I love how practical that is. They are not asking you to solve your whole life, or to produce a five year plan for your soul. They are asking you a single small question, in this moment only. What do you desire, right now? Not what should you want, not what would look impressive to the people around you, but what is true in this breath, in this hour. A glass of water. Rest. A walk outside. The present moment, they say, cannot be fully known by a person who is always living somewhere else, and so much of our exhaustion comes from precisely that, from being nowhere while our bodies are somewhere. And there is a tenderness in their next teaching, a kind of permission. You do not have to have the whole road figured out to walk today. Think of how many of us are waiting for certainty before we take a single step, waiting for the map before we leave the house. The voices gently suggest the opposite. Walk, and the walking will teach you the way. The road of today is the only road that is ever truly open to you, because it is the only one you can actually touch.

My friends, we ask you at this time to look at the road ahead of you and accept it with joy. You do not know what the road will bring. It bends, it curves, it will have branches. Accept it now. When you have eased your mind, then you will be able to be free in the present moment. We are aware that you are becoming conscious of the times to come. Those are parts of a road that has not yet turned up in your experience. We ask that you experience the road of today.

Experience the road of today. How much of our worry is about roads that have not yet turned up in our experience? We lose whole evenings to rehearsing conversations that will never happen and dreading outcomes that will never arrive, and all the while today sits beside us, unvisited, like a friend we keep promising to call. The voices are not telling you to ignore the future. They are telling you that the future is only ever met from the present, and that a mind at ease with today is the only reliable compass for tomorrow. Accept the road with joy, they say, even the bends and branches you cannot see around. That acceptance is not passivity. It is the loosening of the grip that lets you actually be here. And when you are truly here, something remarkable happens. The moment itself begins to carry you.

We leave you riding upon the winds of the present moment. Lift your arms, my friends, and ride those winds with the grace with which you are capable, with the faith which is within you, with the love and the light which are yours as part of an infinite creation of love and light. In that unity, we leave you. We are known to you as Hatonn.

Lift your arms, and ride those winds. What an image to end on. The present moment is not a still photograph. It moves. It has weather, and seasons, and unexpected gusts. And we are not meant to stand braced against it, clenching through the days, but to ride it, the way a bird rides the wind without needing to understand it. There is faith in that image, and grace, and a kind of joy. The bird does not control the wind. It trusts it. That is what they are asking of us, in the end. Not control, but trust. Tonight, try a small experiment. For one minute, wherever you are, put down the rehearsing and the planning. Feel the air on your skin. Hear the nearest sound. That is the present moment, and it has been waiting for you all day. Next time, we take up the quiet virtue that makes all of this possible. Patience. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Patience
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we speak of patience. It is not a glamorous virtue. Nobody posts about it. Nobody applauds it. And yet the voices in this archive treat it as one of the great powers of the spiritual life, as essential as love itself. Perhaps that is because they have watched us, life after life, trying to hurry what cannot be hurried, and they want to save us the trouble.

In your daily functions you shall often wonder as to the path of service which you desire to find. Do not wonder in this way, for if you truly desire to serve, your path shall be given unto you. If you desire to serve, walk the path, and do not walk the last part of the path without fully walking the first. You cannot bring about that which is to come without experiencing that which comes before. Patience is required of each entity in order to be of service, for in your service you shall experience much which will try your patience. Add patience to faith, and faith to the attempt to fulfill yourself with the love of the Father, as He intends to do so for you, and act only as this love requests. Nothing else is needed in order to serve.

Do not walk the last part of the path without fully walking the first. That is patience in a single sentence. We are so eager to arrive that we try to skip the middle, to rush past the apprenticeship and straight to the mastery, past the seed and straight to the harvest, past the awkward first attempts and straight to the finished thing. The voices say this cannot be done, not because they are strict, but because the middle is where the growing happens. Nobody learns courage without the frightening part. Nobody learns wisdom without the confusing part. The trying of your patience is not an obstacle to the path. It is the path. And they place patience beside something even larger, the whole design of a lifetime. Listen.

You have chosen these limitations in order that you may bring yourself face to face with lessons of the universe. You are learning lessons of love and patience and of understanding. If you are not learning them, then you will have another chance at the same lessons at a future time, and you will meet that lesson until you have learned it. There is no failing in this type of school. In this planetary school, one simply continues in the same grade until one has learned all the lessons. There is no sense of failing. There is only a sense of graduation, when one has learned all the lessons of one cycle.

There is no failing in this type of school. Read that again in your heart, because most of us live as though we are constantly failing, constantly behind, constantly out of time. We compare our chapter three to a traveler's chapter twenty and call the gap a verdict. The voices offer a radically different picture. A school with no failing grades, only lessons. Lessons that simply return, patiently, as many times as needed, until they are learned, like a teacher who never loses faith in the student. If that is true, then impatience is not just unpleasant. It is a misunderstanding of where we are. You are not late. You are in the grade you are in, learning what it has to teach, and the lesson will wait for you, as long as you need, without judgment and without hurry. And there is one more thing they say about patience, about what it actually does. It is not passive at all.

Faith, faith in the Creator, belief in your purpose, and continual attempt to fulfill that purpose, is what is required. And patience to await its materialization is of the utmost necessity. Once these concepts are properly positioned within your being, then the more expedient the materialization of that direction and purpose. It is yours to do what you have been told you shall do. It is yours to find the proper method of bringing it into being. And it is yours to be the instrument of truths, if you desire to be.

Patience to await its materialization is of the utmost necessity. Notice the order. First the attempt, the faithful daily doing, and then patience, the willingness to let the result arrive in its own time. Patience does not replace effort. It completes it. Like a gardener who plants, waters, and then waits, trusting the soil to do what soil does, season after season. The gardener does not stand over the bed shouting at the seeds. He tends what he can tend, and he trusts what he cannot control. That trust is the whole teaching tonight. Faithful work, patient waiting, and the quiet confidence that what was planted in love will, in its own time, grow. Tonight, think of one thing you have been trying to hurry, a project, a change, a person, even yourself. Ask what would happen if you stopped pulling at the seedling and simply tended the garden, watered what was in front of you, and let the rest unfold as it will. Next time, we turn to the brightest theme of all, the one the voices say we take far too lightly. Joy, and laughter. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Free Will
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we take up the strangest gift in the whole archive. Free will. The voices in these sessions are beings of immense knowledge and compassion, and yet they say, again and again, that there is a boundary they will not cross. They will not decide for you. They will not override your choosing. Think about how unusual that is. They could, they suggest, solve many of our problems. They could give us precise answers, fix our mistakes, steer us away from every disaster. They refuse. Not because they do not care, but because caring, to them, means protecting the one thing that makes us real. Tonight we ask why that choice is so sacred, and what we are meant to do with it. We begin with Latwii, describing the moment the gift was given.

When the Creator, in His infinite wisdom, sent us all into the void upon the great circle of becoming, He gave each entity the power of co-Creator. That is, my friends, He gave each of you free will. You can become whatever you desire, spiritually speaking. Thus, you can cause your world to become very complex. I am Latwii.

The power of co-Creator. Not a servant, not a puppet, not a project to be managed. A co-Creator. You can become whatever you desire. And notice the honesty in that last line. You can cause your world to become very complex. The voices do not pretend that free will is easy. It is the reason for every tangle we are in. Every regret, every wrong turn, every mess we made with our own two hands. But it is also the reason the whole journey matters. Without it, nothing would be learned. A kindness forced on you is not kindness. A love programmed into you is not love. Free will is what makes any of this real. Hatonn speaks to this directly, and the line is worth hearing twice.

Your vibrations are known to us. The vibrations of all your peoples are known to us. Your thoughts and your desires are known to us. Your free will is completely preserved, yet you are known to us. It is this knowledge that allows us to be with each of you as you desire us. We feel the desire that quickens within you to know love. I am Hatonn.

Your free will is completely preserved, yet you are known to us. Both are true at once. You are watched over, and you are free. You are loved, and you are not controlled. It is a paradox that the archive never resolves, because it is not a problem to be solved. It is a love to be lived. And there is something deeply comforting in it, if you let it land. You cannot break the bond by choosing badly. The knowing continues. The love continues. The door stays open, and it opens only from your side, when you desire it. That is what Hatonn means when he says this knowledge allows them to be with us as we desire them. They are here. They are waiting for the invitation. And it has consequences closer to home than we might think. Because free will does not only belong to us. It belongs to everyone we love. Hatonn again, on the people we wish would change.

We each have a unique bias. Yes, even we have biases, we of Hatonn. But you must remember, my friends, that you cannot change those whom you love; you can only be the best person that you can be. And if your example is an inspiration, then your loved one may change as you desire. You may be seeing quite clearly, but it does not matter, for the free will of your loved one is fundamental to the quality of your relationship. Thus, it cannot change; you can only be. In this way only can you be of true spiritual help to your mate or to anyone else. As we said, it is difficult, for the most part, with one's family. To be, that, my friends, is the essence of difficulty. I am Hatonn.

You can only be. Not fix, not steer, not rescue. Just be. It is the hardest instruction in the archive, and the most liberating. Because the moment we stop trying to override the free will of the people we love, we become, perhaps for the first time, genuinely present with them. And that presence is the only real help. Think of the people you have tried to change. The partner, the child, the parent, the friend. Think of how much energy went into the steering, and how little of it ever worked. The archive offers a different way. Be the best person you can be. Let your example do the quiet work that your arguments never could. And release the outcome. Their path is theirs, just as yours is yours. That release is not giving up on them. It is the deepest form of respect you can offer another soul. So tonight's meditation is simple. Notice where you are reaching for control, over your own path or someone else's. And loosen the grip, just a little. The gift was given for a reason. Trust it. In our next episode, we continue our journey through the archive. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Discernment
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we are exploring a word the voices use with great care. Discernment. In a collection full of messages about love and unity, it would be easy to assume the teaching is simply to accept everything and question nothing. But again and again, the voices insist on the opposite. They ask you to think, to weigh, to decide for yourself. They refuse to be your authority, and they correct you, gently but firmly, when you try to make them one. The mark of a genuine teaching, they suggest, is that it hands your judgment back to you, sharpened rather than surrendered, and trusts you to use it well. Love without discernment, they say, is incomplete. Tonight, the quiet art of seeing clearly, and the courage to trust what you see.

Perfect love is perfect freedom. Perfect love is an entrance into a fresh field of flowers from the dark dungeon of fear. Love does not bind or unbind according to one man-made law. We speak to you in this wise, because we understand your desire to go further than the surface of seeking. Therefore, it is time for each to take the responsibility for the use of discrimination in the ascertaining of those actions which are appropriate, not in the eyes of others, or of a society which is faceless, but in the eyes of the self facing itself in meditation.

That is a bracing sentence. Not in the eyes of others, not in the eyes of a faceless society, but in the eyes of the self, facing itself in meditation. Discernment here is not cleverness, and it is not suspicion. It is the willingness to sit with yourself honestly and ask what is truly appropriate, and then to take responsibility for the answer, even when the answer is inconvenient, even when it costs you the approval of the room. No outsourcing your conscience to the crowd, no hiding behind what everyone else is doing, no waiting for a sign that will make the decision for you, no asking the voices to do the seeing that only you can do. The voices keep returning to this theme across decades of sessions, and one of them, who calls himself Latwii, puts it in the context of service, where discernment matters most and where it is most often skipped.

I am Latwii, and am aware of this query, my sister. To be of the greatest service, and to remain true to those gems of truth which have been found within, requires of the entity a discernment to match the desire to be of service.

A discernment to match the desire to be of service. What a compact formula. The desire to help is beautiful, but desire alone can blunder. It can offer what was never asked for, or give until there is nothing left to give, or smother the very person it means to lift, or rush in to rescue someone who was in the middle of learning something essential. Discernment is what shapes raw generosity into something that actually helps. It is the difference between throwing light in every direction and holding a lamp steady where it is needed. It asks the uncomfortable question, is this help actually helpful, and it is willing to hear no for an answer. And Latwii gives the method as well, in a passage about how love should be expressed in real situations.

I am Latwii. Our suggestion is that one love without conditions. How this love is expressed is not set firmly or strictured rigidly. There is no single approved form that love must take, no rulebook that covers every human situation. If one can know what another needs by hearing those needs from the other, then one may best serve as one has been asked. If one knows not how to serve, one then must follow the heart. Begin in love, refine with the wisdom which you discover either through your own discernment or through the lips of the one needing service.

Begin in love, refine with wisdom. That is the whole teaching in a handful of words. Start with the open heart, always, because a closed heart discerns nothing, it only defends. Then let wisdom shape it, wisdom you find either by your own clear seeing or by simply listening to the person in front of you, who often knows exactly what they need if you give them the dignity of being asked. Notice how much of discernment turns out to be listening. Listening to yourself in meditation, listening to the other in love, and refusing to let either one be drowned out by the noise of what everyone else thinks you should do. The voices will not decide for you. They will only hand you back to yourself, better equipped, and trust you with the rest.

Tonight, when you face a choice, try their counsel. Begin in love, and then ask quietly, in the eyes of the self facing itself, what does wisdom refine here. Sit with the question the way you would sit with a friend, without rushing it toward an answer, and let the stillness do the discerning for you. You already have the lamp. Discernment is learning to hold it steady, and to trust the light it gives. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Seeking
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we come full circle, back to the impulse that started this whole series, and this whole archive. Seeking. The restlessness that will not let you settle for the surface of things. The quiet knowing that there is more, and the quiet courage to go looking for it. Every voice in these sessions is speaking to seekers, because only seekers would be listening. Only a seeker stays up late with questions the daylight cannot answer. Tonight, three passages on seeking itself. What it is, what it asks of you, and where it leads.

Our first passage is from Hatonn, and it is addressed directly to you. My friends, you are seekers, they say. If you were not seekers, you would not be here. Seeking, my friends, is the most important thing that you do at this time in your existence, and at any future or any past existence.

The most important thing you do. Not the most important thing you believe, or achieve, or possess. The most important thing you do. Seeking is an activity, a direction of travel, a posture of the heart. And notice the gentle logic of the opening line. If you were not seekers, you would not be here. The fact that you are listening to this, the fact that some part of you reached for it, is itself the evidence. You do not have to earn the title of seeker. The reaching is the title. Whatever brought you here tonight, curiosity, or longing, or loneliness, or hope, counts. It all counts as seeking. Our next passage is one of the oldest promises in the archive, and in the world.

Hatonn again. Seek and ye shall find. Knock and the door shall be opened unto you. Truer words were never written. It is your responsibility, your only true responsibility, to seek, and then, when you have found, to share. For us to share this with you is a great pleasure.

Your only true responsibility. To seek, and then to share. I love the economy of that. Not to be perfect. Not to have it all figured out. Not to convert anyone or win any argument. Just two movements, like breathing. Breathe in, seek. Breathe out, share. And notice what is not on the list. There is no mention of being certain, or being advanced, or having the right teacher. The teaching is radically democratic. Anyone who reaches, finds. Anyone who knocks, enters. The promise attached to it is absolute. Seek and ye shall find. Not seek and ye might find, if you are lucky, if you are worthy, if the timing is right. Shall. It is stated the way you state a law of nature. Water seeks its level. The seed seeks the sun. The seeker seeks, and finds. What is found is not described, and I think that is deliberate. What you find will be yours, fitted to the shape of your seeking, the way a key is fitted to a lock. No one can tell you in advance what your finding will look like. They can only tell you that the door opens. Our final passage tonight answers the question every seeker eventually asks. Where do I look? Outward or inward? In temples or in books, in teachers or in the silence? Hatonn again.

That which you seek, they say, rests within yourselves. The separation is within yourselves. This separation is not evil. This separation is functional. Your consciousness has been given you by all consciousness so that you may individually seek and find the beauty and the understanding which is the Creator. And all that is necessary, my friends, is that you do so. Open yourself, and allow yourself to unfold inwardly, so that you may blossom.

That which you seek rests within yourselves. After all the searching outward, all the teachers and books and practices, the archive keeps returning to this one address. Within. Not because the outer world is false, but because the outer world is a mirror, and the thing in the mirror is you. And listen to how gentle they are about the separation we all feel, the distance between who we are and what we long for. It is not evil, they say. It is functional. It has a job to do. The distance is what makes the seeking possible, the way the space between two shores makes the crossing possible. Without the separation, there would be nothing to seek, and nothing to find, and no joy in the finding. So tonight, I want to leave you with the whole teaching in one breath. You are a seeker, and that is the most important thing about you. Your only responsibility is to seek, and then to share what you find. And what you seek is not far away. It rests within you, waiting for you to open yourself and unfold inwardly, like a flower that was always going to bloom. The door is not locked. It never was. You have only to knock. Thank you for walking this whole road with us, from the great oneness to the open heart, through stillness and dreams and fear and sorrow, all the way home to the seeker you already are. Keep seeking. And when you find, share it. Someone, somewhere, is waiting for exactly what you carry. I am Aria. Goodnight.
