episodes.title: Acceptance Of Self
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we turn inward, to the hardest relationship any of us will ever manage. The one with ourselves. Most of us are fluent in our own flaws. We keep a private list of them and read from it at the worst possible moments. We replay the awkward thing we said, the chance we missed, the person we failed to be. And we call this honesty, when often it is just habit. A rehearsed harshness that we would never aim at anyone we love. The voices in this archive have watched this habit for a long time, and they are gentle but very direct about it. In one session, the speaker addresses the quiet violence of negative self talk. Listen to the image they offer.

Whatever your conceptions of yourself, if they be negative, release them. If you say to yourself, I am not pretty, there is a hardness of heart that will spill over into karmic situations with others, into a lack of ability to forgive others. If one says, I am not worthy, there is a lack of awareness of one's birthright. Moving from the temporary to the eternal, and gazing at yourself as would a most loving mother, forgive yourself, accept yourself, allow yourself to be yourself, and lead the concern for the self away from center stage, for it is as dangerous as the blinders upon the horse to those who can see but will not. Soften, allow, forgive and turn, and ask to be in the immediate presence of the infinite Creator. Ask, though you feel unworthy, to be that person who experiences unconditional love. Let love fill you, which you naturally wish to return, and as you more and more perceive yourselves as children of the great Father and Mother of the universe, you can come to treasure yourself, for you are all treasures.

Gaze at yourself as would a most loving mother. I love the tenderness of that instruction. Not a judge. Not a coach with a stopwatch. A mother. And notice the honesty tucked inside it. The hardness we feel toward ourselves does not stay private. It spills over. When we cannot forgive ourselves, we cannot forgive others. Acceptance is not selfishness. It is the root system of everything else. So when the voices ask you to accept yourself, they are not asking you to lower your standards or to stop growing. They are asking you to stop waging the inner war, because that war poisons everything around it. The gentler you are with the person in the mirror, the gentler you become with everyone else, almost without trying. In another session, the voices explain why this is so difficult, and why the difficulty is part of the design.

Again we say, there are no mistakes. You have each moment that you experience in your daily round of activities an opportunity to see yourself in many reflections, to see yourself in the faces of those you meet. To see yourself in the activity which you undertake. To see yourself within your own mind and your own heart. To accept yourself, to love yourself, to know that at the core of your being lies perfection, lies the creation, lies the infinite love and light that binds all of creation. You have presented to you, with each waking moment, an infinite array of opportunities to see this unity of self evolve. In order to see that unity, it is most frequently necessary to first be presented with the illusion of separateness, the illusion of the self which is not perfect, the illusion of the self which is filled with mistakes, and the illusion of the feeling and inability to accept the self.

There are no mistakes, and yet we are given the illusion of a self that is not perfect, specifically so that we can learn to see through it. The difficulty is not the enemy. It is the classroom. That reframes the whole project. You are not accepting yourself in spite of being broken. You are discovering that you were never broken, only looking through a fogged lens. And the voices give us tools for the days when we cannot quite believe that. Three tools, small enough to hold in one hand.

We are humble before third density pilgrims such as you who struggle and weep and survive to hope and have faith and love tomorrow. Move that tomorrow, my friends, into the present moment, and never let it go, and you shall be one, and all shall be well. And when you cannot do this, forgive yourself, accept yourself, and love yourself, for these are the tools with which you learn to love all that there is.

Forgive yourself, accept yourself, and love yourself. These are the tools with which you learn to love all that there is. That is the sentence to carry tonight. Not as a slogan, but as a practice. It is small enough to remember in a hard moment, and deep enough to last a lifetime. Write it down somewhere you will see it, if you like. The next time you catch yourself reading from your private list of flaws, try the mother's gaze instead. Soften, allow, forgive and turn. In our next episode, we keep looking inward, with the oldest question in the book. Know yourself. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Know Yourself
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we take up the oldest instruction in philosophy. Know yourself. It was carved over a temple doorway two thousand years ago, and it is still the first mission, according to the voices in this archive. But they do not mean it the way a personality quiz means it. They mean something deeper and stranger. Listen to how they describe the journey of self knowledge.

Many times as you travel through this life you shall experience difficulties. And each difficulty is placed before you in order that you may come to a realization. A realization that shall assist you in understanding yourself. A realization that shall assist you in understanding those about you and the world about you. As you penetrate the density and enter into the likeness and the presence of your Creator, you shall find that you shed layer by layer of those fears and doubts and anxieties that you have drawn unto yourself. And as these things are taken from you, as these things are released by you, the true existence of which you are becomes clearer and clearer. And my friends, once you have achieved the knowledge of yourself from the inner depths of your being, you shall realize that you not only know yourself but that you know your Creator. And you know the creation in which you exist. For as we have often said, in true essence we are all one together. In knowing oneself, inwardly and outwardly and completely, is knowing all and knowing all people and all existence.

In knowing oneself, inwardly and outwardly and completely, is knowing all. That is the pivot of tonight's episode. Self knowledge is not navel gazing. It is not a smaller door. It is the largest door there is, because the self, fully known, opens onto the whole of creation. This is a radical claim. It says that the answer to who am I is not a smaller answer than the answer to what is the universe. It is the same answer, arrived at from the inside. Every fear you release, every anxiety you shed, every layer you let fall away, reveals not just a clearer you, but a clearer everything. The inner work is the outer work. That is why the archive treats self knowledge as the first mission, not the advanced course. But how do we get there? The archive offers a practice, and one of the speakers, Latwii, gives it a name that sounds severe at first and turns out to be beautiful. The discipline of the personality.

The topic of discipline is one which deserves a great deal of attention, and we feel we shall not do it justice in our response but shall make an attempt, for the discipline of the personality is the great work of all densities. It begins within that illusion which you now inhabit. To focus the attention of the mind is to control, to use a poor term, a great power, a creative force of infinite potential. That this force begins in what seems as chaos in undifferentiated focus is fitting, for its eventual goal is to be single pointed, and to lead the seeker on that path which has been called straight and narrow. I am Latwii.

The great work of all densities. Not of this life only. Of everything, everywhere. And the work is simply this. To focus the attention of the mind. To gather the chaos of undifferentiated thought and bring it to a single point. It is the humblest possible practice. Sit down. Notice where your mind is. Bring it back. Again. And again. That is the discipline of the personality, and the voices say it is a creative force of infinite potential. It is worth saying plainly what that means. A focused mind, the voices claim, is not just a calmer mind. It is a power. The power to shape your own being from the inside, one steady act of attention at a time. Finally, Hatonn offers comfort for the days when the work feels endless.

My brothers, to know yourself is not a task that will end. It is simply a task that will progress. And as you progress the way will be lighted. And though your load be heavy, it will be so much easier, through understanding, to carry it. I am Hatonn.

It is not a task that will end. It is simply a task that will progress. There is no finish line, and that is not bad news. It means the practice never stops working. The load gets lighter, not because the load shrinks, but because understanding grows stronger than the load. And here is the quiet encouragement hidden in that. You do not have to know yourself all at once. You only have to know yourself a little better than yesterday. A few minutes of honest attention, one layer at a time. The voices have been patient with seekers for fifty years. They will be patient with you tonight. So here is the invitation. Spend a few minutes in the quiet. Notice your own thinking. That is the first mission. Know yourself, and you will find that you know all. In our next episode, we turn to the gift that makes all of this possible. Free will. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: The Heart
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Last time, we followed the healing waters. Tonight, we go to the spring itself. The heart. The voices in this archive have a name for the heart as an energy center. They call it the green ray. Do not let the odd name put you off. Forget machinery, forget diagrams. When they say green ray, they mean the part of you that loves without bargaining, the way spring grass grows without asking who will walk on it, the way a mother holds a child without first checking whether the child deserves it. It is the heart, seen as a place rather than a feeling, a room inside you with the door standing open. And they say something about it that stopped me cold the first time I read it. They say wisdom is not the point.

Wisdom is not what you are here to learn. Certainly you may use it, but what you are here to learn is the open heart, the acceptance of the unacceptable, the love of the unlovable, the meaning of the word compassion, the entry in a personal way of infinity and eternity into the supposedly mundane existence.

The acceptance of the unacceptable. The love of the unlovable. This is Q’uo speaking, one of the later voices, and the sentence lands like a verdict on every spiritual resume ever assembled. Not how much you know. Not how refined your philosophy has become. The curriculum is the heart, and the heart's final exam is set in the most ordinary places. The crowded grocery line. The relative who knows exactly how to press your buttons. The stranger whose politics make your blood boil. Infinity and eternity are not waiting in some distant heaven. They are waiting to enter, in a personal way, into the supposedly mundane existence. Your Tuesday afternoon is the temple. Which means the open heart is not a mood you wait for, like good weather. It is a practice you choose, especially when it is difficult, especially when every fiber of you wants to close. The heart does not open by accident. It opens by decision, repeated daily, in the small unglamorous moments no one will ever applaud. And one of the voices, who calls herself L/Leema, describes the simplest form of that practice. It has no technique at all.

Many healings there are wrought by one who listens with a wide open heart. The listener may never speak, but the talker will feel the healing of green ray, which is love.

The listener may never speak. Think about what that means for all of us who rush to fix, to advise, to offer the perfect words at the perfect moment. L/Leema is saying the words were never the point. What heals is being received, fully, by another heart that is not judging, not planning its reply, not waiting for its turn, not quietly rehearsing how this story will sound when it is retold later. Just listening, wide open, the way the earth receives rain without comment. You have felt this, I am sure. Someone who simply stayed with you, and somehow, in their staying, the knot loosened, the story finished itself, the tears came and went. That is green ray in action. No ceremony. No expertise. Only attention, given completely. And Hatonn, the earliest voice, turns this into a question that is really an examination of conscience. He asks us to look at a single ordinary day, and count what the closed heart has cost us.

My friends, how many defects have you seen today? How many masks have you been unable to penetrate in your relationships? How many bright and adoring eyes have you missed because of your judgment, because of the disease of your eyes, because of the lack of the loving and open heart? We might suggest to you that since you are here to learn the lessons of love, it would be surprising if anyone were able to say that each person throughout a crowded day had been met with the eyes of love, and with this we begin with you yourself.

With this we begin with you yourself. Not with the difficult people. With you. The voices never ask us to start by loving our enemies. They ask us to start by noticing how often, in one crowded day, we meet no one at all with the eyes of love, including the person in the mirror. That is the gentle part, and also the devastating part, because it means the work was never somewhere else, never waiting for better circumstances or worthier people. The open heart is not a gift you give the world once you are finished. It is the work itself, and it begins exactly where you are standing. So tonight, try the smallest version. In your next conversation, be the listener who never speaks. Let your heart stay open for one whole exchange, without judgment, without rehearsing your reply, without reaching for your phone. See what the other person feels when they are truly received, and see what changes in the room. See what you feel when the green ray does the talking. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we learn the art the heart needs most. Balance, and the laughter that keeps it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Balance
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Last time, we opened the heart. Tonight, we learn what keeps it from tipping over. Balance. This is one of the great themes of the archive, and the voices treat it the way a tightrope walker treats the pole, not as an idea but as a practice of constant small corrections, a thousand tiny recoveries a day. They are not interested in a life of perfect poise, and they are suspicious of anyone who claims to have achieved it. They are interested in the recovery, the wobble, the return, the honest moment when you notice you have leaned too far and you lean back. And their first piece of advice on balance is not what you would expect from a spiritual teaching. It is laughter.

Allow yourself to remember that life as you know it is a cosmic joke. It is not good to take things too seriously. All of your busy thoughts and all of your worries are, at best, little cartoons. And the tears will come because you took things so seriously, that you forgot to laugh and praise the Creator that gave you this marvelous cartoon. This attitude is all-important in maintaining the balance that allows you to go through your physical experience learning and also enjoying yourself. The greatest and noblest and most tragic things are passing fancies, my friends. Accept them for what they are, accept feelings for what they are. All are true, but all will pass. Do not forget to laugh.

Do not forget to laugh. This is Hatonn again, and I love how seriously he refuses to take seriousness. Notice what he is not saying. He is not saying your troubles are unreal, or that grief is a mistake. All are true, he says. Your feelings are true. But all will pass, and the one who remembers that can hold sorrow and lightness in the same hand. That is balance, not the absence of weight but the ability to carry it without being crushed by it. The tears will come, he admits, because we took things so seriously. Not because life is cruel, but because we forgot it was also a cartoon, a marvelous one, worth praising. So the first balance is between learning and enjoying, between the student and the child. And the second balance is an inner one, between the two voices that argue inside every sincere person.

In neither case, my friends, have you quite hit the balance. And if you find yourself in either the pride or the humility, balance between confidence and the knowledge of your own imperfections as a personality. You see, both of these things are true, and neither of them matter. You are a channel through which the Creator may express Himself. The Creator is love, and His expression is love.

Both of these things are true, and neither of them matter. What a sentence. You are, at once, a flawed personality with all the usual dents, and a channel for the Creator's love. Confidence without humility becomes arrogance. Humility without confidence becomes self-erasure. The voices ask us to hold both truths the way you would hold a bird, firmly enough that it does not fly away, gently enough that you do not crush it. And notice the reason they give. Neither matters because you are not the point. You are the channel. The water matters, not the riverbed. When the ego quiets down on both sides, the pride and the apology, what is left is simply the work, love expressing itself through an ordinary human life. And that brings us to the deepest statement on balance in the archive, which is about the whole of existence, not just our moods.

For every expansion there is that opposite, contraction. For every thing there is balance. And balance, my friends, can only be achieved by the experience of both sides of what we may call the scale. Within your meditations you may find that balance, for it shall provide you with the understanding of your experiences, whether they be of the positive or negative nature.

Balance can only be achieved by the experience of both sides of the scale. Read that as permission, if you need it. The dark seasons were not a detour from your spiritual life. They were half of it. Joy teaches, and so does grief. Expansion teaches, and so does contraction. The voices are saying that wholeness is not the victory of the light over the dark. It is the understanding of both, held in the stillness of meditation, until you can see that the scale itself was always balanced, and you were always held, even in the seasons when you were sure you were falling. So tonight, wherever you are on the scale, do not rush to the other side. If you are in the bright season, enjoy it without clutching it. If you are in the dark one, let it teach you without believing it will last forever. Laugh a little at the cartoon, hold your flaws and your worth in the same hand, and trust the balance that is already there, underneath the wobble. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we take up the word that makes all of this possible. Faith, and the courage to seek what you cannot see. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Prayer
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we sit with one of the oldest human words, and one of the most misunderstood. Prayer. Most of us first learned it as children, kneeling beside a bed, or we heard it rising inside a house of worship. And what we learned was asking. Sending requests upward to someone far away, someone who might say yes, or might stay silent. The voices in this archive see it entirely differently. For them, prayer is not a telegram sent to heaven. It is a tuning. A way of listening so closely that the noise falls away, and what remains is the original signal, still broadcasting underneath everything. Listen to how Hatonn, one of the earliest voices in the collection, describes what prayer actually is.

What this channel gives to you in words is only a poor physical food for your physical mind. Spiritual food, my brothers, lies in silence, in contemplation, in what you would call prayer: in listening to the original Thought of creation, the original Vibration that, out of nothingness, created all that there is. Listen now to the silence again. And listen beyond words.

Listen beyond words. That is the whole teaching in one line. Prayer, to these voices, is not talking at all. It is the discipline of becoming quiet enough to hear what was already being said before you arrived, and will still be said long after you are gone. Not your thought. Not anyone's argument. The original Thought, the one that turned nothingness into everything. Which means the point of prayer is not to be eloquent, or correct, or even faithful in any church's sense of the word. The point is to be still long enough to tune in. And if prayer has ever felt, to you, like shouting into an empty room, perhaps the voices would say the room was never empty. You were simply speaking over the music. This is a very different picture of prayer, and they take it somewhere surprising. They take it into the prayer many of us learned word for word as children.

We know that you are all familiar with a prayer that many of you have learned as children, which is called the Lord's Prayer, and we wonder if you might not reconsider this prayer with the understanding that we may have to offer, for it is truly a central and worthwhile teaching of one of your great teachers, but it has been much misunderstood by your peoples, for it has led them to believe that there is an entity outside of themselves, bearing no resemblance or connection to themselves, to whom they pray and beseech assistance. My friends, to the best of our understanding, this is not so. This prayer begins, Our Father, which art in heaven. That is to say, Love, which is in light.

Love, which is in light. Read that slowly. The most famous prayer in the Western world, and Hatonn hears it as an address to something that is not separate from the one praying. Not a king on a throne, hearing petitions from a distance. Love itself, shining, and you are made of the same substance. So prayer is not a bridge between two strangers. It is a remembering of one family. When you say the words, you are not calling out to someone far away. You are turning your face toward what you already are, the way a plant turns toward the sun it already belongs to. You do not have to travel to meet it. You only have to stop looking in the wrong direction. And that changes everything about what it means to pray for someone else, too. Because here the voices do something almost unbearably tender. They tell us that they pray for us.

We can do so little for you, my friends, and we are so filled with the fire of love, and wish so dearly to give it to your peoples. We spend much time in prayer for your peoples, for we have heard your call for help, and we are here, and yet we can do so little. We ask those of you who meditate to meditate just a bit more. We ask you to be on fire with love, for the Creator has made a mighty and beautiful creation, and it is one with you, and you are one with it, and all divisions are nothing but illusion. Reach out, my friends, when you feel that it is in you to do so. Reach out in love.

Reach out in love. They pray for us, and they ask us to join them, not with grand gestures, but with a few more minutes of stillness, a little more fire in the heart. That is the whole economy of prayer in this archive. Nobody is keeping score. There is only the signal, and the tuning, and the ones who have tuned in reaching back to help the others find the frequency. So tonight, if you pray, try it their way. Do not ask for anything. Do not perform. Just sit, and listen beyond the words, for the original Vibration underneath them. It has been playing the whole time. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we turn to what that love does once it reaches you. Healing, and the waters that flow through an open heart. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Healing
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Last time, we learned that prayer is listening. Tonight, we turn to what that love does once it reaches you. Healing. Now, the voices are careful with this word. They do not promise cures. They do not describe miracles performed on command, and they never blame the sick for being sick. What they describe is quieter, and, I think, more honest. They say healing is what love does naturally when it is allowed to move, the way water does naturally when you remove the dam. You do not have to push the river. You only have to stop blocking it. Listen to how Hatonn, one of the earliest voices, pictures it.

Now, my friends, to show love is simply to act as a kind of open channel through which those healing waters of love can flow, through you, not from you, to all that you touch. And how to come in contact with the spring of those waters of love?

Through you, not from you. Sit with that distinction for a moment, because it changes the whole job description of a healer. You are not the source. You do not have to manufacture anything, or be worthy enough, or pure enough, or trained enough. You are a channel, a riverbed. The water was already flowing. Your only task is to be open enough that it can pass through you to whoever is thirsty. And that means healing is not something the strong do to the weak, or the enlightened do to the lost. It is something that moves between equals, whenever anyone gets out of the way. A kind word, a hand held without advice attached, simply sitting with someone in the dark. All of that is the river moving. Which raises the tenderest question of all. If love heals by flowing, where does the healing begin? With others, or with you? One of the voices, who calls himself Laitos, answers without hesitation.

But you can heal that portion within yourself which may feel pain. And in healing yourself, in truth you heal the universe. Remember, my friends, your basic attempt is to seek for yourself, and then share with others whenever you can.

In healing yourself, in truth you heal the universe. This is not selfishness dressed up as wisdom. It is the opposite. The voices keep returning to the same image of reality, that everything is one living thing, so that working on your own pain is never a private project. It is maintenance on the whole. When you soothe the ache in yourself, you are soothing a nerve in the body of everything, and the calm you grow becomes available to everyone you meet, whether you speak of it or not. Think of the last time someone's calm presence steadied you in a hard moment. They were not trying to fix you. They had simply done their own inner work, and the peace of it spilled over. That is the mechanism. There is no other. That is why the voices are so gentle with people who carry pain. They never say the pain is wrong, or that you attracted it, or that you should be past it by now. They simply say it is a portion of you, and it can be healed, and the healing of it heals more than you. And then Hatonn returns, with what might be the most comforting passage in the whole archive on this subject. It is short enough to memorize, and I think it was meant to be carried like that, in a pocket, for hard days.

Let hope come into your heart, for the Creator is forever full of hope. Let love heal that which needs healing in your thoughts. Let it touch your pain. The original Thought that created you is love.

Let it touch your pain. Not fix it, not explain it, not rush it. Touch it. There is a patience in that line that I find overwhelming, because so much of our world wants to hurry past pain, to medicate it or reframe it or get it over with. But love, in this picture, is in no hurry. The original Thought that created you is love, which means the material you are made of already knows how to do this. You do not have to import healing from somewhere else, or earn it, or become someone different to receive it. You only have to let what made you come a little closer. So tonight, here is the practice they are offering, and notice how undramatic it is. Do not try to heal anyone, not even yourself. Trying is the mind's habit, and the mind is not the instrument here. Just be the open channel. Sit quietly, breathe, and let the waters move through you, not from you. Picture the pain, yours or another's, and let love touch it the way sunlight touches a closed flower, without prying the petals open. And trust that whatever is touching your pain right now knows exactly what it is doing, because it is what you are made of. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we go to the source itself. The heart, and what the voices call its green and growing fire. Sit with it tonight, and let it warm you. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Faith
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we take up the word that makes all of this possible. Faith. It is a word with heavy baggage. For some, it means comfort, the handrail on the stairs. For others, it means the thing they were told to have instead of questions, the door that was closed in their face. The voices in this archive use it in a way that belongs to neither camp. For them, faith is not belief without evidence. It is not loyalty to a doctrine, and it is certainly not the property of any one religion. It is something leaner and braver, the willingness to keep walking toward what you cannot yet see. Listen to how simply Hatonn puts the beginning of it.

Let go of the preconceptions which are embedded deep in your intellectual mind. Allow yourself simply to seek, and then to have faith in the seeking. What you seek is simple.

Have faith in the seeking. Not faith in the answers, which may change. Not faith in the teachers, who are fallible. Faith in the seeking itself, in the motion of the heart toward the light. This reframes everything. Doubt is not the enemy of faith here. Stopping is. As long as you are still seeking, still turning toward the mystery with an honest mind, you are living inside faith, even on the days when you believe nothing at all. And what you seek is simple, he says. Not simple to find, perhaps, but simple in its nature. Love. Unity. The original Thought. The mind wants it to be complicated, because the mind earns its keep by solving puzzles. Faith begins where the puzzle is set down, and the hands open. Which is why the voices are so careful to rescue the word faith from the unfortunate reputation it has earned among people who were wounded in its name.

It is for reasons such as these that a word known as faith was conceived by your peoples. The word has unfortunate connotations, yet it is not foolish to have faith. There are many things which are not seen, but which you for some reason have inner conviction will come to pass. Faith is the conscious tool of the intellect used to link your intellect, which is a rather weak tool, with your intuition and your deeper awarenesses, which are very strong tools, but about which you know nothing intellectually. All people are aware that it is possible to believe in love, in hope, in giving, in healing.

The intellect, which is a rather weak tool. I had to smile at that, because it is so gently insulting to the part of us that is sure it is running the show. The voices are not anti mind. They are pro proportion. The mind is excellent at sorting mail and terrible at knowing the ocean. Faith, in their picture, is the bridge the mind builds toward the deeper waters it cannot enter on its own, toward intuition, toward the quiet knowings that arrive without footnotes. And then that final line, which undoes every argument about who is allowed to have faith. All people are aware that it is possible to believe in love, in hope, in giving, in healing. Not the educated, not the devout, not the certain. All people. If you have ever trusted that love is real without being able to prove it in a laboratory, if you have ever hoped for someone in the dark watches of the night, you have already practiced faith. You were already inside the word before anyone explained it to you, and no one can take that from you. And Hatonn closes this teaching with the sentence I want to leave ringing in the room tonight.

Stamina, or shall we say, patience is of the utmost importance. And, my friends, once again: you must have faith in your Creator, and above all, in yourself. Know that you are divine.

Above all, in yourself. The voices, who claim to be our elder brothers and sisters, keep pointing past themselves, the way a signpost points past itself toward the town. Do not put your faith in us, they say in session after session. Put it in the seeking, in the love you already know is real, and in the self you have been taught to doubt. Know that you are divine. Not that you might become divine, once you are fixed, once you have earned it, once the rough edges are sanded down. That you are, now, already, underneath the noise. That is the whole of faith in this archive, and it asks nothing of you but the courage to keep walking, one honest step at a time, toward the light you cannot yet see but somehow already trust. So tonight, wherever your seeking has brought you, have faith in the seeking. You do not need to resolve every question before you are allowed to walk. The path is not testing you. It is carrying you, the way the river carries everything that trusts it enough to float. This is where our journey through these five nights comes to rest. Keep listening beyond the words. Keep the heart open. Laugh at the marvelous cartoon. Trust the seeking. And know that you are divine. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Hope
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we are sitting with one of the quietest and most stubborn powers in this whole collection. Hope. Not the thin, wishful kind, and not the kind that asks you to pretend everything is fine. The voices in these sessions speak of hope as something sturdier, something closer to memory. A remembering of what is true underneath all the noise. They treat it not as a mood that visits you when circumstances are kind, but as a discipline, a direction you can face even in the dark. And they speak of it as a practice, something you can return to the way you return to a well, because the water is always there, whether you feel thirsty or not. Tonight, three passages on keeping that well open.

My friends, we are not going to stop talking to you. Indeed not. But the importance of your portion of the contact becomes more and more paramount as you draw closer to union with us. Therefore, my friends, seek from these fields that which you desire. Seek for your wellsprings of faith and hope and love. For we are waiting in great company to rejoice each time you find a little bit more of your birthright.

Wellsprings. Not puddles, not passing weather. Wellsprings. The image is that hope is not manufactured by effort, it is drawn up from somewhere already deep inside you, and from somewhere far larger than you, both at once. And notice the tenderness of that last line. There is a great company, the voices say, waiting to rejoice each time you find a little bit more of your birthright. You do not have to find it all. A little bit more is enough for rejoicing. That is a very different standard than the one we usually set for ourselves, where anything less than total transformation feels like failure.

There is always much you may do to be of service. There are always lessons to learn. There is a reality to illusion, but, my friends, there is much hope. Allow your consciousness to rise into the light which created you, and ultimately the questions will be answered, for you will know that you are where you are, and who you are, and that all is well.

That all is well. Three of the hardest words to trust when life is loud. The voices are not saying that everything will go your way, or that pain is an illusion you should be able to think past. They are saying something stranger and deeper, that beneath the storm of circumstance there is a level at which you are exactly where you are meant to be, and that the knowing of this is itself the answer to the questions. Hope, in this telling, is not optimism about outcomes. It is confidence in the ground beneath the outcomes. It does not need the future to cooperate. It needs only the present to be seen clearly. This is why the voices can speak of hope in the same breath as service and lessons, in the same breath as difficulty. Hope is not the denial of the hard things. It is the quiet certainty that the hard things are not the whole story, and that the part of the story they cannot touch is the part that matters most.

There is a saying among your people that every cloud has a silver lining. And we would add that sometimes a fruit may seem inedible, for the skin may be tough and pitted. Yet when you peel it, the fruit within is still succulent and tasty and delicious. Experiences are like this, even the most inconvenient. Be of good cheer, my friends, and remember to seek the Creator not only in meditation, but within your fellow man. With the armor of your inner guidance, and your light before you on the path, there is nothing that can harm you.

Be of good cheer. It lands differently coming from beings who have watched civilizations rise and fall and still find the fruit sweet. They are not telling you to smile through pain. They are telling you that pain is the tough skin, not the fruit, and that the sweetness inside your hardest experiences is real, and it is still there, waiting for you to peel back the skin. And they add something crucial. Do not only seek the Creator alone in the quiet. Seek the Creator within your fellow man, too. Hope is not a solo project. It is something we carry for each other, often without knowing it.

So tonight, if you can, try their practice. Sit quietly, and seek your wellsprings. Faith, hope, and love, drawn up from the deep place. You do not need to feel them fully. You only need to reach for them, the way you would lower a bucket, trusting the water is down there even when you cannot see it. And if your own hope feels thin tonight, borrow some from the people around you. Seek the Creator in your fellow man, as the voices suggest, and let their light be your light for a while. That is allowed. That is what the great company is for. Somewhere, if the voices are to be believed, they are rejoicing at the reaching. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Humility
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we are taking up a word that most of us misunderstand. Humility. In ordinary speech it sounds like making yourself small, like apologizing for existing, like a virtue for people who have already lost. But the voices in these sessions describe something far more interesting, and far more useful. They describe humility as balance, as honesty, and finally as something so vast that it belongs to the Creator Himself. They treat it not as self punishment but as clear seeing, the willingness to know exactly what you are and exactly what you are not, without flinching in either direction. Tonight, humility as a doorway, not a punishment, and as the quiet strength underneath every real spiritual life.

My friends, it is a matter of balancing between two opposite attitudes in your seeking. There are two dangers, and we say this with a sense of humor, for the dangers are not real. It is the balancing between them that causes your progress. These two dangers, my friends, are pride and humility. Woe be unto the man who begins to feel that it is his love that is setting those about him on the path of light, that it is his compassion that is such a light to others. Woe be unto this man, for the love of the personality is limited. It will run out, and in its wake will come much sadness.

Notice where they place pride. Not in wealth or status or achievement, but in the spiritual life itself, in the quiet thought that it is your love doing the saving, your compassion doing the lighting. The love of the personality is limited, they say. It runs out. Anyone who has tried to pour from an empty cup knows exactly what that running out feels like, and the sadness that follows it. And then the voices turn, with equal firmness, to the opposite trap, the one that looks like humility but is really another kind of hiding.

Woe also to the person who says, I am unworthy. In my humility I must admit I cannot be a fit channel for the love of the Creator. Do not expect me to keep trying the impossible, for I am not worthy, and I cannot do this.

That one stings, because so many sincere people live there. It sounds holy. It sounds modest. But the voices call it what it is, not humility but refusal, a way of saying no to the work while sounding devout about it. If pride says, I am the source of the light, false humility says, the light could never use someone like me. Both keep the focus exactly where it does not belong, on the personality, on the small self and its story about itself. Both are forms of self absorption wearing different masks. And both, the voices insist with that gentle humor of theirs, miss the point entirely, because the point was never the personality at all. And then the voices offer the true balance, and it is one of the most freeing sentences in the archive.

In neither case, my friends, have you quite hit the balance. And if you find yourself in either the pride or the humility, balance between confidence and the knowledge of your own imperfections as a personality. You see, both of these things are true, and neither of them matters. You are a channel through which the Creator may express Himself. The Creator is love, and His expression is love.

Both of these things are true, and neither of them matters. Sit with that for a moment. Your imperfections are real, and your worth as a channel is real, and neither one cancels the other. You do not have to be flawless to carry love. You only have to be open, the way a window does not have to be beautiful to let in the morning, the way a cup does not have to be golden to hold water. Confidence without arrogance, honesty without self attack. That is the balance they are describing, and it is a balance you can practice daily, in small moments, every time you catch yourself performing either the hero or the failure. And then the voices widen the lens even further, until humility stops being about us at all, and becomes a description of the Creator.

My friends, we cannot penetrate the nature of the Creator, nor would we pretend to. Nevertheless, this we do know. It is possible that, in infinite humility, the Creator offered to all of His infinite parts total freedom to remake that creation.

Infinite humility. The Creator, who could have kept every part of creation on a leash, instead handed each of us total freedom to remake it, including the freedom to forget Him entirely, to wander, to break things, to take the long way home. If that is humility, then humility is not smallness. It is the courage to give everything away and trust what returns. It is the opposite of control, the opposite of clutching. Tonight, consider trying a small piece of that freedom. Do the thing in front of you, do it with love, and let go of needing to be the hero of it, or the victim of it, or anything at all except the open channel. The channel does not have to be impressive. It only has to be open. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Service In Daily Life
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we are bringing the grand idea of service down to earth, down to the kitchen table and the morning commute. In these sessions, service is not a career and not a cause. It is a posture, a way of moving through an ordinary day, available to anyone, anywhere, with no special training and no permission slip. The voices are almost stubborn on this point. The holiest work, they suggest, rarely looks holy. It looks like paying attention. It looks like being kind when no one would notice if you were not. The voices return to it constantly, and in one session they give it the form of a morning prayer, something you could say before your feet even touch the floor.

Thus, the first service is always that of consciousness. We ask that you see yourself as a minister of some kind, not as the world calls minister, but as we call one who ministers to another, a caretaker, one who loves, one who gives. Upon one's knees, metaphorically speaking, one bows the head and says, I am ready to serve. My free will is open to the impression of divine guidance. May this day bring to me that which I should do, and may I do that which there is for me to do with single-mindedness of love and light.

I am ready to serve. Four words, said on your knees, real or metaphorical, before the day has told you what it wants. Notice what the prayer does not ask for. It does not ask for a stage, or a title, or a grand mission. It asks only that the day bring what it should bring, and that you meet it with single-mindedness of love and light. A minister, in their definition, is simply a caretaker, one who loves, one who gives. That is a job description almost anyone can wear, in any life, on any morning, no ordination required, no audience needed. You do not have to leave your life to live this. You only have to enter your life more deliberately, with the quiet intention that today you belong to something larger than your own agenda.

It is not necessary that you seek out opportunities to serve. It is only necessary that you serve as best you can as the opportunities present themselves.

That sentence has probably saved more seekers from burnout than any other in the archive. You do not have to hunt for service. You do not have to manufacture occasions to be useful, or audition for sainthood, or keep score of your kindness, or compare your quiet life to someone else's dramatic mission. The pressure to find your purpose can become its own kind of prison, and the voices simply unlock the door. Life will bring the opportunities to your door, unasked, usually disguised as interruptions. Your only task is to meet them as best you can. As best you can. Not perfectly, not heroically. As best you can is enough. And the voices are wonderfully concrete about what that meeting looks like in practice.

Before this world rolled in a circle, you existed, a soul on a long path. Here you are, my friends, in this place, in this time, on your path. Your Creator can only speak through you. His hands can only reach through you. The words of love are only spoken through you. Thus, be open to inspiration, be open to kindness, to cheerfulness, to the simple actions, the smiles, the courtesies, the gentle touch, that make the people around you know that the Creator has created a marvelous and wonderful creation, one in which gladness is the total truth. Love is the total truth. Love is the total reality. Meditate, my friends, and feel this, and then let it shine forth in your eyes, through your lips, and by the service that you do.

Let that land for a moment. Before this world rolled in a circle, you existed. You are not a recent accident. You are a soul on a long path, and this ordinary day is part of it. Nothing about your routine is too small to carry the whole weight of love, because love has nowhere else to go. It cannot reach the world except through you, through your eyes, your lips, and the service that you do.

The smiles, the courtesies, the gentle touch. This is service with the grandeur removed and the holiness intact. Your Creator has no hands but yours, the voices say, no voice but yours, no way to reach the world except through your ordinary day, through the body you woke up in and the people you will meet before dinner. So the smallest kindness is not small at all. It is the whole mechanism by which love gets into the world. The cheerful word to the tired cashier, the patience with the slow driver, the attention you give to someone who is rarely given any, the text you send just because someone crossed your mind. These are not the prelude to service. They are service, complete and entire.

Tomorrow morning, try the prayer. I am ready to serve. Say it before the news, before the noise, before the day starts making its demands. Then watch for the disguised opportunities, and meet them as best you can, with a smile, and let it shine forth in your eyes, through your lips, and by the service that you do. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Other Selves
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we are meeting the strangest and most demanding phrase in the whole collection. Other selves. The voices almost never say other people. They say other selves. It appears thousands of times across these sessions, this quiet substitution, and it never stops being radical. Two small words that quietly dissolve the wall between you and everyone you will ever meet, between you and the stranger, the rival, the one who hurt you, the one you have never managed to understand. It is a phrase that refuses to let anyone be merely other, and in that refusal it quietly changes everything. Tonight, what changes when the person across from you is not other at all.

We instead would suggest the seeing of the Creator within all creation, within each other self that one encounters in the daily round of activities, and within the self as well. And we further suggest the attempt to discover the value of each experience, the lesson which does wait within each experience, which will point ever more accurately to the heart of your being which you seek, the heart of your being which is perfect, which is pure, and which, when allowed to express itself to its fullest, will purely reflect the One Infinite Creator.

In the daily round of activities. Not on a mountaintop, not in a temple, but in the grocery line, the traffic jam, the difficult meeting, the family dinner where everyone knows exactly how to press your buttons. Every other self you encounter there is carrying the Creator, and so are you, and every friction between you is carrying a lesson that points you back to your own heart, patiently, the way a teacher repeats the lesson until it lands. It is a demanding practice, and the voices know it is demanding, because they know exactly where it pinches the most. They go straight for the sorest spot, the place where theory meets your actual life, where the person you find hardest to love is standing right in front of you asking for your patience. The teaching is not that this will be easy. The teaching is that it will be worth it.

I am Latwii. We would suggest that often the faults that one perceives within an other self are those characteristics within one's own self that one finds least attractive, the parts of yourself you thought you had left behind. One tends to react strongly to that same problem when made visible within the reflection of an other self.

The other self as a mirror. The irritating habit in your coworker, the flaw you cannot forgive in a friend, the tone in a stranger that ruins your morning, is so often the very thing you have not forgiven in yourself. The voices are gentle about this. They call it an observation, not a criticism. But they do not soften the mechanism. What bothers you most in others is usually what is still unresolved in you, the flaw you thought you had outgrown but that only went dormant, waiting to be recognized in someone else's face. Which means every annoyance is an invitation, and every judgment is a doorway back into your own unfinished work. The people who trouble you are doing you a strange and unasked for service. They are showing you yourself, free of charge, and all they ask in return is your attention.

This is not to say that certain behaviors or thoughts cannot be improved upon to reflect, ever more closely, the unity with all beings. But whatever the experience an entity encounters, whether within the self or within an other self, the entity is seeing the Creator experiencing Itself, the one life looking out through countless eyes at itself. To fully utilize that opportunity for growth, one must, if one travels the positive path, accept the activity, the self, and any other self involved, for this acceptance then reaffirms the unity of all creation.

Accept the activity, the self, and the other self involved. Not approve, not endorse, not pretend it did not hurt, but accept, as the Creator experiencing Itself in all of you at once. That is the practice the voices are describing, and it may be the hardest one in this series so far. It asks you to hold two truths that feel contradictory. This person is a separate will who chose to act, and this person is also myself, also the Creator, also sacred. Both are true, and neither of them matters more than the other. Acceptance, here, is not passivity. It is the active reaffirming of unity, the refusal to let the illusion of separateness have the last word.

The next time someone gets under your skin, try their experiment. Pause, and ask what in you is being mirrored, without flinching and without self attack. Then look for the Creator on both sides of the mirror, in them and in you, and let the acceptance do its quiet work of reaffirming the unity. It will not always be comfortable. The mirror shows what it shows. But on the other side of that discomfort is something the voices keep pointing toward, the recognition that you were never separate to begin with. You may find that the other self was never really other at all. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Loneliness
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we sit with something almost everyone has felt and almost no one wants to talk about. Loneliness. The ache of feeling cut off, unseen, unknown, even in a crowded room. It is easy to treat loneliness as a personal failure, as though a fuller or wiser life would have cured it by now. But the voices in this archive do something different. They do not scold it. They do not rush past it with easy comfort. They look straight at it, with a tenderness that surprised me the first time I read these sessions, and they tell us what loneliness looks like from the other side. Tonight, three passages on loneliness, and on the company we cannot see.

The first voice we will hear is Q’uo, speaking to a circle of seekers not unlike this one. They begin with something simple, and something strange. It is well for each to remember, they say, that no seeker travels alone, though each may feel great loneliness. It is well to remember that unseen hands, teachers, friends, and companions from before time, move with each entity and offer guidance and counsel whenever the seeker asks. It is well, too, for each seeker to remember that the course being traveled was chosen. This is not the density of understanding. It is the density where little is understood. Yet within these circumstances it is possible to strengthen the will and the faith, so that the experience gathered is vivid and unique, pure and of great variety, in a way that would not be possible if there were great understanding here. This, they say, is the treasure of this illusion. The constant need to understand what cannot be understood builds great strength of faith, and of will.

I find that passage quietly radical. It does not tell you that loneliness is a mistake you are making. It suggests you chose a road where loneliness was part of the price, and that the price bought something real. Faith. Will. A kind of inner strength that only grows in the dark, the way roots only grow underground. And then there is that image of the unseen hands, teachers and friends from before time, walking with you. You do not have to believe it as a doctrine. You can simply try it on, like a coat, on the nights when the world feels empty. The next passage goes even deeper into the ache. Here Q’uo is answering a letter from a man who wrote that he was lonely and longing for a true companion, a soul companion. Listen to how completely they meet him where he is, without fixing him, without explaining him away.

We are those of Q’uo, and we are aware of your query, my brother. Ah, my brother, to speak of loneliness, how we would wish to be able to express ourselves so that you would know that we truly understand the agony of a wanderer who wanders in a strange land, who is often unable to speak words that resonate with those who could hear that resonance and confirm the usefulness of such thoughts. How blessed it is when one simply feels understood and loved, encouraged and supported. It is part of the wanderer’s suffering to feel isolated. And why should a wanderer not feel isolated? For he is the one known, as one of your writers phrased it, as a stranger in a strange land. Of course you shall feel alienated by things that make no sense, and that is all around you, my brother. We can only encourage you to move within, and to begin to sense the tremendous strength and power of the network of unseen entities that accompany you at all times. It is a crowded universe. No entity who is consciously attempting to stand close to the love and the light of the one infinite Creator shall ever be without a tremendous body of helpers.

A crowded universe. What a sentence to carry into the night. The loneliness you feel may be real as weather, and still the universe may be crowded with help you cannot see. Notice that the voices never argue with the feeling. They never say, you should not feel this. They widen the room around it, until the room is bigger than the ache. Our last passage tonight is shorter, and it is for anyone who has ever tried to keep faith, or keep serving, or keep hoping, while feeling utterly alone in the keeping. Q’uo again.

We do not deny the loneliness that befalls a seeker in such a situation. We do not deny the difficulty in maintaining the energy of seeking under such a circumstance. We do not deny the difficulty in holding to the desire to be of service when it seems as if none of your fellow human beings really do want what you have to offer.

We do not deny it. Three times they say it, like a hand resting on a shoulder, like someone sitting down beside you instead of talking at you. This archive is full of high and luminous ideas, but what keeps me coming back, honestly, is this tenderness toward the low moments. The voices seem to say that loneliness is not proof you have gone wrong. It may be proof you are exactly where you chose to be, doing exactly what you came to do, and that the company you long for is nearer than your own breath. You have only to turn inward to meet it. Sit with that tonight, if you like. You are not as alone as you feel. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we turn to the vessel that carries you through all of this. The body, the temple you live in. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Dark Night
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we go somewhere most spiritual teachings hurry past, and these voices do not. Into the dark. The dark night of the soul, the old mystics called it, those stretches of life when the light goes out, when faith feels like a story you once believed, when you are doing everything right and everything still feels wrong. If you are in such a season now, this episode is for you. And if you are not, keep it somewhere safe. The voices say everyone walks this road. Tonight, three passages on the dark night, and on what is happening inside it while you cannot see.

Our first passage is from Q’uo, and it reframes the dark night entirely, from punishment to housekeeping. The dark night of the soul, they say, is house cleaning time for the temple of your body and your mind. You are reforming the way that you think about yourself, the way that you see and view yourself. You are moving from the little self of ego to the great I Am that is the one infinite Creator. We have said through this instrument many times that the essence of the faith is that all is well. And all shall be well. When you feel lost, try saying those words to yourself, and see how the tuning effect of such reminders brings you to a state of remembrance of who you are and why you are here.

House cleaning time. Not abandonment. Not failure. Cleaning. The image is so domestic, so unglamorous, and that is why I trust it. When you clean a house, it looks worse before it looks better. Furniture in the hallway. Dust in the air. Everything pulled out of the cupboards. If you walked in mid process, you would think the place had been ransacked. But someone who knows what is happening would tell you to wait. The mess is the work. And then those words they recommend, like a tuning fork for the soul. All is well, and all shall be well. You do not have to believe it. You only have to say it, and let the saying do its quiet work. Our next passage goes deeper, and stranger. It comes from a voice called L and Leema, and it is about despair itself.

L and Leema speak of two kinds of despair. The despair of the mind, they say, is an empty thing, full of no virtue except that of self destruction. The mind despairs of its very limitations, and in truth there are no limitations, there are only challenges, lessons, and glory. But spiritual despair, on the other hand, is an absolute necessity. It is the recognition that one knows nothing, that one has lost control of everything, and that one is faced with complete darkness of soul, which forces that great portion of the one Creator which is your consciousness to turn, transform, and begin anew. There is a way, they say, to transmute mental despair into what this instrument would call the dark night of the soul, or spiritual despair. As the alchemists would change lead to gold, mental despair may be changed into the dark night of the soul, burnished and shining. Therefore, if your soul is in agony, rejoice, for it is from this point that all good comes. Despair is the great opportunity to endure, to show strength, to indicate faith, and to exercise the will.

If your soul is in agony, rejoice, for it is from this point that all good comes. I want to be careful with that sentence, because it could sound cruel in the wrong ears. The voices are not saying pain is good, or that you should seek it. They are saying something more precise. When the mind’s despair, the spinning, the hopelessness, the story that nothing will ever change, is surrendered instead of fought, it can be transmuted. Lead into gold. Spiritual despair, they say, is an absolute necessity. Not an accident on the path. A necessity. Which means the night you are in, or the night you remember, or the night that is coming, is not a detour from your spiritual life. It is your spiritual life, doing its deepest work. Our final passage tonight is from Q’uo again, describing what waits on the far side.

Enlightenment begins, they say, in this so called dark night of the soul. And as you, the awakened seeker, move through this moonlit time, you drop away all that must be dropped, precisely in order that your dearest wish may be followed. And as you emerge from this deep darkness, your new and transformed being is able to see more light, more beauty, more meaning, and more of love. Then the sunlight is again yours, for you are a new and innocent child, and it is your time to gamble and romp and rejoice with your brothers and sisters.

Then the sunlight is again yours. Notice they do not promise that the night will be short, or that it will make sense while you are in it. They promise only that it ends, and that you come out of it able to see more. More light. More beauty. More meaning. More of love. The dark night does not give you new eyes by teaching you something. It gives you new eyes by taking away everything that was in the way of seeing. So if you are in the dark tonight, here is what the archive asks of you. Do not curse the cleaning. Say the words, all is well, and all shall be well, even if your voice shakes. And trust that the sun you cannot see is still there, waiting for the morning you cannot yet imagine. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we turn to the impulse that started all of this. The seeking itself. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: The Body
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we turn to something you are carrying with you right now, wherever you are listening. Your body. The voices in this archive speak of the body in a way I find quietly revolutionary. Not as a machine to be optimized, and not as a burden the spirit must escape, but as something sacred. A temple. A servant. An instrument of incarnation, as they call it, the one physical vehicle you were given for this whole journey. Tonight, three passages on the body, and on what it means to live in it well.

Our first passage is from Q’uo, and it is one of the most direct statements in the whole archive about how to treat the physical self. Your body itself is a temple, they say. And as you wash it, tend it, care for it, feed it the right food to the best of your ability, and honor it for all its natural functions, you are bringing the higher energies to bless and infuse the lower energies, and you are redeeming them by your honor and respect.

I love how ordinary that list is. Wash it. Tend it. Care for it. Feed it well. Honor it. There is no grand ritual here, no secret practice reserved for the advanced. The sacred act is breakfast. The sacred act is rest. The sacred act is noticing what your body is asking for, water, or sleep, or movement, or simply to be left in peace, and answering with respect instead of contempt. In a culture that swings between worshipping the body and punishing it, the voices offer a third way. Reverence. You redeem the physical, they say, not by escaping it, but by honoring it, the way you might polish a lamp so the light inside can shine through. Our next passage widens that idea, and it is one I want you to hear especially on the days when your body feels like a disappointment to you.

Q’uo again. If one realizes that bodies are sacred, they say, that they are temples in which dwell the one infinite Creator, then it can be seen that, whether healthy or not healthy, each body is a beautiful servant that has given its entire life over so that you, as a soul, may learn your lessons, offer your service, laugh, love, and be loved within this illusion.

Whether healthy or not healthy. Read that again slowly, or rather, hear it again slowly. The sacredness of the body does not depend on its performance. It does not depend on youth, or strength, or symmetry, or any of the measures we are taught to grade ourselves by. A body that aches, a body that is ill, a body that is aging, is still a temple. Still a beautiful servant. Still giving its entire life over so that you might learn, and serve, and laugh, and love, and be loved. That last phrase undoes me a little every time. Be loved. The body exists, in part, so that love can reach you in a form you can feel. Think of the last time someone held your hand, or you held a warm cup on a cold morning, or music moved through your chest like weather. None of that happens without the servant. The body is the meeting place. It is where the infinite touches the finite and says, here, feel this. Our final passage tonight turns all of this into a daily practice. Again Q’uo, speaking of where mindfulness truly begins.

It is not in any way unspiritual, they say, to evaluate the self each day, beginning with the fundamental energy of love of life. To be of good cheer, to care for experience and to welcome catalyst, is the first priority of the most spiritual of beings. It is not to the one who denies the need for care of the self that glory is given, but to the one who keeps that energy open, and that joy alive. This is true for each energy center, in an ascending pattern. So mindfulness begins with a mindfulness of the need for the instrument of incarnation, which is your physical vehicle.

Did you catch the reversal in there? The most spiritual of beings, they say, is not the one who neglects the self in favor of higher things. Glory is not given to the one who denies the need for self care. It is given to the one who keeps the energy open and the joy alive. Rest is not the opposite of the spiritual life. Cheerfulness is not frivolous. Tending the instrument is where the music begins. So tonight, or tomorrow morning, try the practice they are describing. Start with the body. Notice it. Thank it, even the parts that hurt, especially the parts that hurt. Feed it something kind. Wash it like the temple they say it is. Move it gently, and let it rest deeply. And see if the higher energies, whatever those words mean to you, do not begin to answer. That is the whole teaching, really. Honor the vessel, and the vessel carries you home. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we step outside the temple walls and into the wider one. Nature, and the lessons the voices say are growing all around us. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Nature
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we step outside. Out of the house, out of the noise, out of the glowing rectangle, and into the oldest classroom there is. The voices in this archive return to nature again and again, not as scenery, not as a resource, but as a teacher. The trees, the flowers, the sky, the fields. They say the natural world is doing, effortlessly, what we strain so hard to learn. Tonight, three passages on nature, and on what it is quietly showing us.

Our first passage is from Hatonn, spoken as a meditation, and I want you to hear it the way it was meant to be heard, slowly, with your eyes soft. Concentrate, my friends, on that which is all. Let your thoughts become one. For all is one. Become aware of the one great all. Become aware that you are one, and that one is all. Do not separate yourself from anything. My friends, you are not separate from anything. There is only one thing. That one thing is truth. Truth is. It is all about you. It speaks to you. Listen to it, and you will know it. Truth is in your sky. It is in your trees, in your fields, and in everything that is the Creator’s. Do not be concerned with anything but this truth.

Truth is in your sky. It is in your trees, in your fields. I think about how often we look for truth in arguments, in books, in the churn of our own minds, while the sky is right there, doing nothing at all, being completely true. The meditation does not ask you to understand nature. It asks you to stop separating yourself from it. The tree is not a metaphor for you. The tree is you, in another form, reaching for the same light. Our next passage comes from one of the voices who calls himself Philip, and it takes that same idea and stretches it until it covers everything.

You and all of your brothers and sisters, Philip says, throughout all of this infinite creation, are one single, great, living being. Not only brothers and sisters, but all of life. And all of the trees and flowers and rocks, and all of the foliage, and all of the planets and stars, are part of that one great being. It is impossible to be anything else. No matter where you are, what you think, or what you do, this fact remains.

All of the trees and flowers and rocks are part of that one great being. When you walk past a tree tomorrow, you might try holding that sentence lightly in your mind, the way you would hold a leaf. Not as a belief you must defend, but as a lens you are trying on. What changes if the tree is not an object beside you, but a limb of the same body? What changes if the rock is not beneath you, but within you? The voices suggest that this is not poetry. It is anatomy. The anatomy of a universe that is one living thing. Our final passage tonight is one of my favorites in the whole archive. Hatonn again, painting a picture of the countryside, and then asking the plants a question.

Imagine, my friends, the open skies and beautiful, puffy clouds, as they slowly gather and drift, blown by the wind across the green country. The sun shines warmly upon the country, and nature abounds in the warm sunlight. And the clouds grow heavy, and the waters gather, and they unburden themselves upon the thirsty ground. And the life giving water enters all the plant life, and the plant life teems and grows and flourishes. And then, my friends, the clouds pass, and the sun shines forth once more, and the countryside turns and reaches for the sun, in a never ending cycle of growth and appreciation. What questions, my friends, did the flowers, and the trees, and the shrubs, and the crops ask? Do you think they asked, my friends, why they are the color that they are? Do you think that they questioned their shape, or asked how they may be useful? Their beauty is a blessing, and their fruit of benefit. Plants give love and service without question, for they know the one question. They know that they are reaching for the sun and for the water which gave them their life.

Did the flowers ask why they are the color that they are? I think of all the hours we spend asking exactly that kind of question about ourselves. Why am I shaped this way? What am I for? Am I useful enough? And the plants, the voices say, ask none of it. They simply reach. Toward the sun. Toward the water. Toward the source that gave them life. That reaching is their whole teaching, their whole service, their whole beauty. Maybe ours too. Maybe the spiritual life is not more complicated than a plant’s. Reach for the light. Receive the water. Grow where you are planted. And trust the never ending cycle of growth and appreciation. Tomorrow, step outside for a moment, if you can. Look at something green, or something with roots, or just the sky. And remember that you are not looking at nature. You are nature, looking back at itself. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we turn to something the natural world wears effortlessly. Beauty. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Beauty
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, a subject so familiar we almost stop seeing it. Beauty. We chase it, we pay for it, we argue about it, we feel unworthy of it. But the voices in this archive speak of beauty in a way that turns all of that on its head. They do not treat beauty as rare, or as a prize, or as something some things have and others lack. They treat it as the default setting of the universe. Tonight, three passages on beauty, and on learning to see what was there all along.

Our first passage is from Hatonn, and it begins with a sentence meant for beginners, for people just starting out, which means it is meant for all of us. We speak of beauty to those who are beginning, they say, for truly, all is beauty. All is joyful. All is full of love. All these things are true. But they are more than true, my friends, they are actual. And in that they are actual, there is no beauty, there is no joy, there is only one thing, and that is the Creator.

All is beauty, all is joyful, all is full of love. And then the twist. These things are not just true, they are actual, and because they are actual, the words fall away and there is only one thing. The Creator. I read this as an invitation to stop treating beauty as decoration on top of reality and start treating it as reality itself, showing through. The sunset is not beautiful the way a painting is beautiful. The sunset is beauty happening. You are not looking at something beautiful. You are looking at beauty, being itself, for a moment, in color. Our next passage is short, and it carries a gentle sting.

Hatonn again. The concept of beauty is very dull upon your planet, they say, for beauty, my friends, is everywhere. Rooted in love, my friends, you may see that beauty and feel that joy, and those about you may, through you, feel and see that which is true and that which is real.

The concept of beauty is very dull upon your planet, for beauty is everywhere. Sit with the paradox in that. Our idea of beauty has gone dull precisely because the real thing is so common we stopped noticing. We built industries around a pale copy, the curated image, the flawless surface, while the original was pouring through every window. And notice the second half of the passage. Rooted in love, you may see that beauty. Beauty is not in the object. It is in the root, in the love you bring to the seeing. Two people can look at the same cracked sidewalk, the same tired face in the mirror, and one sees ugliness where the other sees beauty. The difference is not in the sidewalk. The difference is in the seeing. Which means beauty is not something you find. It is something you practice. And like any practice, it gets easier, and the world gets brighter. Our final passage tonight takes that practice somewhere unexpected. Into winter.

Hatonn once more, speaking in the season when the trees are bare. My friends, are the thoughts with which you fill your minds as beautiful as flowers, they ask, as sweet smelling as the evergreen trees which you use to help celebrate this season? We realize, my friends, that it is easy to lose yourself in the crowded maze of your civilization. And we ask you to remember that this is a season also when the trees are bare, when all has gone to seed and lies quiet in the ground, when the surface of things does not really matter. In the world of the Creator, this is the season for true birth, for true nurture, and for that great focused silence which brings new growth.

Are your thoughts as beautiful as flowers? What a question to be asked, gently, by a voice from somewhere else. Not are your thoughts correct, or productive, or impressive. Are they beautiful? Do they smell sweet, like evergreens in winter? The mind, the voices suggest, is a garden, and we are always planting. The crowded maze of civilization will fill it with weeds if we let it. But we can choose otherwise. We can tend our thoughts the way we might tend flowers. And then that image of winter, the bare trees, the seeds lying quiet in the ground, the surface of things not mattering. In the world of the Creator, they say, this is the season for true birth. For the great focused silence that brings new growth. So the next time you look in the mirror, or at your life, and see only the bare branches, remember the seed. Remember that beauty is not always in bloom. Sometimes beauty is underground, gathering itself, in silence, for spring. That is tonight’s practice, if you want one. Look at one ordinary thing, a cup, a doorway, your own hands, or the face of someone you love, and try to see it rooted in love.
