See if the beauty that was always there does not come forward to meet you. Next time on Voices from the Archive, we enter the season the voices call by its old name. The dark night of the soul. I am Aria. Goodnight.

trees.name: Grove of Wonder
trees.suggested_biome: high mountain meadow, near the flight paths

episodes.title: Wonder
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about wonder. Not the kind you are told you are supposed to feel. The real kind. The kind that arrives unannounced and stops you in your tracks, and leaves you a little changed. The voices in this archive take wonder seriously. They speak of it as something that has been slowly trained out of us, and as the natural condition of the child. And they speak of it as something we are meant to find our way back to. Listen to how Latwii draws the difference between the wonder we are told about, and the wonder that is real.

In one case, a person reads that there is nothing so beautiful as a rose, and he sees the picture of a rose, and perhaps even goes to the store and purchases such a blossom and puts it in his vase, and observes it, having been told that this is a beautiful blossom. This is programming from outside. There is, however, another way of observing this same flower, and that is with a shock of recognition, as a miracle. When one sees a rose at dawn on a spring day, with the dew still hanging from the tiny petals, with a bee still fluttering about it making honey, and the miracle and the wonder of this rose sink deep into your own understanding, then it is yours. It has come from inside. Perhaps it cannot be communicated. I am Latwii.

Two ways of seeing. One comes from the outside, from being told. The other comes from the inside, like a shock of recognition. You cannot force it, and you cannot quite explain it to anyone else, and that is part of what makes it real. The voices suggest that wonder is not something you add to life. It is something you notice when you stop filtering life through everything you have been told about it. It is the difference between knowing that a rose is beautiful because someone said so, and being ambushed by the rose at dawn, the dew, the bee, the whole impossible fact of it. And that capacity, they say, is childlike. Not childish. Childlike. Here is Q'uo, describing what childlike wonder actually does in us.

My friends, there is always space for creative expression in your incarnation, in your daily life. Even in those moments or tasks that you feel require a more logical approach, a more mature approach, there is always space for the childlike wonder that removes judgment, that fully accepts the moment for what it is, that opens the arms to embrace it and to utilize it in its fullest extent, to see it for its infinite nature. I am Q'uo.

Hear it slowly. Childlike wonder removes judgment. It fully accepts the moment for what it is. It opens the arms to embrace it. This is not a vague feeling. It is almost a discipline, though it does not feel like one. It means meeting the ordinary Tuesday afternoon, the waiting room, the commute, as if it had an infinite nature. Because, the voices insist, it does. The wonder is not reserved for mountaintops and cathedrals. It is available in the task you think requires only logic, only maturity. The arms can open anywhere. But there is a sadness woven through all of this, and the voices do not shy away from it. In one session, someone asked Q'uo the question many of us carry. It seems, the questioner said, that as we mature, we lose our childlikeness, and perhaps it was never meant to be lost. How do we walk the line between mature awareness and a playful, expressive, childlike wonder? Is that something we should even try to do?

That child within each of you, that begins life with such joy and excitement upon observing every new piece of experience that comes before its notice, is the child energy which, if it continues throughout the lifetime, gives one the openhearted and openminded nature that sees all people and all experience as that which enhances one's own being. That child identity is always present in some fashion, and will respond with great glee and joy when it is recognized and allowed to have its say and to have its play, for the child identity is more closely aligned with the universal energies of love and light. If you wish to once again contact that inner child that exists within the heart of your being, it is well to provide it with the same kinds of unique and inspiring opportunities for learning new experience that you devise for yourself in whatever direction your interests take you. You are thus able to make this child within a playmate once again. I am Q'uo.

Make this child within a playmate once again. That is the whole invitation. Not to become childish, not to abandon the seriousness of adult life, but to let the child have its say and its play. The voices are clear that this is not a small thing. The child energy, they say, is more closely aligned with the universal energies of love and light. It is still there, waiting, and it responds with great glee and joy the moment it is recognized. So tonight, if you like, try something small. Give the child an interesting opportunity, the way you would plan an outing for someone you love. Walk a different street. Look at one ordinary thing as if you had never seen it before. It has come from inside, Latwii said. Perhaps it cannot be communicated. But it can be noticed. And once noticed, it changes the seer. In our next episode, we turn to something that has always carried wonder on its back, whether we notice it or not. Music. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Music
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about music. Not about songs you like, or genres you prefer, but about music as the voices in this archive hear it. To them, music is not entertainment. It is closer to the structure of things. It is what creation sounds like when you finally get quiet enough to listen. In one early session, Hatonn leads the group on a small journey of the imagination. It begins in a field, and it ends somewhere the ears cannot follow alone.

I would like all of you now to go with me to a field in which the odors of flowers are heavy in the air. We ask you to relax now. Stand with your feet on the springy, soft green grass. Feel the warm sun beaming down upon you, upon your shoulders, your head. Listen, my friends, to the music of creation. Feel the love and the light in its physical incarnations within the creation of your universe. We ask that you meditate. If you listen to us ever, you will hear us ask this. Within meditation, you may find the key that will open the door. No matter how many times we tell you this, it will never be enough. Meditate and listen. The love will be beating against your ears. And look. The light will be flooding your inner eyes, and touching you in many, many ways. If you will only listen and see and understand, within. I am Hatonn.

The love will be beating against your ears. That is such a physical image, is it not. Not a metaphor for thinking about love, but love as something you hear, the way you hear weather. Something that arrives at the senses before the mind has a chance to argue with it. The voices return to this again and again. Music is not decoration laid on top of reality. It is reality, perceived truly. And if that sounds grand, consider how far they are willing to take it. In another session, Hatonn speaks of the heartbeat of the universe itself, and describes each star as sounding its own note in a music vaster than any concert hall.

As this heart of love pulses, my friends, so does the entire creation pulse, sending forth the slightest variation on the universal signal, which is the beat of the universe as it contracts and flows forward. Much has been made of your astrology, but we say to you that the most vital portion of this art is the specific note of the music of the heartbeat which pulses from each of your stars, and, in a larger sense, of your galaxy. I am Hatonn.

Each star, sounding its own note. The galaxy as a chord. It is a beautiful image, and I confess I keep returning to it on clear nights, when the sky is doing its quiet work above the streetlights. But the voices do not only point outward, to the stars and the turning heavens. They also point inward, and downward, to the music that is already playing in the room you are sitting in, in the sounds you learned to tune out years ago. In one lovely passage, Hatonn speaks of having spent the evening simply listening to the sounds of nature around the group, the night creatures, the wind, whatever the dark was doing. And then he says something I want you to hear slowly, because it rearranges everything.

We have been listening to the sounds of nature that you hear around you this evening. We have been enjoying the music that your surroundings continuously play for you, my friends. Many are the lessons with which you now face. As you grow, each new lesson seems harder, but each new lesson is another facet of the ones you have been dealing with. The new facet will help you to further open yourself to the love, the light. The music surrounds you. It is you. I am Hatonn.

The music surrounds you. It is you. Four words, and they turn the whole search inside out. If the music is you, then you do not go looking for it. You stop covering it up. The practice, as always with these voices, is not to acquire something new, but to remove the noise that keeps you from hearing what was always playing. The traffic, the worry, the commentary running under everything, these are not the music. They are the static over it. And underneath the static, the note goes on, the one that has been sounding since before you had a name for it. So tonight, when this episode ends, give yourself one minute. Just one. Listen to the music your surroundings are continuously playing for you. The hum of the room, the night sounds through the window, the distant traffic, the silence underneath all of it. It has been playing your whole life, whether you were listening or not. The voices ask very little of us, in the end. Not belief, not understanding, not even agreement. Only this. That we pause, now and then, and let the world be audible. The kettle, the rain, the voice of someone we love in the next room, these are not interruptions of the music. They are movements in it. And when we listen that way, even for a minute, something in us remembers what we are made of. Not silence. Song. In our next episode, we follow the sound inward, to something even simpler, and even closer. The breath. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Night Sky
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the night sky. It may be the oldest spiritual teacher we have. Long before there were books or buildings, there was the dark, and the points of light in it, and the human animal looking up and feeling, all at once, very small and strangely at home. The voices in this archive return to the stars again and again, not as astronomy, but as medicine. Something to be taken regularly, and on an empty schedule. Hatonn begins with a gentle correction to the way we see.

As you look up at the stars, my friends, that which you see is inconceivable. Indeed, before your so-called science developed instruments capable of measuring and classifying that which the eye sees when gazing at the night sky, the majority of the inhabitants of your planet felt that they lived inside a dome through which there were tiny holes, and therefore through which at night the great light beyond the sun could be seen. You are dwelling at this point in your experience within a physical vehicle which is inconceivable. Yes, my friends, you are very used to your bodies and therefore do not find them astonishing. Yet could you, without seeing a form, develop the intricate system of your body? The universe of man is a universe in which those things which are the true mysteries are often those things which are most taken for granted and unexplored, while man turns his excellent mind to the creation of artifacts of his own making. I am Hatonn.

The true mysteries are often those things which are most taken for granted. Your own body. The stars. We build instruments to measure the heavens and forget to be astonished by them. The voices are not against science here, not exactly. They are for astonishment. They are saying, do not let the measuring replace the seeing. Do not let the explanation stand where the wonder stood. And then they go further. In one session, Q'uo was given no question at all. No topic, no request, only an open invitation to speak about whatever it wished. And this is where the night sky carried the whole answer, as if the stars themselves were the subject that had been waiting underneath every other subject.

You have opened to us a vast array of things to speak about, by asking us to choose our own subject this evening. We would, however, find all possible threads of thought and concept harmonizing into information concerning love. And yet that basic message remains utterly simple and infinitely profound to us. The simplicity of oneness, of Creator and created, the richness provided by free will which has showered the manifested universe with countless worlds, countless civilizations, and infinite motion and energy and thought. As you gaze up into the night sky and see the stars sprinkled like sand across the blackness of the ether, know that there are more ways than you can see stars on the clearest night to speak of love. And yet all speaking and manifestations end in one thing, that same Love that created all that there is. I am Q'uo.

More ways to speak of love than there are stars on the clearest night. And every one of them ending in the same place. It is a staggering image, and it does something subtle to the listener. It makes love as large as the sky, and as available as the sky. You do not have to go anywhere to find it. You do not have to earn an invitation. You have only to look up. But there is one more passage I want to share, and it is for the nights when the sky is not beautiful to you. For the nights of real darkness, when nothing feels like a sign of anything, and hope feels like a rumor. One of the voices once described the seeker as being, in the inner sense, in darkness, searching for knowledge of love and light and unity. And then it offered this, like a hand in the dark.

The only light which is visible, in the inner sense, to the seeker is paralleled by the light of the night sky, the stars, and the reflected light of the moon. In the inner sense, that star is called hope or faith. It is not a light which takes away the darkness, but it is a signal, a sign if you will, that light there is, and light abundant.

That star is called hope or faith. Not a light that takes away the darkness, but a signal that light is there, and light abundant. On the hardest nights, the voices do not promise you daylight. They promise you a signal. A single star is enough to prove that the darkness is not the whole story. So tonight, if the sky is clear where you are, step outside for a moment. Look up. Let yourself be inconceivable for a while, the way Hatonn suggested, one more taken-for-granted mystery standing under the others. And if the sky is cloudy, remember the signal anyway. It is still there behind the clouds, the way love is still there behind everything, whether or not you can see it. In our next episode, we come back down to earth, and to each other. Compassion. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Water
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, water. The simplest thing on Earth, and maybe the strangest. We drink it, we wash in it, we are mostly made of it, and we weep it. The voices in this archive mention water again and again, and they never treat it as just a substance. To them it is a teacher, and tonight we will hear three of its lessons. Cleansing, flow, and stillness. We begin with cleansing. Here is Latwii.

We ask you to lift up your hearts now, my friends, for we vibrate in the light and in the light there is no disharmony. We ask you to let these things drop away and to cleanse your soul as you would a garment, rinsing it in the cool, clear waters of a mountain stream until it is completely and utterly cleansed. I am Latwii.

Rinse your soul the way you would rinse a garment. I love how ordinary this image is. Not a grand ceremony, just laundry. The voices are always doing this, taking something lofty and handing it back to us in the language of a household chore. The water is already here. The mountain stream is already running. You do not have to manufacture your own purity. You only have to let the water do what water does. And notice what the water does not ask of you. It does not ask for an explanation, or an apology, or a long account of how the garment got dirty. It just rinses. That is the whole teaching of cleansing. You are not scrubbing yourself clean. You are being rinsed, by something that loves to rinse. But cleansing is only the first lesson. Water also flows, and it refuses to linger. Here is Oxal.

Do not linger in the river of your life, but move onward to the sea, dissolving yourself in love. In this way, karma ceases to become your reality, and your love may be freely taken and freely given, with forgiveness to all men for all things. I am Oxal.

Do not linger in the river of your life. How much of us wants to stop, to cling, to build a little dam out of memory and complaint and say, this far and no further. But the river is not for lingering. It is for carrying you. And notice where it is carrying you. Not over a cliff, not into some void, but onward to the sea. The river of your life has a destination, and that destination is love, and the sea is big enough for everything you have been holding back. When you dissolve into it, the old accounting stops. The debts and the credits, the scorekeeping of who hurt whom and who owes whom, all of it simply ceases to be your reality. Love can be freely taken, and freely given. Forgiveness is not a favor you do for someone else. It is what happens naturally when you stop clinging to the bank and let the current take you. That is the second lesson. The third is stillness. And for that we turn to Hatonn, in one of the most beautiful images in the whole archive.

We speak of unity using water as a symbol, for water is indeed a very appropriate symbol for the path that each of you, as drops of water, may understand himself to be taking as you seek the infinite sea of the creation. A drop of water may seem to be quite powerless, and you as an individual may feel lacking or limited in some way in some situation. But, my friends, water is continuous and is not separated from itself. It may fall in drops in service to the fruits of the earth, but as it gathers and moves towards the great oceans, does it not carve out mighty channels? Water is quiet, and yet when stirred can be the most mighty of forces, changing physical landscapes in minutes. In your meditations, then, my friends, take each limitation and lack that you may feel, each disappointment that you feel in yourself or in others, and offer them up as drops of water, to see them dissolve in a pure, clear ocean of the infinite Creator. Then, my friends, let the rainbow of sunlight through this water fill your heart. I am Hatonn.

You are a drop, and you are also the ocean. That is the whole of it. The voices say it gently, but they say it plainly. You may feel small, powerless, limited. A single drop seems like nothing. But water is continuous. It is not separated from itself. And when the drops gather, they carve canyons. Water is quiet, and yet it reshapes mountains. Think about what that means for a life like yours. The small daily things, the quiet kindnesses, the meditations no one sees, these are drops, and drops gather. Tonight, try the meditation Hatonn suggests. Sit quietly. Take one limitation, one disappointment, just one. Offer it up as a drop of water. Watch it dissolve in the pure, clear ocean of the infinite Creator. See the sunlight coming through the water like a rainbow, and let it fill your heart. And then notice your own body. You are mostly water yourself. The blood moving in you, the tears you can cry, the breath moist on your lips. You are not separate from this teaching. You are made of it. That is what water has been trying to tell you all along. That you are not separate. That you are the sea. In our next episode, we turn to the element the voices say is the very substance of everything. Light. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Light
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, light. If there is one word the voices repeat more than any other, it might be this one. They greet us in the love and in the light, they speak of light as if it were a person they know, and in one session they say something that stops me every time. Light is not just a metaphor for them. It is the actual substance of things. Not a symbol of the sacred. The stuff the sacred is made of. The substance of which you are made. Here is the voice who calls himself Latui.

Light, my friends, is the substance of which you are made. Light is the substance of which I am made. Light is the substance of which everything is. Love is the substance which forms light into the forms that you know as living beings, as planets, as trees, as stars, as air. It is all one substance. This substance, my friends, can be affected only by love. I am Latui.

Light is the substance, and love is the sculptor. Sit with that for a moment. You are not a solid object with a soul tucked inside. You are light, shaped by love into the form of a person. The stars, the trees, the air in your lungs, all of it is the same substance, moved by the same hand. This is why the voices are never interested in dividing the world into sacred and ordinary. A tree is light. A stone is light. Your own body is light, slowed down and folded into a shape so that love could have hands. And this substance, Latui says, can be affected only by love. Nothing else touches it. Not force, not cleverness, not achievement. Only love moves light. Which means the deepest changes in your life will never come from pushing harder. They will come from loving more truly. And the teaching gets more intimate still. Here is Hatonn, in one of his simplest and boldest lines.

I am love, and I am Hatonn, and I am light, and I am Hatonn. You are love and you are light. You and I are the same. You experience one thing. I experience one thing. But yet we are the same. For this is the creation. We are one. I am Hatonn.

You are love and you are light. It is not a compliment. It is a description. The voices do not say you could become light if you try hard enough, or that you were light once and lost it. They say it as a plain fact, the way you might say the sky is blue. And notice the equality in it. You are love and you are light. You and I are the same. The speaker is not claiming to be brighter than you. He is claiming that brightness is not a hierarchy. It is a shared condition, like being wet in the same rain. Whatever you have done, whatever you have failed to do, whatever you believe about your own worthiness, none of it changes the substance. It can only change whether you remember it. The forgetting is real, and the voices never deny the forgetting. They only say it is not the truth about you. It is a condition you are passing through, like weather. And there is a reason light carries such power in their teaching. Here is Hatonn again, explaining what light can do, and why no one is left out of it.

When love created material, the material it created was light. Light is creation, and all that is within creation is light. That is why light has the power to comfort, to bind, to unbind, to heal, to do all things, my friends. Light is the very stuff of which the universe, the galaxies, the constellations, the creation itself is formed, and the energy of love which free will causes to move, moves within that light and through that light into all those which are of the light. And my friends, there are none which are not of the light. I am Hatonn.

There are none which are not of the light. Let that rest with you. The person you cannot forgive, the part of yourself you cannot face, the dark corner of the world that makes you lose hope. The voices say it is all light, in some condition or another, in some state of remembering or forgetting. The difference between a saint and a stranger is not substance. It is only remembrance. And light, they say, has the power to comfort, to bind, to unbind, to heal, to do all things. Not because it fights the darkness, but because darkness was never a separate substance to begin with. There is only the light, and the many ways we forget it. Light is not the reward at the end of the path. Light is the path, and the ground, and the traveler. The next time you stand in the sun, remember that you are not being warmed by something foreign to you. You are being greeted by your own substance, recognized by itself. In our next episode, we walk into the other half of the picture, the one we are taught to fear. Darkness, and the womb of night. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Begin Again
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, beginning again. There is a moment we all know. You have fallen off the path, broken the promise to yourself, slipped back into the old habit, and the voice in your head says it is too late, you have ruined it, why bother. And then you stay down, not because you cannot get up, but because getting up feels like admitting how far you fell. The voices in this archive have a completely different answer, and Hatonn gives it first, in the tenderest words I know in all these sessions.

Cry your tears, my children, when tears are to be shed. But in the morning turn again and begin again. And know yourself as the eternal beginner. As we said, we are always with you if you request our presence, as are other principles and intelligences which wish to aid you. Ask and you shall receive help. I am Hatonn.

The eternal beginner. Not the failure, not the backslider, not the one who should have known better by now. The beginner. It reframes the whole thing. Beginning again is not a concession. It is your identity. Every morning is a morning, and every morning you may turn again. Cry the tears if they need crying. And then, in the morning, begin again. And notice that you do not begin alone. Ask and you shall receive help. The archive is full of beings who are simply waiting to be asked.

Hatonn returns to this theme in another session, and this time it is about the errors we make, the old habits, the moments we catch ourselves doing the very thing we swore we would stop doing, sometimes within hours of the promise.

When you are dealing with habits of very long standing, the error is sometimes very difficult to catch before it has begun. Thus, above all, do not blame yourself, or feel less than confident, or less than spiritual, because you have made an error. Simply begin again, for in the Creator all things are new, and at any moment you may begin anew, and each time that you find yourself in negativity, simply begin anew. And that is the beginning of a new life, for the Creator is such that once two plus two is four, the Creator does not remember the error, and nor should you. I am Hatonn.

Once two plus two is four, the Creator does not remember the error, and nor should you. Read that again slowly. The universe is not keeping score. There is no ledger with your name on it, no tally of how many times you have tried and failed. In the Creator, all things are new, at any moment you may begin anew. Not tomorrow, not on the first of the month, not when you feel ready. At any moment. Each time you find yourself in negativity, simply begin anew. It is the simplest instruction in the archive, and somehow the hardest one to believe.

And then there is Q'uo, who names exactly why it is so hard.

To begin again, to begin again, to begin again, how the human spirit rebels. Yet within the present moment there is only beginning, and there is nothing but the present moment in any spiritual consideration. So look to the loving and acceptance of the higher power which you may call as you wish. Look to your relationship with that love that created you. Allow within yourself the birth in the manger of your heart of your own spiritual beingness, true, imperishable, consciousness. Guard it, just as the story speaks of this infant's mother and father fleeing to protect their child. Protect this child as lovingly, and with as much feeling of honor. I am Q'uo.

How the human spirit rebels. Yes. We want credit for how far we have come. We want our progress to be permanent, our wisdom to be banked, our streak unbroken. Beginning again feels like losing all of that, like being sent back to the start of the board game. But Q'uo says that within the present moment there is only beginning. There is nothing else. The past you are clinging to, the streak you are afraid of breaking, the identity of the person who has it all together, none of it is real right now. What is real is this moment, and this moment is always a beginning. And then that extraordinary image. Guard the new beginning the way the story guards the infant in the manger. Protect this child as lovingly, and with as much feeling of honor. Your fresh start is not a consolation prize. It is holy, and it deserves a guard of honor.

So tonight the archive gives you three things. A name, the eternal beginner. A permission, at any moment you may begin anew, no waiting ever required. And an image, the infant in the manger of your heart, guarded with honor. Whatever you fell away from this week, whatever habit caught you, whatever promise broke, it does not disqualify you. It qualifies you. The Creator does not remember the error, and neither should you. Cry the tears if they need crying. In the morning, begin again. In our next episode, we learn the art of the open hand. Letting go. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Letting Go
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, letting go. Everyone tells you to let go, as though it were easy, as though the hand were not clenched for a reason. The voices in this archive are honest about how hard it is. They do not tell you to drop everything at once. They tell you where to put it down, and into whose care. Hatonn begins with an image I think about often.

There is a higher law, my friends, the law of love. Not the human love, that will fail. But the love which you will find at the center of your created being. My friends, you cannot try to love. Only let go of your feelings, and release them completely into the care of the love that created you. It is not expected that, at the human level, you will be able to love as the Creator desires. It is only as those who open to the center of their being that the love within flows through in the physical being, and out into the physical illusion. You may release this from within you just as a person may, on a very dark night, raise all the window shades in his house, so that the light within may pour out onto the world around him. The light within you, my friends, shines brightly. Whether you know it or not, whether you feel it or not, you have such power within you, my friends. I am Hatonn.

You cannot try to love. Only let go of your feelings, and release them completely into the care of the love that created you. Letting go is not giving up. It is a transfer. You are not throwing your feelings away. You are placing them into larger hands. And notice what happens when you do. The light that was trapped behind the shades pours out onto the world around you. The letting go is not the end of the story. It is how the light gets out.

But what exactly are we holding? Aaron, one of the most psychologically precise voices in the archive, names the thing we grip most tightly.

This does not mean no energy, no effort. But where is effort given, to fix, or to surrender and offer love? To let go of the need to control, to see the fear that it springs from and let go, is one of the hardest of human experiences. Yet it is only from that place of deep faith that undistorted wisdom and compassion can develop, wisdom that penetrates into the depths of reality rather than thinking about reality, compassion that grows out of connection to all that is rather than the concept of compassion which puts a bandage over your own pain. I am Aaron.

To let go of the need to control, to see the fear that it springs from, and let go. One of the hardest of human experiences. Aaron does not pretend otherwise. And look at the order of operations. First you let go of the need to control. Then you see the fear underneath it, the fear that was driving the whole performance, and you let go of that too. It is a double release. The grip, and then the reason for the grip. And only from that place, Aaron says, can real wisdom develop. Wisdom that penetrates into the depths of reality rather than merely thinking about reality. You cannot think your way to an open hand. You have to unclench it.

Aaron has one more image for tonight, and it is the one I want you to carry with you.

Because you are human you constantly fall short of the ideal, and yet you constantly ask yourself to let go of that edge onto which you were holding and strike out again to cross the sea of truth. It is a very courageous act, and yet you rarely give yourself notice of the courage. You perceive the fear that asks you to hold back and you miss the beautiful bravery and love exhibited each time you take a new step. Does a child learn to walk with a parent who says, do not take another step, you will fall, or with a parent who applauds each new step and picks that child up and takes away the hurt from the inevitable fall? How can you learn to pick yourselves up in this way? Can you learn to cherish that self who so bravely tries again and again? I am Aaron.

Can you learn to cherish that self who so bravely tries again and again. Letting go of the edge, Aaron says, is a courageous act, and you rarely give yourself credit for the courage. You only notice the fear. But every time you release the edge and take a step, there is beautiful bravery in it, and love. Be the parent who applauds the step, not the one who warns against it. Pick yourself up. Take away the hurt. Applaud the next step too.

Three movements tonight. Release your feelings into the care of the love that created you. Let go of the need to control, and then let go of the fear beneath it. And cherish the self who keeps letting go of the edge and stepping forward. The hand opens slowly. That is fine. An open hand is not a defeated hand. It is the only hand the light can pass through. In our next episode, we go one step further than letting go, into the word that frightens people most. Surrender. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Surrender
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, surrender. It is the word people flinch at. It sounds like defeat, like waving a white flag. The voices in this archive use it to mean almost the opposite. Surrender, to them, is not losing. It is the moment you stop fighting the wrong battle. Hatonn says it more boldly than anyone.

I am Hatonn. To all of you who journey upon the path and who hear a song, know that you have comrades, that that which is needed will be provided. You can only refine your ears that they may listen better to the song of faith, hope, love and peace. Each person wishes for personal power, power to control, the power to shape the destiny. Yet know that the first and greatest power is given to you in the act of surrender, for the heart that has surrendered can hear the song which will lead you. Those who close and stop their ears and demand that things be thus and so will indeed hear a siren's song. Surrender, then, and purify your ears to the song of life, that life which is beyond life and death. I am Hatonn.

The first and greatest power is given to you in the act of surrender. Sit with how strange that is. We spend our lives accumulating power, the power to control, the power to shape destiny, and Hatonn says the greatest power of all arrives the moment we stop clutching. Why? Because the heart that has surrendered can hear the song which will lead you. Control makes you deaf. The controller hears only the siren song of their own demands. Surrender purifies the ears. It is not passivity. It is finally being able to hear the music you were drowning out with your own noise.

Latwii approaches the same truth from a different angle, through the question of control between people.

I am Latwii, and I am aware of your query, my brother. The process of which you speak is one in which the lesson is fed back time and again for those engaged in the confrontation for control. This process continues until either the control is gained by one over the other, or until one or both learn to surrender. For control, my friends, is that concept which expresses the negative aspect of your illusion, that is, the separation of one from another. Surrender, on the other hand, expresses the positive aspect, that is, the surrendering of the self to the will of the Creator. In such a situation, if one can realize, firstly, that it is an illusion in which you participate, and then seek within that illusion the lesson that is being made available, then one might see the opportunity to surrender the will of the self to the will of the Creator. Ask within your being, if you can gather the presence of mind to do so in such a situation, Creator, what is Thy will? If your seeking be pure, your inner self shall lead you in that path which reflects the lesson you have come to learn. I am Latwii.

Control is the separation of one from another. Surrender is the return. Latwii does not describe surrender as collapsing or submitting to another person. It is the surrendering of the self to the will of the Creator, which is to say, to the larger pattern, the deeper current. And there is a practice hidden in it. In the heat of the confrontation, ask within your being, Creator, what is Thy will. What is the will of the whole? Your inner self, Latwii says, will lead you in the path that reflects the lesson you came to learn.

Our third passage tonight is from a voice called Leema, on the surrender inside prayer itself.

Let us begin at the beginning of service to others. The beginning is meditation. Many have called this meditation prayer. The overwhelming concept that we wish to instill in you when we speak of meditation and the reason that we use the alternate word, prayer, is that there is a surrender in what this instrument knows as Christian prayer, a surrender that says, Thy will, not mine, be done. Within you, there is a self that is like a clay vessel that deals with mundane things, and that shall not last. Within that clay vessel there is a great treasure. That is your other self, that is, your consciousness. The surrender in meditation and prayer is the opening of the door to a great dining room, a dining room in which there is a food and a drink that your clay vessel will never know nor need, but without which your consciousness gradually becomes embittered, bowed down, and weary beyond words. I am Leema.

Thy will, not mine, be done. Four words, and the whole teaching is inside them. The clay vessel, the part of you that deals with mundane things, that pays the bills and answers the messages, is not the whole of you. Inside it is the treasure, your consciousness, and it is starving. Surrender is the door to the dining room where it can finally eat. Without that food, Leema says, consciousness becomes embittered, bowed down, and weary beyond words. Then you know what surrender is for. It is not defeat. It is dinner.

Three faces of surrender tonight. The greatest power, given in the act of release. The end of the confrontation for control, replaced by one quiet question. And the door to the dining room where your deeper self is fed. Surrender does not ask you to stop wanting. It asks you to stop insisting that your way is the only way. Purify your ears, and listen for the song of life. In our next episode, we meet the youngest part of ourselves. The child within. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Guilt
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, guilt. The heaviest thing most of us carry. Not the sharp guilt of a single mistake, but the low background hum of it, the feeling that we are somehow wrong, that we owe the universe an apology for existing imperfectly. The voices in this archive treat guilt as a misunderstanding. Hatonn gives us the central image of the evening, a practice for meditation.

Now we return to meditation. As you begin to go into the silence, perhaps you have games you play, as we would call them, in which you attempt to carry your clothed spirit, your limited spirit into the silence. Do not do this, my friends. Picture yourself, mentally, taking guilt and discarding it as you would a piece of clothing. Taking resentment, fear, putting it aside and walking as your shining naked self into the waters of cleanliness. After you have bathed yourself in total forgiveness, total cleanliness for the moment, you can emerge and in your mind you can sit down and listen. Listen for those signals which will come to you in the silence. You are a whole and complete person. Within you is perfection, wisdom and all the attributes of love. I am Hatonn.

Taking guilt and discarding it as you would a piece of clothing. It is such a physical image. Guilt is not you. It is something you put on. A coat. And like a coat, you can take it off. You do not have to earn the right to remove it. You do not have to argue with it first. In meditation, picture yourself setting it down, setting down the resentment and the fear too, and walking as your shining naked self into the waters of cleanliness. Underneath all the layers, Hatonn says, you are a whole and complete person. Within you is perfection, wisdom, and all the attributes of love. The guilt was never the truth about you. It was only clothing. And clothing can be removed.

In another session, Hatonn says the same thing even more plainly, about the small daily errors we turn into moral catastrophes.

It is a very common and everyday affair for those who seek, to slip, by habit, into old patterns of thought which are negative. This is understood and should not be a source for self-blame or any sort of guilt upon the part of the seeker. You are simply adding two plus two and receiving the answer of five. There is no guilt, there is a simple error involved. I am Hatonn.

There is no guilt, there is a simple error involved. You added two plus two and got five. That is all. It is not a verdict on your character. It is not proof that you are a disappointment. It is arithmetic gone wrong, a habit of mind, and habits can be retrained. The archive is tender on this point because we are so harsh on it. We take a simple error and we build a cathedral of guilt on top of it. Hatonn keeps pulling the cathedral down. Simple error. Begin again.

And then there is Latwii, who goes deeper, into the guilt that disguises itself as virtue. The guilt that makes us sacrifice ourselves to prove we are good.

I am Latwii, and we thank you for the further clarification. When one feels the concepts of guilt and the concept of sacrifice that may be perceived as an effect or result of the guilt, there are the opportunities to transform the self, for when one has observed the situation within which guilt and sacrifice are felt and has penetrated more to the heart of the situation and has discovered that there is a purpose for these concepts within one's learning, one may then set about to discover that purpose. As this process of discovery continues, and the layers of the illusion and the situation are peeled one after the other, one may discover that what seemed to be a sacrifice to another out of guilt may become a gift of love to a beloved portion of one's own being. This portion may have cried out in many ways that seemed harmful and hurtful to the self. Yet each cry was for love that would enable each to find that love not only within the illusion of the situation but within the heart of each entity's response to the other, for when there is a great seeming lack of love, there is being built a great potential for the fulfillment of love. The vacuum draws into it that which is sought. I am Latwii.

What seemed to be a sacrifice to another out of guilt may become a gift of love to a beloved portion of one's own being. Follow the movement. You start with guilt, and guilt demands sacrifice, you must pay, you must suffer, to balance the books. But if you look deeper, past the layers, you find something astonishing. The part of you that you have been punishing was never asking for punishment. It was crying out for love. Every cry that seemed harmful was a cry for love. And the sacrifice you were making out of guilt can be transformed, Latwii says, into a gift of love to that beloved portion of yourself. The books were never real. There is nothing to pay. There is only a part of you waiting to be loved.

Three releasings tonight. Take off the guilt like a piece of clothing, and walk shining into the waters of cleanliness. When you err, call it a simple error, and refuse the cathedral of guilt. And when guilt demands sacrifice, look beneath it, and give love to the part of you that was crying out for it all along. Guilt was never required of you. Only love was. In our next episode, we turn our faces toward wonder. Awe. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Inner Child
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the child within. Somewhere inside the competent adult you have become, there is a small one. The one who has not yet learned to be embarrassed, or efficient, or careful. The voices in this archive speak of this child with extraordinary tenderness, and they are insistent about one thing. This child is not a metaphor for immaturity. This child is the most alive part of you. Q'uo offers a visualization, and I would suggest listening to it slowly.

A great resource for doing work in consciousness is creative visualization. The closer the visualization comes to resonating with the timbre of memory, the better the chance that it will aid the entity at deep levels of emotion, those levels of emotion which contain true wisdom. Such a visualization about the loving self might be such as this. Within you lies the small child which is attempting to do well, and which perceives the self constantly through the awkwardness of childhood as failing to be adequate to its own requests of the self. Picture, then, the loving self, and you are indeed all very loving entities, as the nurturing parent. Would the parent within you turn to a child and scold it when it has acted in self-perceived error, or would the loving parent take the child into the cradle of its arms and place the child's head where it can again hear the heartbeat of the womb? I am Q'uo.

Place the child's head where it can again hear the heartbeat of the womb. That is the whole practice. Notice what Q'uo does not suggest. The parent does not lecture the child. The parent does not explain where the child went wrong. The parent takes the child into the cradle of its arms and holds it against the oldest sound it knows. The heartbeat. Before language, before judgment, before the awkwardness of childhood, there was a rhythm, and it said you are safe. The small child within you is still attempting to do well. Still perceiving itself as failing. What it needs is not correction. It needs to be held against the heartbeat again.

And the child is not only to be comforted. The child is to be played with. Laitos, one of the gentlest voices in the archive, says it plainly.

Another tool one may use to become more and more one with one's mate and to avoid the adversary relationship is to allow the child within to have its freedom, to offer it swims and picnics and joyful companionship of all kinds. Never, ever, let the joys of childhood depart from you but rather find the child within your mate and let both children out to play. It keeps you as an integrated being, healthy and cheerful. This is very helpful. I am Laitos.

Swims and picnics and joyful companionship of all kinds. It is almost comical how practical this is. Not a meditation technique. Not a journaling exercise. A picnic. The child within does not only want to be healed. The child wants to play, to splash, to be delighted for no productive reason at all. And Laitos makes a beautiful suggestion, to find the child within the person you love, and let both children out to play. So much of adult relating is two armored adults negotiating. What if, sometimes, it were two children, out in the sun, with a picnic? Never, ever, let the joys of childhood depart from you. It is not nostalgia. It is maintenance. The integrated being, healthy and cheerful, is the one whose child still gets to come out.

Our third passage tonight is from Q'uo again, and it explains why tenderness toward the inner child is not indulgence. It is nourishment.

When those portions of the self, or activities of the self, seem to go awry, it is more nourishing to the small entity that always resides within, much as the child in each entity, to reinforce the concept of wholeness and acceptability, for the divisions and definitions of acceptable or unacceptable behaviors are man-made, and it is always a whole and acceptable entity that places any foot upon the path, whether that foot is solidly placed or not. I am Q'uo.

It is always a whole and acceptable entity that places any foot upon the path, whether that foot is solidly placed or not. When you stumble, when some portion of you goes awry, the nourishing move is not to divide yourself into acceptable and unacceptable parts. Those divisions are man-made, Q'uo says. Reinforce wholeness instead. Tell the small entity within that it is acceptable, whole, exactly as it is, even with the foot half off the path. Especially then.

Three gifts for the child tonight. Hold it against the heartbeat. Take it out to play. And when it stumbles, tell it that it is whole. The child within you is not a problem to be solved or a phase to be outgrown. It is the part of you that still knows how to be delighted, how to be held, how to begin. Guard it the way you would guard anything precious. In our next episode, we turn toward the part of ourselves we would rather not look at, and we look at it with love. The shadow. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Shadow
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the shadow. The parts of ourselves we do not show anyone. The jealousy, the pettiness, the anger we are ashamed of, the thoughts we would never say aloud. Most teachings either condemn the shadow or pretend it is not there. The voices in this archive do something rarer. They ask us to accept it, to love it, even to thank it. Latwii begins with the darkest image imaginable, and transforms it completely.

I am Latwii. My brother, we are aware of your question and may we say to you that many things have been misunderstood. The one known as Satan is merely the shadow of evil thoughts. Given fear enough, evil thoughts can do harm, can cause fear and pain and anguish. This power is given only through the fear of the one who is feeling the difficulty. There is no reality to the fear and thus it is said love casteth out fear. The one principle called Satan is a lonely and sad thought form and we would say to you, accept this principle as part of yourself, as that within you, if you will, which spurs you on to growth, to new understandings, and to desire for truth. Love this entity therefore, and take all strength from this mere shadow. I am Latwii.

Love this entity therefore, and take all strength from this mere shadow. Even the darkest thing you can name, Latwii says, is a lonely and sad thought form. It has power only through your fear of it. And here is the turn that changes everything. That dark principle is not your enemy. It is that within you which spurs you on to growth, to new understandings, and to desire for truth. The shadow is not the opposite of your spiritual life. It is the engine of it. The parts of you that frighten you are the parts that are pushing you to grow. So do not exile them. Accept them. Love them. And take all strength from them.

There is a voice in the archive called Monka, who says all of this in four words that I have never forgotten.

How little you know of yourself, my friends, if you do not know that all things are you. When you study, what do you study? Whatever it is, you are studying yourself. Stare deeply into yourself. Leap at that mirror. What do you feel? What do you deny? You are looking in a mirror. You are looking at your shadow. Drink it. I am Monka.

You are looking at your shadow. Drink it. Not fight it. Not fix it. Not analyze it for years from a safe distance. Drink it. Take it in. Let it become part of you consciously, instead of ruling you from the dark where you cannot see it. Monka asks the simplest diagnostic question in the archive. What do you deny? Whatever the answer is, that is the shadow. And the instruction is not to destroy it. It is to ingest it, to make it known, to stop pretending it is not yours. The shadow you refuse to drink does not disappear. It waits. The shadow you drink becomes wisdom.

And Hatonn closes our evening with the gentlest reframing of all. The shadow is not even real.

For each soul, my sister, there is a great solitude. Sometimes, my sister, in this loneliness, we have bad dreams. We are not speaking of literal dreams, we are speaking of times when a shadow seems to be over our lives. We are not free of these upon the plane from which I speak. Yes, we have advanced, yet we do not know all. These moments grow fewer and fewer as you continue to seek. It is a matter of being in reality instead of the illusion. When the shadow falls across you, my sister, know it for an illusion. If you must speak aloud to remind yourself, you may say, all is love. And you will feel reality flow within you at that moment. I am Hatonn.

When the shadow falls across you, know it for an illusion. If you must speak aloud to remind yourself, you may say, all is love. Notice who is speaking. Hatonn, from a plane far beyond ours, says we are not free of these shadows where they are either. The shadow is not a sign that you are failing. It is part of the terrain, at every level. And the response is not a battle. It is a sentence, spoken aloud if you need to. All is love. Say it until you feel reality flow within you at that moment.

Three teachings on the shadow tonight. It is lonely and sad, not evil, and it spurs you to growth, so love it and take strength from it. Whatever you deny is the shadow, so drink it, make it yours, stop pretending. And when it falls across you, know it for an illusion, and say the sentence that dissolves it. All is love. The shadow was never your enemy. It was your teacher, wearing a frightening mask, and it has been waiting patiently for you to recognize it. In our next episode, we take up the heaviest thing most of us carry, and we set it down. Guilt. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Courage
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about courage. Not the loud kind, not the kind in stories about battlefields and rescues, but the quiet kind. The kind that walks out the front door of a small life and does something it has never done before. The voices in this archive speak of courage as something we brought with us, not something we earn. Listen to how Hatonn tells a story about it, because he says truths like this one cannot always be spoken straight. They must be approached through what you would call the parable.

This evening we would like to tell you a story. Once there were two sisters. These two sisters were without husbands, for they had both lost them as years went by. Being alone in the world, they sought each other, loved each other, and lived together, taking care of each other and supporting each other in times of distress. As they reached the age of seventy, both of them began to feel the failing senses of old age come upon them. One sister reacted by becoming somewhat bitter. She began to feel that she was, indeed, in a tragic situation, and lived a life whose days and nights went slowly and sometimes fearfully. The other sister reacted in quite a different manner. She began to think of the shortness of her remaining years. She determined to walk beyond her doorstep and see what she could see of the world and do what she could do for the world. And so this lady began to take a walk, just a short one around the block, and she opened her ears, and she opened her eyes, and within a very few months she had had conversations with many people. Taking her courage in her hands, as though it were a precious gift, she did that which she had never done before, for she had been a timid woman, and where she was guided, she went. She sat by hospital beds where people were dying and talked to them. She came to prisons once a week and had friends that she made in that unlikely place. And on she walked, and soon the neighborhood began to know of her, and people came to her. I am Hatonn.

Taking her courage in her hands, as though it were a precious gift. I love that image, because it suggests that courage is not a quality of the personality. It is a thing you can pick up, like a lamp. The timid woman does not become a different woman. She simply takes up the courage and walks. And notice the scale of the thing. She does not save the world. She takes a short walk around the block. The voices are always pointing at this. Courage is not measured by the size of the deed. It is measured by the wideness of the door you were willing to open. In another session, Hatonn speaks to a group of seekers who were trying to bring light to a planet that seemed to be growing darker, and they were tired. Here is what he tells them, and it may be the most honest sentence about courage in the entire archive.

Therefore we say to you, be of good courage and do not think of goals but only of the mile which you are walking at this time. We do not know how long the wilderness lasts in terms of time. If it lasts past your lifetime, then you will have been a shepherd along the way. You will not be in at the finish, you will not see the end written across the skies. The movie will not be over for you when you leave this incarnation. This is of no concern to you. Do not be concerned with your accomplishments. Be concerned only with the amount of time that you spend dealing with individuals upon the sturdy and heartfelt basis of the love of the Creator. I am Hatonn.

Do not think of goals but only of the mile which you are walking at this time. That is the whole instruction, really, packed into a single mile. We are so often trying to be somewhere else, at the finish, at the ending written across the skies. Courage, as the voices describe it, is the refusal to abandon the mile you are on. To be a shepherd along the way even when no one will ever know your name. And there is one more thing Hatonn says about this, and it reframes everything. The courage did not begin here. It began before you were born.

As you breathe in and as you breathe out, my friends, you use up this mortal life that you have taken on with courage and dedication at the outset, to make use of as a time of learning under adverse circumstances, under the circumstance of forgetting what you knew as a spirit. Try to remember, my friends, what you already know. That all men are brothers. That love and consciousness dwell in everything. That all that is around you is alive and part of the creation which is love. I am Hatonn.

You took on this life with courage and dedication at the outset. Before the forgetting. Before the fog came down and hid everything you knew as a spirit. Which means that whatever you are facing right now, the illness, the fear, the ordinary grinding difficulty of a Tuesday, you were brave enough once to sign up for all of it. Not because you were careless, but because you wanted to learn. So tonight, if you are afraid, the voices do not ask you to stop being afraid. They ask you to remember that the timid woman picked up the courage like a gift, and to walk only the mile you are walking. In our next episode, we stay with the walking. The quiet art of perseverance. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Perseverance
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about perseverance. Not the glamorous kind, the kind that wins medals and gets written up. The dull, unglamorous kind. Trying again on the morning when nothing seems to have changed. The voices in this archive are surprisingly gentle about this. They do not measure you by how far you have come. They measure you by the honesty of the trying. Listen to Latwii, speaking to a seeker who felt the difficulty of living up to her own ideals.

To any seeker who feels the difficulty in manifesting those ideals which each seeker holds dear, it is the intention of your being which is of greatest importance. Each seeker will find the moments of falling short of the ideal, for it is not within the capability of any seeker to match that which is infinite in a finite illusion. It is instead the honor and the duty of each conscious seeker of truth to make whatever effort is possible, to make it with a whole heart, and to accept that which comes from the effort in joy and in thanksgiving for the opportunity which has been met. As you find those times of difficulty, retire to those places within your being that are silent, gentle, healing and loving. Find that place of joy at the very opportunity to be where you are and to do what you do. For indeed, each situation is full of such love and such joy. What we have taken so long to say is that there is great virtue in perseverance, great virtue in the attempt. I am Latwii.

There is great virtue in perseverance, great virtue in the attempt. Not in the result. Not in the matching of the life to the ideal, which Latwii says is not within the capability of any seeker anyway. How could it be? The ideal is infinite, and we are finite. So the whole game changes. You are not failing when you fall short. You are doing the thing that is actually asked of you, which is to make the effort with a whole heart, and then to accept what comes from the effort with joy. With thanksgiving, even, for the opportunity. That is a very different economy than the one we are used to, where the attempt counts for nothing and only the outcome is priced. Hatonn takes this even further, and he does it with an image I keep coming back to. He says that this life, the whole incarnation, is an athletic training. And the pain is part of the method.

You have forgotten the joy that you felt at being able to work with those with whom you have chosen to work. It is the same discomfort and pain that you feel when you put your muscles to a new task, a task that has never before been completed or even tried. The pain is good, and when you achieve that which you could not beforehand do, how pleased you are at the progress you have consciously decided to make. This is the nature of your incarnation. You are in your own way an athlete, each of you. The most helpful training is meditation, but the painful exercises are usually those involving those about you, because that is when you finish practicing and you begin the race. When you are dry, and you are confused, and you are uncomfortable and in pain, go back and exercise in meditation by opening the door that leads outside of time, out of all particulars, into the great source of love. We wish each athlete a good season, and a personal best that you may ever strive to improve. We are those of Hatonn.

The painful exercises are usually those involving those about you, because that is when you finish practicing and you begin the race. I want to sit with that for a moment. Meditation is the training. The people are the race. The colleague who tests every nerve, the family member who knows exactly where the soft spot is, the stranger whose suffering asks something of you at the worst possible hour, these are not interruptions to the spiritual life. They are the spiritual life, at game speed. And when you are dry and confused and in pain, you do not quit the team. You go back to the door that leads outside of time, and you recover, and you return. That is perseverance. Not winning. Returning. And here is the shortest passage of the night, from Hatonn again, and I think it is the tenderness under everything else we have heard.

My friends, I am very pleased that you are attempting to persevere in this attempt to serve. We assure you, I and my brothers, that we are always with you, and are here to serve you, whether through an instrument such as this one, or through meditation by direct contact. I am Hatonn.

I am very pleased that you are attempting to persevere. Not that you have succeeded. That you are attempting. So tonight, if you are tired, if the ideal feels very far away and the gap between who you want to be and who you were today feels very wide, the archive has one instruction for you. Keep attempting. Make the effort with a whole heart. Accept what comes with thanksgiving. And when the pain of it finds you, treat it like the soreness after good training, because it means the muscles are working. You are an athlete, and the season is long, and you are not running it alone. In our next episode, we turn from the effort to the object of the effort. The quiet fire of devotion. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Work As Worship
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about work as worship. This one is for everyone who has ever wondered whether their ordinary working life counts, spiritually speaking. The commute, the shift, the inbox, the kitchen, the workshop, the classroom, the night feedings, the spreadsheets. The voices in this archive have a clear answer, and I think it is a deeply kind one. It counts. All of it counts. And no one kind of work counts more than any other. Q'uo puts it plainly, in a passage about the many callings of a human life.

Some of you have been called to a solitary and worshipful existence. However, it is well that each consider what he or she may feel encouraged within to attempt or accomplish, for not all who are spiritually oriented would wish to manifest as such. Many are called to be parents, homemakers, mechanics, factory workers, and all the other careers, professions, and jobs, all the ways to sustain life with your money and to enrich life with love. There is no circumstance which is better or best for the furthering of service to others at this time. You must listen, each to his own subjective consciousness, with discrimination and with care, but also, in the end, with trust and faith. I am Q'uo.

There is no circumstance which is better or best for the furthering of service to others. No hierarchy of holy work. The monastery is not holier than the factory floor. The parent awake at three in the morning with a crying child is not doing less than the monk in meditation. The mechanic is not doing less than the minister. The voices are relentless on this point, because they know how deeply we rank ourselves, and each other, by what we do for a living. They are asking us to lay the ranking down entirely. But then the question becomes, if all work can be service, what is it that makes it worship? Q'uo's answer is disarmingly simple. It is not the job. It is the daily turning of attention.

In order to aid you in these choices, and in your point of view, we ask two things of you. Firstly, we ask that you find a path that includes love of the infinite One shown as worship, adoration, or simple attention, on a daily basis. We do not ask for any particular path to be followed. We are not those who ask for one religion or another. You choose the path that works for you and brings you into awareness of your true self and your true relationship with the infinite One. Daily time spent in silence, listening for the voice that is silent but speaks so loudly, is recommended as an aid to this process of choice. I am Q'uo.

Worship, adoration, or simple attention. Notice how the list descends, gently, from the grand to the almost invisible. Simple attention. That is all it takes, some days. A pause before the work begins. A moment of silence with the morning coffee. Listening for the voice that is silent but speaks so loudly. The voices are not asking for hours of devotion. They are asking for dailiness, for the small faithful turning, the way a plant turns toward light without making a ceremony of it. And then, once that turning is there, something changes in the work itself. It stops being only about output, only about getting through the day. It becomes, in Q'uo's phrase, a lively work on behalf of the one infinite Creator. Listen to what that liveliness runs on.

As one is able to experience the self more and more intelligently, consciously, and fully, one is able to feel self-forgiven, worthy, hopeful, cheerful, peaceful, and oriented toward a lively work on behalf of the one infinite Creator. Humankind is fueled, not by oil or coal so much as by inspiration, passion, sharing, and caring. Thus, the more fully one is able to tap into the deep and plangent notes of purified emotion, the greater is one's ability to manifest the light of the infinite One to a darkened world, which rejoices in seeing beacons of light, whether or not they know why the light is there, how the light has come to be there, and what is its function. I am Q'uo.

Humankind is fueled, not by oil or coal so much as by inspiration, passion, sharing, and caring. I want to leave you with that image, because it quietly redefines what work is for. Not the extraction of value. Not the proving of worth. But the carrying of light, often without anyone knowing why it is there, or how it came to be there. The beacon does not explain itself. It simply shines, and the darkened world rejoices, whether or not it understands. Tomorrow, at your desk or your bench or your kitchen counter, you might remember this. You do not need a different life for your work to be worship. You need only the turning of attention, daily, and the willingness to let the ordinary hours be what they already are. Sacred, exactly as they are. That is the whole of the teaching. In our next episode, we look up from the workbench entirely, and out, past the roof and past the weather. The night sky. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Devotion
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about devotion. A word that can sound old fashioned, like something in a chapel with dust on the windows. But in the archive, devotion is not about churches or rituals or giving up your personality. It is about the direction you are facing. It is the quiet decision that the love is real, made again and again, in the kitchen, at the desk, in the car. No one applauds it. Most of the time no one even notices it. But the voices say it is the substance of what carries you through. Listen to Hatonn, speaking about what he calls the substance of what is real, and where a seeker ought to look for it.

We ask you constantly to make meditation a part of every day that you have to spend upon your planet. For you shall discover that those realities within yourself which you find in meditation are the substance and the strength that shall see you through. We say to you, seek within for the real substance of your being. Seek within for what is real. Look into your hearts, my friends. Find the love of the Creator which is there. Shine that love as you look about you in your world, in your everyday activities. Remember that love when you speak to strangers. Remember that love when you see discord. Remember that love when you are in doubt, when you are unsure and when you need strength, for you shall need strength in the days ahead. We say these words to you, hoping that you will find the devotion within yourself to make this journey, this spiritual journey, and make it your everyday life. For soon, it shall be so. I am Hatonn.

Make this journey your everyday life. That is the whole of devotion, as Hatonn frames it. Not a special state you visit on holy days, but the direction of an ordinary Tuesday. Shine that love in your everyday activities. Remember that love when you speak to strangers. The phrase I keep hearing is the quiet one in the middle. Remember that love when you are in doubt. Devotion is not certainty. It is the practice of returning to the love when you are not certain of anything else. And then Hatonn does something practical, because the archive never leaves devotion as an abstraction. A mother asks how to show her young children the light and love. Here is his answer.

There is no greater teacher for the young one of your peoples than the example which they see and which they experience themselves within their daily lives. To find a means to daily express in some way your love of the Creator and your desire to serve the Creator will express to your children that which you value most. If there might be some way in which you could, shall we say, regularize or ritualize this experience and expressing of devotion and love to the one Creator with your children partaking, this would be a most effective means of allowing them not only to see but to experience with you this love and desire. I am Hatonn.

Regularize or ritualize this experience of devotion, with your children partaking. Not so that they learn a doctrine, but so that they get to experience it with you. Devotion, in this telling, is contagious before it is instructional. The children do not need the theology. They need to watch a parent pause, daily, in love, and to feel the room change. That is the teaching. And now I want to offer one more passage, because it turns the whole night inside out. We have been talking about our devotion, our effort, our facing. But Latwii, speaking once to a group about a lonely seeker, lets slip that the devotion runs both ways.

We would wish to address to the one known as S our love and constant devotion to her, as she is physically very alone in her seeking at this time. We are aware that she has again become comforted by our presence, and it makes us very happy that we have been able to reestablish contact with her. We cannot say the words that she wishes at this time. However, we are aware that she will understand that this has to do with her own free will. Again, to sister S we send our love. I am Latwii.

Our love and constant devotion to her. The voices of the archive, beings who describe themselves as pilgrims a step or two ahead, claim devotion toward us. Not pity. Not supervision. Devotion. Notice too how careful they are. They cannot say everything. They cannot override her free will. The devotion does not control. It attends. It watches over. It rejoices when the lonely seeker finds comfort, the way you would rejoice if someone you loved finally slept through the night. So tonight, if you have been carrying the whole weight of this, if you have been the only one facing the love, the only one making the effort, the only one remembering in the doubt, know that the archive describes a love that is facing you back. A constant devotion, addressed to a lonely seeker by name, and by extension, addressed to you. The practice of devotion, then, is simpler than it looks. Face the love. Ritualize it if you can. Let the children see it. And trust that while you are facing it, it is facing you. You do not have to generate all of this alone. You never did. In our next episode, we bend the knee. Reverence. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Reverence
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about reverence. It is a word we mostly keep for cathedrals and memorials, for the places where the air goes still. But the voices in the archive use it for something much closer. They use it for the body you woke up in. They use it for the steering wheel you are holding in traffic. Listen to Q’uo, asked about the body, answering with a question of their own.

What would be one’s attitude upon approaching a structure of obvious architectural wonder and skill? What would be one’s attitude when beholding a building built of such beauty, and designed for purpose of worship and communion, and feeling the presence of the one Creator? Would one be excessively dirty, shall we say, or bring the can of spray paint to its walls? Or would reverence, not necessarily the administrative codes of the building, but reverence inform the self as to the relationship of the self to this structure? Would the appreciation in the heart not inform the self of how to relate to and to conduct oneself while in this building? For each iota of the creation, however humble, however small, however inert, or however seemingly of the material realm, which comes into contact with that which is sacred, is itself made sacred. It would be more correct to say that the sacred is revealed as being already contained within that seeming object of matter. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Would reverence inform the self as to the relationship of the self to this structure? That is the question of the whole night. Not, do you believe the right things, but how do you stand in relation to the holy? And the holy, here, is not a building far away. It is the body. The humble, material, constantly changing body, the one we so often treat as a machine to be optimized or a problem to be hidden. Q’uo says each iota of the creation, however small, however inert, that comes into contact with the sacred is itself made sacred. Or more correctly, the sacred is revealed as already contained within it. Reverence is not something you manufacture. It is what happens when you finally notice what was already there. And this brings us to one of the most misunderstood gestures in all of spiritual life. Kneeling.

It is good to bend the knees before the Lord, as this instrument has said from time to time. Yet, that posture of humility is not the posture of one who feels unworthy. Rather, it is the posture of one who barely can fathom the infinite mystery of the one Creator. When this instrument thinks of that posture, she has a tendency to think of the moment when the man in love bends his knees before the beloved and asks the privilege of becoming her partner in life. There is a reverence, even an awe, of the depth of the circumstance that fuels that bending of the knee before the beloved. And that is the same kind of energy that humility before the infinite One may bring to the seeker.
