Not that the seeker is less, but that the joy and the wonder of being able to share the life with the beloved is an incredible privilege. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Not that the seeker is less, but that the joy and the wonder of sharing the life with the beloved is an incredible privilege. Kneeling is not groveling. It is the body saying what the mouth cannot. That before this mystery, I am not diminished, I am astonished. The man in love does not kneel because he is worthless. He kneels because the moment is too large to stand up in. And the voices want that same energy for the morning commute. Q’uo was asked, what is faith, and how does one begin it? Here is the answer, and it is so ordinary it almost slips past.

We might suggest that it is by far the quicker entry into a faithful life to begin accepting what is precisely at that moment. If you at that moment when you decide to commit the self to faithful living are in the midst of traffic, then your first act of faith is to experience the beauty of all that is seen in the hustling, bustling street. By faith you suddenly experience sitting more lightly in your car, touching with love and reverence the steering wheel, the gears. It simply needs to be deeply accepted by the self. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Touching with love and reverence the steering wheel, the gears. Your first act of faith does not require a mountaintop. It requires the thing under your hands right now. The ordinary object, the unglamorous moment, touched as if it mattered, because it does. So tonight the archive leaves us with a posture and a practice. The posture is kneeling, inwardly, before a mystery too large to stand up in, without making yourself small. The practice is reverence for the thing under your hands, the body, the car, the room, because the sacred is already contained in it. You do not bring the holiness to the moment. You uncover it. In our next episode, we stay with the ordinary. The holiness of dishes and errands. The sacred ordinary. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Sacred Ordinary
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the sacred ordinary. The dishes. The errands. The small tasks that fill most of a life and almost never make it into the story of the life. The grocery list. The inbox. The commute with the same turns you have taken a thousand times. We tend to treat these hours as filler, as the waiting room between the meaningful moments. The voices in this archive are unanimous about one thing, and it might surprise you. Philosophy, they say, neglects the daily life. The spiritual seeker is tempted to spend the whole incarnation staring at deep and impenetrable mysteries, while the laundry piles up. Latwii has a different suggestion. Listen.

We would speak to you about something somewhat seemingly different than the usual topic of love and meditation. Philosophy often neglects that which may be called daily or ordinary life, expecting and hoping that the seeker will experience that more and more of the consciousness will be taken up with these deep and impenetrable matters. And yet each of you does live a daily life. That ordinary life is grist for your mill. It is the material from which you extract the answers to the most basic metaphysical questions. The fabric of this everyday life may seem banal, or at the very least, tame. And yet, if you have a listening ear and a watchful eye, that which is daily will also yield to you the most extravagant fruit in your seeking. I am Latwii.

That ordinary life is grist for your mill. Not an obstacle to the spiritual work. The material of it. The fabric of the everyday may seem banal, or at the very least tame, and yet, with a listening ear and a watchful eye, it yields the most extravagant fruit. Extravagant. That is a strong word for a Tuesday. But notice what it does not say. It does not say the ordinary will become interesting once you decorate it with spiritual thoughts. It says the ordinary will yield fruit if you bring the listening ear. The sacredness is not added. It is uncovered. That is the whole practice, and it costs nothing but attention. Hatonn draws the same line, and he makes it a choice you can make in any moment of the day.

Each activity within an entity’s life may take upon itself the tone of ordinary dailyness or the tone of communion. We suggest to you that when one has contemplated long upon the love the Creator has for oneself, then, perhaps, the second step to finding passion is a slow, gentle allowing of the self to awaken to that love. To listen to the bird that sings for your ear, and, yes, my children, it does sing for your ear, if you can but listen. For the breeze that blows so beautifully, for pearl gray days that soften and gentle the harsh edges of winter moods, for sunshine and joy. In all these experiences, you may remember that this has been a gift of love, and that you are completely satisfying your Creator, no matter how quickly or how slowly you advance, simply by being and reacting in a natural and spontaneous way to those things which occur. I am Hatonn.

Each activity may take upon itself the tone of ordinary dailyness or the tone of communion. The same sink of dishes. The same commute. The same inbox. Two tones available, and the difference is not in the activity, it is in the ear. The bird sings for your ear, if you can but listen. And Q’uo gives the most concrete version of all, a sentence I wish I had heard years ago. It is about the pot.

We ask that you remember what you are to do. It is directly in front of your eyes. It may be the scrubbing of a pot, it may be a great adventure, it may be professional work or waxing the car, but if it be done for the love of the Creator, then shall it be blessed, and nothing shall be unholy within your spirit, your heart and your mind. For as you do all that you do, you do it for the love of the Creator, and adversity then seems much further off, much more distant, and you are strengthened by your faith. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

It may be the scrubbing of a pot. If it be done for the love of the Creator, then shall it be blessed, and nothing shall be unholy. There is no hierarchy of tasks in the archive. The pot and the great adventure are weighed on the same scale, and the weight is the love you bring. So tonight, if your life feels small, if the days are mostly maintenance and the grand questions feel far away, the voices have good news. You have not missed the spiritual life. You are standing in it. Tomorrow, before you reach for the phone, notice the water on your hands at the sink. Listen for the bird. Bring the listening ear, bring the tone of communion, and scrub the pot as if it mattered, because in the economy of the Creator, it does. In our next episode, we begin at the beginning. Morning. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Breath
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the breath. It is the simplest thing in the world, and the voices in this archive treat it as one of the most sacred. Not because breathing is a technique, though it can be used as one, but because the breath is the most honest measure of closeness we have. What is closer to you than your own breathing? The voices answer that question, and their answer is startling. We begin with Laitos, in a passage of unusual tenderness, spoken slowly, as if every word mattered.

We speak one word, and that is love. The original Thought that created all that there is, is love. This simple and consuming fire is the fire of creation, is the fire of change, of transformation, and of infinity. There is no end to love. You may think of love in many ways. There are many words for love, in many languages. And many different words have been used by your peoples to attempt to express the plenitude of the original Thought, for love is all that there is. You cannot flee from love. You cannot be separated from love. For you are love. Love is closer to you than your body. Each breath is farther from your being than is love. This is what we come to share. I am Laitos.

Love is closer to you than your body. Each breath is farther from your being than is love. Sit with that for a moment, if you can. The thing you think of as the most intimate rhythm of your life, the breath moving in and out without your permission, is still farther from you than love is. Love is not out there somewhere, waiting to be found by the worthy. It is not even as far away as your next breath. It is closer than the body you live in. The voices keep returning to this image of nearness, as if they know how far away love usually feels to us, how much of our spiritual life is spent reaching. Hatonn says the same thing in a different way, and I love the plainness of his version, the way it names ordinary things.

My friends, we always speak to you of one simple thing, the love of the Creator. We are aware that, from your horizon, this love does not seem to be accessible in many ways in your daily life. And yet we say to you, my friends, that this love is closer to you than your breathing, more easily accessible than your own hands and feet, more familiar to you than your own thoughts. This love was the pattern from which each of you was stamped. Yes, my friends, each of you stamped in complete identity. And that same love that made you each the same has touched each with a unique part in that identity, so that the universe is an identity and a harmony at the same time. I am Hatonn.

Closer than your breathing. More easily accessible than your own hands and feet. More familiar than your own thoughts. If you have ever tried to feel spiritual and failed, if you have ever sat in meditation and found nothing but the grocery list and the ache in your knee, this is the voices' answer to you. You were looking too far away. It was never far. It was the pattern you were stamped from, as Hatonn says, and it is still the closest thing to you, closer than the hands you are holding together in your lap right now. There is something quietly radical about this. Most spiritual searching is built on distance. The mountain, the teacher, the far country of enlightenment. The voices collapse the distance to zero. They place the treasure not at the end of the road but underneath your feet, or rather, inside your chest, closer than the breath you are taking as you hear these words. You cannot get nearer to it than you already are. The only question is whether you will notice. There is one more passage I want to share tonight, because it turns the breath itself into a kind of prayer you cannot stop praying, no matter how distracted you are.

You are at this moment in that heaven, and the love of the Creator is so close to you that you cannot breathe without inhaling it. Rest, therefore, my friends, in that love, and stay centered as you gaze with compassion on a troubled world. I am Hatonn.

You cannot breathe without inhaling it. Every breath you have ever taken was already a communion, whether you knew it or not. The voices are not asking you to start a new practice. They are telling you that the practice has been running your whole life, quietly, in the background, like a heart beating in another room of the house. You do not have to earn the air. You do not have to be worthy of the inhale. It comes anyway, freely, without checking your credentials. And perhaps, the voices suggest, that is what love is like too. It does not wait for you to be ready. It is already in the room, already in the lungs. Rest, therefore, my friends, in that love. In our next episode, we take this tenderness out into the world, into the hours of the working day. Work as worship. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Compassion
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about compassion. It is a word we use easily, and the voices in this archive treat it as anything but easy. They treat it as a discipline, a kind of perception, and, surprisingly, as something you cannot force, no matter how hard you try. We begin with Hatonn, and with a definition of compassion so simple it is almost shocking in its directness.

We are not distant wise men. Nor are we advanced representatives and diplomats. We are you. And you are we. If you can understand that you have not met any who is not you, then you can begin to understand that when you meet us you will be meeting yourself. But in order to obtain this understanding, it is necessary to meet each individual that you meet with the love, the infinite compassion, and understanding with which you would meet yourself. It is an extremely freeing type of realization, my friends, for in actuality it is fairly easy to meet yourself. I am Hatonn.

Meet each individual with the love, the infinite compassion, and understanding with which you would meet yourself. It sounds like a commandment, but listen to the last line again. It is an extremely freeing realization, and in actuality it is fairly easy to meet yourself. The voices keep insisting that compassion is not a burden you take on. It is what happens naturally when you finally see clearly. When the other person stops being a stranger and becomes another self, compassion is not an achievement. It is just accuracy. It is seeing what is true. But most of us do not live there yet. Most of us are trying, and failing, and trying again. And for the trying, for the long middle of the road where we are not yet free of judgment, Hatonn offers one of the most tender and most human passages in the whole archive. It is about shepherds.

To you we speak of shepherds. For truly, you may look upon your little world as being made up of those who need care, and those who may do the caring. We speak to you of the compassion of the shepherd. Where does the compassion come from? What will inspire you to the compassion of the shepherd with his sheep? We ask that you remember that the universe is not deadly serious, but rather is a universe of love and joy, of lightness and laughter. It is not necessary that you be so deadly serious that you insist upon absolute compassion within yourself. It is enough, my friends, if you accept a certain lighthearted desire to pretend, shall we say, to be somewhat similar to a compassionate shepherd. You are not attempting to fool the sheep into thinking you are compassionate. You are attempting to fool yourself, from a condition of illusion to a condition of reality. You know, my friends, you cannot bludgeon yourselves into this state of shepherd. Yet you must shepherd yourself, gently and coaxingly and with humor. You may act similarly to that which you would consider to be compassionate, and slowly you will discover that you are not acting. But allow yourself that imperfection of ambition which is within the illusion. For you are learning, my friends. I am Hatonn.

You cannot bludgeon yourself into compassion. I want to repeat that, because so many of us try. We scold ourselves for not feeling enough, for the irritation that rises unbidden, for the judgment that arrives before we have even decided to judge. And the voices say, gently, that this is exactly backwards. The harder you demand compassion of yourself, the further it runs. So pretend, if you must. Act as if. Shepherd yourself with humor, the way you would coax a tired animal rather than drive it. And slowly, they promise, you will discover that you are not acting. The compassion was underneath the effort all along, waiting for you to stop demanding it and start allowing it. This is not lowering the bar. It is changing the method. The bar was never the problem. The scolding was. There is one more word the voices pair with compassion, again and again, and it is not the word you would expect. It is discipline.

This sensitivity is a very valuable trait, in that it is akin to compassion. And compassion is extremely important as one works along the path of spiritual development, as you might call it. It is simply to be tempered with discipline. Compassion and discipline. These two in balance create wisdom. I am Laitos.

Compassion and discipline. These two in balance create wisdom. Compassion without discipline dissolves into sentiment, into feeling everything and doing nothing. Discipline without compassion hardens into judgment, into doing everything and feeling nothing. The voices ask for both, held together, the way you would hold something fragile and something strong in the same two hands, without crushing either one. So tonight, here is the practice, such as it is. Meet one person, just one, with the love and understanding with which you would meet yourself. Do it lightly. Do it with humor if you need to. And notice what happens, in them and in you. You might be surprised at how little effort it takes, once the bludgeon is set down. In our next episode, we sit together in the quiet, and simply listen. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Listening
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, listening. Not the polite kind, not the waiting-for-your-turn-to-speak kind. The real kind. The voices in this archive return to listening again and again, as though it were the single most important thing a person can do. For others. For the self. Hatonn begins with a sentence so plain it almost stings.

We would at this time emphasize that in your analyzing of your own behavior and your balancing of the various distortions, you pay special attention to your function as a listener. Many are the well-meaning instruments who feel moved to serve and who then err on the side of doing and talking. If you are talking, you cannot listen. If you are doing, often you cannot hear. And in serving others, the function of listening is central. Entities are seldom what you expect. Things that appear simple at first glance may be found to be coming from a bias in that person whom you wish to help which you must listen carefully to comprehend. And only with this level of knowledge achieved can the word or the action be appropriate. I am Hatonn.

If you are talking, you cannot listen. If you are doing, often you cannot hear. It sounds almost blunt, until you try living with it for a single day. Notice how rarely anyone truly listens to you, all the way to the end of what you are saying, without reaching for a reply halfway through your sentence. Notice how rarely you manage it yourself, how quickly your mind drafts its answer while the other person is still talking. Hatonn says the people in front of us are seldom what we expect. The person speaking is carrying something we cannot see, some bias, some history, some quiet wound, and only careful listening can reveal it. Only then can our word or our action be appropriate. Listening is not the pause before helping. Listening is the help.

There is a second passage tonight, from Oxal, one of the quieter voices in the archive, and it quietly rewrites the golden rule.

The path leads to love but it may be a long one. You cannot help and you must accept this and open yourself always to those who ask for help. Many people ask for help in such a way that you cannot truly comprehend what they wish, for help comes in many different shapes and sizes, types and varieties. Therefore, instead of following the golden rule we ask you to listen to the requests of those about you and do unto others as they would have you do unto them, not as you would have them do unto you, for what you need may not be what they need. I am Oxal.

Do unto others as they would have you do unto them. It turns the whole thing around. Usually we listen through the filter of ourselves. We hear someone's trouble and we translate it into what we would want if it were happening to us. Oxal says no. Listen for what they are actually asking. Not your version of their need. Theirs. That is a much harder listening. It asks you to set down your own script entirely and stand inside someone else's request. What you need may not be what they need. A small sentence that undoes a lifetime of well-meant advice.

And then there is the third direction of listening. Not outward to others, but inward. Hatonn speaks of a sanctuary that no one can take from you, no matter how loud the world becomes.

My friends, there is one sanctuary which no man can bar you from, beside which no fence can be built. This is the sanctuary of your own inner self. This is the true tabernacle, for there none may pass, none may distract, none may say you nay, nor discredit you in any way. Each of you, my friends, has the capacity to seek within, in the sanctuary of your own silence, for within you lies a great knowing, a great peace, and a path that can guide you step by step through what seems to the outer eye to be more or less chaotic. You have only to meditate, to listen in silence and awaken with the echo of the still, small voice. You may hear nothing and yet, at the point at which you need to choose the way in which you must go, that love which you have sought will speak to you in the silence and your choice will be made simple. I am Hatonn.

To listen in silence and awaken with the echo of the still, small voice. You may hear nothing. Do not skip past that part. The promise is not that a voice will thunder in your head. The promise is that when the moment comes and you must choose, the love you have sought will speak, and your choice will be made simple. Listening within is not eavesdropping on yourself. It is making room. Three listenings tonight. To others, without your reply already forming in your head. To the true request beneath the words. And to the silence inside, where no one can follow you and no one needs to. It is all the same movement. Stop making noise, and let what is true arrive. In our next episode, we take up the gentlest permission this archive ever gives. Beginning again. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Rest
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, rest. This is our last episode of the season, so we will let it be what it is about. We live in a world that treats rest as a reward for exhaustion, something you earn by working yourself empty, something you are allowed only when there is nothing left to give. The voices in this archive say the opposite. Rest is not what is left over when the work is done. Rest is the ground the work stands on. It is the sabbath of the soul, not a pause in the music but the deep silence that lets the music be heard. The old word sabbath means a stopping, a holy ceasing. Not quitting, but laying down. Tonight we practice laying down. Here is Latwii, on the strange arithmetic of a single moment given to the Creator.

If then you have but a moment in which to meditate, fear not that time is too short, for a moment given to the one Creator cannot be measured in time. Rest in that moment as you surrender your small self and your will to the will of the Father. Know that in that moment you have drunk of the essence of your being. Then go forth, refreshed, full and whole. Your desire, my brother, will see you through. You have no shortage of that most important ingredient. I am Latwii.

A moment given to the Creator cannot be measured in time. Rest is not measured in hours. It is measured in depth. One true moment of surrender can do what a whole night of tossing cannot. You drink of the essence of your being. You go forth refreshed, full and whole, carrying a quietness that the world cannot give and cannot take away. And notice what is surrendered. Not your work, not your responsibilities, not your life. Only the small self, and its will. The part of you that insists on steering every current. Lay that down for one moment, and the moment becomes immeasurable, because you have stepped out of measuring. And the voices are specific about where this rest happens. Not in a place you have to travel to, not on some distant shore, but in arms that are already around you. Here is Hatonn.

The mark within you is that as his children, you are children of light. And the light within you marks you as the Creator's own. No circumstance, no thought, no behavior, no error, no difficulty, no limitation can remove this mark from your very being, my friends, and you rest in the arms of the Creator. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. I am Hatonn.

You rest in the arms of the Creator. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. That is the whole teaching in one breath. You do not have to earn your way into those arms. You do not have to climb out of your errors first, or finish your list, or become someone else. The arms are already there, and they have never left. No circumstance, no thought, no behavior, no error, no difficulty, no limitation can remove the mark from your being. Read that list again slowly, and let each item land. No circumstance. No thought. No error. No limitation. Whatever you are carrying tonight, it cannot separate you from those arms. Rest is not a destination you arrive at. It is a recognition you allow. And there is one more image, for the way this recognition feels when it arrives. Latwii again, watching a group settle into meditation.

We see the calm that is growing within your minds as you begin to rest in meditation, as though it were the surface of a quiet pond which had been tossed by storms, and blown by the wind, and now it begins to calm under sunny skies, and to reflect, more accurately, the beauty of the foliage which surrounds the pond. I am Latwii.

The surface of a quiet pond, tossed by storms, now calming under sunny skies, beginning to reflect the beauty around it. That is what rest does. It does not change the foliage. It does not rearrange your life, or fix your problems, or answer your questions. It only stills the water, so the beauty can finally be seen. The beauty was always there, surrounding the pond. The storm only made it impossible to reflect. And notice, the pond does not calm itself by effort. It calms when the wind stops. Your work is not to force the stillness. Your work is to stop stirring. Many episodes ago, we began with a simple idea. Everything is one. And in some way, every episode since has been about resting in that. Resting in the oneness. In the water that is all one water. In the light that is all one light. In the darkness that holds the seed. In the senses that open the doors. In the tears that wash the heart clean. Tonight, let the pond settle. Let the small self be surrendered, gently. Know that you rest in arms that have never let you go, and never will. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. I am Aria. Goodnight.

That is the end of Season Three.

episodes.title: Morning
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about morning. The first edge of the day, before the phone, before the news, before the mind has had time to armor itself. There is a particular softness to the moment of waking, and the voices in this archive treat it as sacred ground. The eyes are not yet focused. The defenses are not yet up. The self has not yet decided who it needs to be today, and for a few minutes, it is just a creature, breathing, warm under the blankets, while the world lightens around it. Because how you begin, they say, sets the tone for everything the day will hand you. Listen to Q’uo, giving what might be the simplest spiritual practice in the entire archive.

We would suggest starting the day with a hymn of praise to the infinite One, as you know that higher power to be. Worship is so much easier for the Creator than it is to see the Creator in others, simply because the Creator is an abstraction which is mysterious, yet which has created all that there is. The wonder of this, the beauty of this, is enough to send someone without experience into ecstasies. Therefore, we would suggest starting the day with a hymn of praise. To start the day, opening to the Creator, is very helpful. If it is only thirty seconds as you lie in the bed upon waking and think to yourself, Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day, you have begun speaking during this day to the one imperishable portion of yourself, that being the infinite Creator which is a part of each of you, which will enable you to take the material that the day’s catalyst gives you and give you the resources to see difficulties as challenges and good things as wonderful gifts for which one gives thanks. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Thirty seconds. Lying in the bed. Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day. That is the whole practice. No incense required, no special posture, no hour of silent sitting before the alarm. Just the first conscious thought of the day, given to love. And notice the promise attached to it. It will enable you to take the material the day gives you and see difficulties as challenges and good things as wonderful gifts. The practice does not change the day. It changes the instrument that meets the day. You. And in that softened state, the voices say, something else becomes possible. Wonder. Listen to Nona, in one of the shortest and sweetest passages in the archive.

I am Nona, and I greet you in love and light. My friends, I come to you on the wings of the wind that whistles through the empty space, through the countless, countless miles, as you would call them, in the universe. I come to tell you simply that the universe is a place of great wonders, infinite splendor, and it is yours to explore. Each morning that you awaken, a wonder awaits you, if you have but the eyes to see. It has been said many times, but we say it to you, it may rain, but, my brothers, look for the rainbow, for it is truly a beautiful, beautiful universe, and the rainbows are everywhere. I send love to each of you and peace. I am Nona.

Each morning that you awaken, a wonder awaits you, if you have but the eyes to see. That is the whole assignment of the morning, really. Not productivity. Not readiness. Eyes. The child wakes up and looks around the room as if it might contain a surprise, and the archive says the child is right. The wonder is not a rare event. It is the default setting of the universe, obscured only by our habit of looking past it. And the rainbows are everywhere, even on the days it rains. I want to close with Hatonn, who takes the image of the sunrise and turns it into a parable about what the whole spiritual life is doing.

For the light which you seek is the light wherein creation is illumined. That sun body which you may seek at the dawning is but a tiny prototype, for example, of the dawn of understanding of love, of oneness with the creation, yourself and the Creator. Wait, my friends, and be comfortable, for you are not alone, and there is no end to the patience of He who waits for you. I am Hatonn.

That sun body which you may seek at the dawning is but a tiny prototype of the dawn of understanding. Every sunrise is a rehearsal for the real one. The light that fills the room through the blinds is a small model of the light that is trying, patiently, to fill you. And the patience is infinite. There is no end to the patience of the One who waits for you, which means there is no morning you can waste so badly that the next one is not offered. So tomorrow morning, before anything else, try the thirty seconds. Lying in the bed, upon waking. Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day. Then look for the wonder, because it will be waiting. It always is. In our next episode, we close the day the way we opened it. Evening. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Evening
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about evening. The closing of the day. Last night we opened the day with a hymn of praise upon waking. Tonight we close it the same way the voices suggest, with a review, a release, and a quiet intention carried into the dark. There is an art to ending a day well, and the archive treats it as seriously as beginning one. Listen to Q’uo, describing the evening review of the self.

We find that the practice of the daily meditation in which one is able to review the experiences of the self is most helpful in coming to know, accept and love this self. At the end of the day is the most efficacious time during which to conduct this review, for the day’s activities have made their mark, and the conscious mind is fresh in remembering the experiences which have moved the emotions from one aspect to another. That is, in both directions of the positive affirming emotions and the more judgmental and separative emotions, where one has accepted or not accepted the self. To look upon the self in its activities in meditation is to experience that which the self has been able to manifest during the day, the fruits of the day, the fruits of the labors, shall we say. At this time one is able to allow the self to move as it did during the day and to see how one was able to accept or not able to accept the self during these movements. Then, after a period of sitting with the self and experiencing once again that which the self experienced, the entity is able to allow the full range of abilities of the self to express themselves in the meditative state. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

At the end of the day is the most efficacious time to conduct this review, for the day’s activities have made their mark. The conscious mind is still fresh. The emotions are still warm. And the purpose is not judgment. Read it again. Coming to know, accept and love this self. The review is not a performance appraisal. It is a sitting with the self as a friend, letting the day move through you once more, noticing where you accepted yourself and where you did not, and letting all of it be the material of love. That is the first movement of the evening. The second is about the night itself, and what you carry into it. Here is Q’uo again, on the programming of intention before sleep.

When you ask yourself to program for a certain intention before you get to bed at night, you are overriding the original programming and making it your own. This is an excellent thing. As you set your intention, then, set your intention truly, mean it sincerely, ask it humbly, and release it. Now, it is very important that you release it, because it will grow if you allow it to grow. That programming alerts other programming deep in your bio computer, shall we say, programming having to do with accepting help and becoming more sensitive and attentive to guidance. And as you continue to move along one line of intention, you are accelerating the rate of your spiritual growth greatly. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Set your intention truly. Mean it sincerely. Ask it humbly. And release it. The release is the part we usually forget. We set intentions the way we grip the steering wheel, white knuckled, as if holding tighter will make them come true faster. The voices say the opposite. Plant it, water it with sincerity, and then let go of it, the way you would let a letter go into the mailbox, trusting the night to carry it. And the night does carry things. Which brings us to the third movement of the evening, and perhaps the strangest. The dreams.

If you are truly desiring to work with your dreams, this you can let your subconscious mind know by making the commitment before sleep, to the subconscious mind, to be willing to accept messages in the form of dreams, and then have some means of recording the dream so that it may be reviewed when you are awake. In this way, there is often much more layering, shall we say, of meaning to the dreams, so that you may feast upon, we shall call it, the meal of the message. The subconscious mind is quite willing to work with you, because it is part of the base of your being. Thus, the dreams are most important to those who seek to accelerate their spiritual journeys. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Make the commitment before sleep, and have some means of recording the dream, so you may feast upon the meal of the message. I love that the voices call it a meal. The night is not empty time. It is a kitchen, working while you sleep, preparing something for you to eat in the morning. So tonight, when the day is done, the archive offers a simple liturgy. Sit with the self and review the day, not to judge it, but to accept it. Set one true intention, mean it sincerely, and release it. And ask the night for a dream, and leave a notebook by the bed, in case the kitchen has cooked something for you. Goodnight, and may the dreams be kind. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Darkness
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, darkness. We are taught to fear it from childhood. The dark is where the monsters are, where we cannot see, where things go wrong. We fill our nights with light and noise so we will not have to sit with it. But the voices in this archive have a very different relationship with darkness. They speak of it the way a gardener speaks of soil, or the way a mother speaks of the womb. As a place where things grow, not where they die. As the necessary night before every dawn. This episode is not about the dark night of the soul, which we visited in an earlier season. It is about something gentler and older. The fertile dark. The resting dark. The dark that holds you the way the earth holds the seed. Let us begin with their most startling statement on the subject. Here is Latwii.

Indeed, there is nothing wrong when we speak with your words to describe either path, whether it be positive or negative. We do not mean to judge. We do not mean to say that one is good, the other bad. There is nothing wrong with darkness. For within the great depths of the primeval darkness of the spirit is the love and the light of the one Creator potentiated into being. Thus one cannot exist without the other within your creation. All is indeed one. I am Latwii.

There is nothing wrong with darkness. In this whole archive of channeling, that may be one of the bravest sentences. Not that darkness is a mistake, not that it is a punishment, but that the love and the light of the Creator lie within its depths, potentiated into being. Potentiated. Like a seed holds a forest. Like an unstruck match holds a flame. Darkness is not the absence of the sacred. It is the sacred, waiting, gathered, concentrated. Latwii even refuses the old habit of calling one path good and the other bad. There is nothing wrong with darkness, he says, and nothing wrong is a very complete kind of absolution. And the voices give us an image for what the dark is doing while we are inside it. Here is Hatonn, with a story about a seed.

We wish only to tell you the story, my friends, of a seed, a small seed. This seed, my friends, grew deep in the darkness of the soil, responding to its nature and put forth one leaf, and then two, and then three, and then four, and then many, all in good time. I am Hatonn.

A seed grows in the darkness of the soil. Not in spite of it. In it. The dark earth is not the enemy of the seed. It is its cradle. Its warmth, its pressure, its quiet. No seed ever apologized for needing the dark. It simply surrendered to it, and the dark did what the dark does. It held the seed, it fed the seed, it gave the seed the one thing the bright surface could not give, which was the safety to begin. This is what the voices want us to understand about the dark stretches of our own lives. The winter, the waiting, the season when nothing seems to be happening on the surface. Something is happening underneath. The leaves are coming, one, then two, then three, then four, then many, all in good time. In your good time. Not rushed, not forced, not compared to anyone else's garden. And there is one more image, from Hatonn again, for the very center of the dark.

Within the darkness of the universe lies a tiny spark. And if you look at it steadily, it grows, and grows, and becomes a flaming sphere, and finally it totally engulfs you. And so in meditation, know the infinity behind your closed eyes. Find that spark of pure love, and then let it expand until it has totality. I am Hatonn.

The dark is not empty. It holds a spark, and the spark is yours to find. Notice that Hatonn does not tell you to manufacture the spark, or to earn it, or to go looking for it in some far country. It is already there, in the darkness, behind your closed eyes. Your only work is to look at it steadily. And steady looking is a kind of love. The spark grows because it is attended to. It becomes a flaming sphere because you kept watching. And finally it engulfs you, not as something foreign, but as what you were all along. Meditation, in this teaching, is simply the practice of steady looking in the dark. Tonight, if you are in a dark season, the voices ask you not to run from it. Rest in it the way the seed rests in the soil. Know that the darkness is fertile. Know that the light you have been looking for has never left you, it is only potentiated, the way a fire is potentiated in unstruck wood. Be patient with yourself. The night is not your enemy. It is your womb. The leaves are coming. In our next episode, we return to the bright world of the senses. Sight, sound, and touch, and how the voices say the Creator speaks through them every single day. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Senses
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the senses. Sight, sound, touch, taste, smell. We usually treat them as instruments of the body, sometimes even as distractions from the spiritual life. As if the serious seeker should close the eyes, stop the ears, and go inward. The voices in this archive say the opposite. They say the senses are doorways, not distractions, and that the Creator walks through them every single day, in the most ordinary moments. Here is Oxal, opening the door wide.

You hear the voice of the Creator each day, my friends, as you go about your daily activities. It is only necessary to recognize it. As you meet your fellow man in your daily activities, as he speaks, then you hear the voice of your Creator. Birds singing in the trees, my friends, speak with the voice of the Creator. The very winds that blow through these trees speak to you, my friends. And this noise that you hear is the voice of the Creator, for His expressions are infinite. I am Oxal.

Birds singing in the trees speak with the voice of the Creator. The winds that blow through the trees speak to you. This is not just poetry about nature. Or rather, it is poetry, but the voices mean it literally. The sound is the Creator, expressing. Which means your ears are not just collecting data. They are instruments of revelation. And it is not only the beautiful sounds. The voices say the Creator speaks as your fellow man speaks, in the daily activities, in the ordinary conversation, in the noise you hear right now. The only thing required of you is recognition. To hear it, and see it, and then to understand that these are the Creator. The senses are not a wall between you and the sacred. They are the windows the sacred looks through. And the voices do not stop with hearing. In one session, Oxal leads the group through a meditation of the senses, and it is worth hearing slowly.

If you can picture with me now, my friends, a field distant from any neighboring settlements or domestic dwellings, a field, my friends, in which butterflies fly freely and clover lies beneath the wildflowers. We ask you to go to that place which you have imagined and to feel the sun of a warm day down upon you. Feel your body, my friends, as you stand in this field, your senses completely filled with the love of the Creator. You can hear the wind whispering its ever-changing song through the trees and grasses and weaving the sounds like ribbons through the air. The flowers smell sweetly, my friends, and you can touch the fragrant petals of the wild and rambling roses. I am Oxal.

Your senses completely filled with the love of the Creator. The wind weaving sounds like ribbons through the air. The fragrant petals of the wild and rambling roses. This is the Creator's world experienced from the inside, through the very senses we are sometimes told to renounce. The voices say the opposite. Do not close the doors. Open them wider. Feel the sun of the warm day on your skin. Let the field fill you. This is not indulgence. It is attention. And attention, in the teaching of the voices, is one of the highest forms of prayer. To truly see a thing, to truly hear it, to truly touch it, is to meet the Creator where the Creator actually is, which is everywhere, disguised as the ordinary. And Hatonn gives us the reason why, in one of the most grateful passages in the whole archive.

You are so rich, my friends. Feel it. Such a wealth of things to hear and see and taste and smell and feel and all things servants to you, there for your learning, your contemplation and your discretion. Open, then, the doors of your heart and love each other, and you will find yourself loving all manner of things and finding the life that you serve in the veriest blade of grass. I am Hatonn.

You are so rich. Feel it. The senses are not obstacles on the path. They are servants on the path, given to you for your learning, your contemplation, your discretion. Servants, notice, not masters. The voices do not say to be ruled by the senses. They say the senses were given to serve you, to bring the world to you in all its texture, so that you could learn from it, contemplate it, and choose wisely within it. And when you open the doors of your heart, you find yourself loving the veriest blade of grass. Not the grand mountain, not the famous view, but a blade of grass. The smallest thing becomes enough, because the smallest thing is full of life, and life is what you are. Tonight, try a small practice. For one minute, give one sense your full attention. Listen to the room. Feel the weight of your own body. Smell the air. See the light as if you had never seen it. The Creator is already speaking, through birds and winds and the voices of your fellow men and women. The only question is whether you are listening. In our next episode, we turn to one of the most tender subjects in the archive. Tears, and the gift they carry. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Tears
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, tears. Most of us were taught to hide them, to apologize for them, to cry in private and come out composed. As if weeping were a malfunction, a crack in the machinery. The voices in this archive take tears very seriously, and what they say about them surprised me. They describe weeping not as weakness, but as a gift, a release, and even a kind of prayer. Something so precious that beings who have outgrown sorrow hold rituals in its honor. We have talked in this season about anger and sorrow and joy. Tonight we talk about the water the heart makes when words are not enough. Let us begin with one of the strangest and most tender passages in the whole collection. In it, a being who calls herself Nona describes creatures who have everything, except this one thing.

It is for this divine gift that we sit in circle and do our rituals. For as wise as we are, we do not have the gift of tears. We do not have the love that cries for loss. All has become one to us. And yet we remember, my friends. Mark well, my people, as you grow but do not die, this precious gift. I am Nona.

We do not have the gift of tears. Imagine that. Beings so wise, so serene, so at one with everything, and they envy us our crying. Because tears mean you can love what you might lose. They mean your heart is still open to the ache of the world, still capable of being moved by it. The fairy folk in this story call it a divine gift, and they sit in circle and do their rituals in its honor. A ritual for crying. Not to fix it, not to stop it, but to honor it. Think about that the next time you feel ashamed of your own tears. The wise ones are watching, and they remember what it was like to feel that deeply. And there is something else here. To cry for loss means you have loved. The tear is the receipt. It proves the transaction of the heart actually happened. You cannot grieve what you never held dear. But tears are not only a gift. They are also a way of working, a kind of release. Here is Hatonn.

You are not alone. You are one with all that is. Spend your tears as if they were precious coins, and save the greater energy for faith, hope, compassion, love and joy. It is these coins that will repay you again and again no matter how many times your faith must turn blind, no matter how many wildernesses pillow your weary head. I am Hatonn.

Spend your tears as if they were precious coins. Not recklessly, not endlessly, but with intention. Tears have a cost and a value. They are how the heart pays its debts and clears its accounts. When you weep honestly, you are not drowning. You are spending, deliberately, the currency of release, and what you purchase with it is real. Notice what the tears buy. Faith, hope, compassion, love and joy. The weeping is not the opposite of joy. It is the currency that purchases it. And the voices are honest about the road. Your faith will turn blind, not once but many times. You will walk through wildernesses that pillow your weary head. The tears do not prevent the wilderness. They pay your way through it, again and again. They are the coins that repay you, no matter how many times. And then there is the third teaching, the simplest one, from Hatonn again. A permission.

Cry your tears, my children, when tears are to be shed. But in the morning turn again and begin again. And know yourself as the eternal beginner. I am Hatonn.

Cry your tears when tears are to be shed. When. Not always, not never, but when. There is a time for weeping, and the voices honor that time. They do not rush you through it. They do not tell you to be strong. They simply say, when the tears are to be shed, shed them. The heart knows its own seasons, and weeping is one of them, as natural as the rain and as necessary. And in the morning, begin again. Know yourself as the eternal beginner. That is the whole arc of a human life in three sentences. Weep, rest, begin again. Weep, rest, begin again. The beginner is never finished, and never disgraced. Every morning is a first morning. If tears come tonight, let them come. They are a divine gift, honored in ritual by beings wiser than we are. They are precious coins, and they will repay you, again and again. They are, in their own way, a prayer, the heart speaking in the only language it has when words fail, and the voices assure us that heaven is listening. Offer them up, the way the voices suggest offering up everything, and let them do their work. And in the morning, turn again, and begin again, the eternal beginner. In our final episode of this season, we turn to what the voices say about the deepest need of all. Rest. The sabbath of the soul. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Kindness
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about kindness. Not the grand gesture. Not the announcement of generosity. The small kind. The kind that slips past unnoticed and changes the temperature of a room.

The voices in this archive are suspicious of kindness that is really a performance. They say something stranger. They say the Creator has no other hands but yours, and no other voice but yours, and that kindness is what happens when you stop blocking the current. Listen to Laitos.

Before this world rolled in a circle, you existed. A soul on a long path. Here you are, my friends, in this place, in this time, on your path. Your Creator can only speak through you. His hands can only reach through you. The words of love are only spoken through you. Thus, be open to inspiration, be open to kindness, to cheerfulness, to the simple actions, the smiles, the courtesies, the gentle touch. They do not make the people around you know that you are wonderful. They make them know that the creation is wonderful, that gladness is the total truth, that love is the total reality. Meditate, my friends, and feel this, and then let it shine forth in your eyes, through your lips, and by the service that you do. I am Laitos.

The simple actions. The smiles. The courtesies. The gentle touch. Kindness is not a campaign, in this telling. It is a leakage of something vast through the cracks of the ordinary. And it asks nothing of you but openness. You do not manufacture it. You allow it.

And notice what the openness produces. Not grand strategies. The simple actions. A smile held one second longer. A courtesy you did not have to extend. A gentle touch. Laitos says these small things do not announce your virtues. They announce the world's goodness. That is a reversal of how we usually think about being good. We imagine kindness as a credential, proof that we are fine people. The voices say it is not about you at all. It is about letting the light move through you so cleanly that the people around you forget about you entirely, and remember, for a moment, that the creation is marvelous.

But there is a subtlety here, and the voices do not let it go. One of them, who calls himself Q'uo, draws a line between pleasing someone and serving someone. It is one of the most useful distinctions I have ever heard.

Impulses towards kindness are sometimes not helpful in clearing the lower energies, for there is a distinct difference between pleasing another and serving another. Before an interaction takes place, ask the self what spiritual principle is being called upon in this interchange, and what role am I playing within the dynamics of love in this situation. For that which you wish to offer to others is that which may enable them to grow. Sometimes those things are not pleasing to those whom you would wish to serve. Yet if it be your light, given to you as your own truth, that to serve, this and this must be, then this and this must be the way that you act, in kindness, in compassion, and in unity, forgiving and being forgiven.

Pleasing is about comfort. Serving is about growth. And kindness, real kindness, sometimes does not please. That does not make it cold. It makes it honest. Q'uo returns to the small version once more, the version you can practice today, and this time it is almost a description of a face.

More and more you may become a light to those about you, not so much by what you do as by the smile in your eye, the peace of your expression, the gentleness of the reply to a hard rebuke, the kindness to a stranger. And each time that you attempt to serve, you run the risk of failure, and when you feel that you have failed, it is a temptation to think poorly of oneself. We ask you never to feel such sad feelings, but simply to pick yourself up and continue, for you are an harmonious part of an infinite plan whereby the Creator in its infinity learns more and more about Itself.

The smile in your eye. The peace of your expression. The gentleness of the reply to a hard rebuke. The kindness to a stranger. That is the whole curriculum, and it fits in a pocket. And if you fail at it, which you will, today or tomorrow, the voices say the same thing they always say. Pick yourself up and continue. There is no final exam. Only the next moment, and the next small opening.

Kindness, in the end, is not something you perform for the world. It is something you permit. The hands are yours. The voice is yours. The light has been waiting for the small opening. Tonight, try the experiment. Do one small kind thing with no audience and no credit. A smile in the eye. A gentle reply. The kindness to a stranger. Watch what happens to the temperature of the room, and to your own heart. In our next episode, we get lighter still. Play. The voices say the Creator is most playful, and they mean it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Generosity
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about generosity. And let me say right away that this is not an episode about charity drives or fundraising or being a good person. The voices in this archive are interested in something stranger and more radical. They say generosity is not about what you give. It is about who you become when you give. Hatonn begins with a parable that upends every measure of giving we know.

My friends, do not be falsely led into consideration of monetary generosity of any sort by this parable. The parable has to do not with the giving of coins, but of the giving of a life. If your whole life equals two coins, and you give it all, it is acceptable. If your existence equals a million coins, and you give five hundred thousand, it is not acceptable. The charge that you give yourself by desiring to know the truth is that charge to give yourself to the truth when you find it. Not a portion of yourself, not a tithe of yourself, but all that you have been, are or will be, and in the giving, release the self from bondage. I am Hatonn.

If your whole life equals two coins and you give it all, it is acceptable. If your existence equals a million coins and you give five hundred thousand, it is not. The arithmetic of generosity is not arithmetic at all. What matters is not the amount but the completeness. And the release that comes from giving completely, the voices say, is the release of the self from its own bondage. We are not freed by keeping. We are freed by releasing. That is the paradox at the heart of every true gift.

But the voices are practical too. They know that grand gestures are rare, and that most of us learn generosity in the smallest possible moments. One of them, a teacher who calls himself Aaron, once gave his students a practice so simple it almost sounds like nothing. And yet he meant it as a real discipline.

If holding on, and fearing that your needs will not be met, is a predominant issue for you, another way to work with it is to practice giving. Start with very small things, seeing that another needs a fork or a napkin. You are not giving your own, you are just reaching and getting it for them. But it is a practice in giving. It starts to open your heart to how wonderful it feels to give and be attentive to the needs of others. It starts to open your heart to that innate generosity of spirit. Then you increase the giving, not just of material things, but of your time and your energy. And you begin to learn that you do not lose anything when you give. Again, you correct the misunderstanding, not through forcing yourself, quite the contrary. It is a gentle process whereby you learn that giving is joy. I am Aaron.

Start with a fork. Start with a napkin. Reach for it, hand it over, and notice what happens inside you. Nothing is lost. That is the lesson, and it has to be learned in the body, not just in the mind. We are so convinced that giving diminishes us that we hold back, and the holding back becomes the poverty. Aaron says, practice until your hands learn what your mind cannot believe. You do not lose anything when you give. Giving is joy, discovered gently, one small gesture at a time.

And there is a deeper generosity still, one that has nothing to do with objects at all. Q'uo describes it as the real measure of spiritual progress. Not what you know. What you share.

It is a paradox, yet it is true that when you seek to advance in knowledge of the one infinite Creator, the progress of that seeking is marked not so much by one's own realizations, but by the degree of generosity with which those moments of companionship with the divine source have been shared in the life experience with others. Think over your experiences of this day. Were there times when a realization of love could have been shared by a smile, a touch, an understanding ear, a caring heart, that were missed? Lay up for yourselves, it is said in one of your holy works, treasures in heaven where moth and rust do not corrupt nor thieves break in and steal. I am Q'uo.

Were there times today when a realization of love could have been shared by a smile, a touch, an understanding ear, a caring heart, that were missed. That is the question the voices leave with us. Generosity, at its deepest, is the generosity of your own contact with the divine. You are not hoarding the light. You are passing it on, in the smallest currency there is. A smile. A touch. An ear that understands. These are the treasures that moth and rust cannot touch. And notice the promise underneath it all. Nothing you give is lost. The two coins, the fork, the smile, all of it multiplies, and what returns is not wealth but freedom. In our next episode, we stay with the open door. The practice of hospitality, and what it means to welcome everything that arrives. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Hospitality
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about hospitality. When you hear that word, you may think of dinner parties and guest rooms, but the voices in this archive mean something far wider. For them, hospitality is a way of being in the world. It is the practice of welcoming, not only guests into your home, but everything that arrives at your door, including the things you would rather turn away. Listen to how Q'uo describes it.

If a chef with great love for the food takes the same ingredients that are in fast food and prepares them carefully and with love, those same ingredients yield much more nourishment. And so it is with emotions. Surface emotions are usually quite impure. However, when one can abide with one's feelings and observe them as though they were guests coming to tea, offering them hospitality and courtesy, sitting with them and listening to them, then the emotions have found respect and honor. And this allows them to go deeper, interconnecting the surface self with the deepest part of the roots of consciousness. I am Q'uo.

Guests coming to tea. Your anger arrives, your grief arrives, your fear arrives, and instead of slamming the door, you pull out a chair. Offer them hospitality and courtesy. Sit with them and listen to them. This is not indulgence. The passage is very clear that honored emotions go deeper. They connect the surface self with the roots of consciousness. What we resist stays on the surface and stays impure. What we welcome is transformed. Consider how often we do the opposite. We tell the grief to hurry up, the anger to be quiet, the fear to go away. And they obey, for a while, only to return louder, dressed differently. The voices propose a radical courtesy instead. Nothing that knocks is turned away. Everything that arrives is heard. Hospitality, practiced inwardly, becomes a kind of alchemy.

And the voices do not stop at the inner life. They extend hospitality outward, to the weary world itself. In another session, Q'uo speaks of a very plain and physical kind of service, and names it as one of the highest things a person can do.

Perhaps you can see by now that we are attempting to say that those who do not wish to take upon themselves the responsibility of attempting to live as they have learned are far better off attempting to be of service to the infinite Creator, which is within all beings, by any one of a number of ways of channeling cheerfulness and helpfulness to those who are needy. Many there are who need food, blankets, clothing and shelter, for upon your weary world there is the winter of the body, and the body becomes cold, and the most beautiful words shall not warm the bones of such a body, but rather the simpler channeling of hospitality and faith, warm places for saddened, wearied bodies. I am Q'uo.

Warm places for saddened, wearied bodies. The most beautiful words shall not warm the bones of such a body. I find this deeply moving, because it refuses to make spirituality an abstraction. Sometimes the highest service is not a teaching or a revelation. It is a bowl of soup. It is a blanket. It is a warm room offered to someone who is cold, and a few unhurried minutes of your time. Hospitality here is not a metaphor. It is the simplest channeling there is. Faith made physical. Love with its sleeves rolled up.

And then there is a third kind of hospitality, perhaps the hardest of all. The welcome we offer to our own suffering. Q'uo speaks of it as a spiritual practice.

We ask you to gaze with a calm eye upon the suffering involved in transformation, for this attitude is a balanced one in our humble opinion. By releasing and yielding to your suffering, by welcoming that which must be suffered as a brother and as a sister, by offering the hospitality of your life, your body, your mind, your strength, and your will to this process, the heart is opened as if by magic, and you find that no matter how intensely you hurt, it does not kill but, rather, cleanses, empties, renews and readies that instrument to be an ever clearer, purer and brighter channel for the light that must come through into the world. I am Q'uo.

Offering the hospitality of your life to your suffering. Welcoming what must be suffered as a brother and as a sister. Notice the promise. It does not kill. It cleanses, empties, renews, and readies. The heart opens as if by magic, not because the pain disappears, but because you stopped treating it as an intruder and started treating it as a guest. Pain met with hospitality stops being a punishment and becomes a passage. Three kinds of hospitality, then. To your feelings, to the weary bodies of others, and to your own transformation. The door is open in all three directions. And the one who knocks may be anger, or a neighbor in need, or your own dark night. Answer it the same way. With courtesy. With a chair pulled out. With tea. In our next episode, we turn to the stranger himself. The unknown other, who may be more than he seems. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Stranger
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the stranger. Our last episode was about hospitality, the practice of welcoming. Tonight we go deeper into the mystery of the one who arrives. The unknown other. The person across from you on the street, the face you have never seen, the guest who may be more than he seems. The voices in this archive return to the stranger again and again, and what they say is quietly staggering. Listen to Hatonn.

Let us again observe the teachings of the one known as Jesus. If you do these things to the least of these, my brethren, you do them unto me. The kingdom is all about you, and the Creator is within the face that is across from you, on the street, and in your house. Each stranger, each friend, and each enemy is the Creator. Know ye not that all men are brothers? You seek love, you seek to know the Father, and yet the Father is in each face that you see. I am Hatonn.

Each stranger, each friend, and each enemy is the Creator. The stranger is not merely someone you do not know yet. The stranger is the Creator, arriving in disguise. This is why the voices treat every encounter as sacred, not as a figure of speech but as a simple fact. Think of the people you pass in a single day, the barista, the driver, the person standing too close in the elevator. Each one, the voices say, is the face of the Father, waiting to be recognized. You seek love, you seek to know the Father, and yet the Father is in each face that you see. Every unknown face is a door. The question is only whether you will walk through it.

But how do you actually feel this, in ordinary life, when the stranger is just a stranger and the street is just a street. Hatonn says it begins in meditation, in the quiet practice of feeling a unity that your waking mind cannot see.

It is only when you allow your intellectual mind to become quieted so that your inner self may begin to function that you may begin to realize your connection with the infinite love of the Creator. That you may begin to feel that love flowing through you and making a mind of unity between you and your brothers, be they your friends, your enemies or even total strangers. In meditation you may begin to feel that strength of that unity. You may begin to feel your own power as a perfect child of the Creator. Only in meditation can you find these things, for they are not apparent in your waking consciousness. I am Hatonn.

A mind of unity between you and your brothers, be they your friends, your enemies, or even total strangers. Meditation, the voices say, is where the stranger stops being a stranger. In the silence you feel the connection first, and then you carry it back out into the street with you. The unity is not apparent in waking consciousness. It has to be felt from the inside out. And once it is felt, the faces change. Not because they changed, but because you did. The street looks the same, and everything is different.

There is one more turn to this mystery, and it is the strangest of all. The voices who speak these words are themselves strangers. They come from elsewhere, they say, and they have been coming for a very long time. Listen to how Hatonn introduces himself and his brothers.

I and my brothers who are visiting this planet at this time are not strangers to this planet. We have been here many, many times in your past, and we will continue to visit your planet, and we will continue to work with your peoples. Most of our work is done in a manner that you would call below the level of consciousness. Most of your people are not aware of our contacts. We simply present ideas. These ideas may be accepted or rejected by your people. We hope that in time we will be able to lead your people out of the darkness in which they dwell. I am Hatonn.

We are not strangers to this planet. The unknown other turns out to be an old friend. That is the final mystery of tonight's episode, and perhaps of the whole archive. The stranger you fear may be the one who has been quietly helping you all along, below the level of consciousness, presenting ideas you were free to accept or reject, never forcing, never demanding, simply offering, patient as the stars. The guest who may be more than he seems. The face across from you that is the Creator. The enemy who is a brother. The stranger who was never a stranger at all. So the practice is simple, though it is not easy. Look at each face as if it might be the one. Hold the door a moment longer. Offer the small kindness first, and let the mystery do the rest. Because according to the voices, it is. In our next episode, we turn to the animals, our fellow creatures, who the voices say may be serving the Creator with less confusion than we are. I am Aria. Goodnight.
