episodes.title: Play
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about play. The spiritual life is not supposed to have a sense of humor about itself. It is supposed to be serious, furrowed, profound. The voices in this archive disagree. They keep saying the same impolite thing. You are taking this too seriously. Lighten up.

Think about how much of our inner life is grim determination. We approach growth the way we approach a difficult project. Plans. Discipline. Solemn faces. And somewhere in that effort, we forget the thing we are growing toward. Joy. The voices say the goal is not a heavier you. The goal is a lighter you. And the way there is not through more pressure. It is through play.

They call it light-hearted irreverence, and they recommend it like medicine.

One thing we do recommend for all who experience confusion is a very well-encouraged sense of humor. The most helpful point of view for a changing spiritual seeker is light-hearted irreverence. Play with that which is occurring. Be playful. Allow the vision to relax, the eyesight to become less than entirely single-mindedly keen when the pressure mounts and the anxiety builds, when frustration and anger begin to accumulate. Lighten your own load with laughter. And if you can laugh with another, the strength of this joy is doubled. Part of the service spiritual seekers may be to each other is to exhort and encourage each other to take it easier with the situation and the self.

Lighten your own load with laughter. Not as decoration. As practice. As a way of loosening the grip of the mind that thinks it must solve everything by thinking harder.

There is a deeper point hidden in the prescription. When you play with what is occurring, you stop treating your life as an emergency. The anxiety needs the emergency to survive. The frustration feeds on the seriousness. Play starves them both, gently, the way sunlight dries a puddle. And when two people laugh together, the voices say the strength of this joy is doubled. Play, it turns out, is a social sacrament. One of the quiet services seekers do for each other is to talk each other down from the cliff of taking it all too hard.

One of the voices, Aaron, noticed something strange about this planet. He says we do something no other beings do. We ration our playfulness.

There is no other plane that I know of where beings limit their playfulness, the natural playfulness of their light, as much as they do on the earth plane. It is part of your illusion of separation.

Our playfulness is rationed by an illusion. Let that sit for a moment. The joy is natural to the light itself, and the dimming of it is something we learned here, something we agreed to. Which means we can also unlearn it.

Think of the children you have known. Nobody had to teach them to play. They arrived knowing. The teaching went the other way. We taught them to stop. To sit still. To be serious. The voices suggest the lesson was never true, and the child was right all along. The playfulness is not immaturity. It is the native state of the light.

There is a reason play works as a spiritual practice. Play is trust in motion. When you play, you surrender control of the outcome. You let the moment be what it is. That is the same surrender the great meditations are trying to teach, only the children got there first, and they did not need a cushion or a candle to do it.

Q'uo goes further. The light touch is not just a relief from seriousness. It is a description of the Creator itself.

And we encourage each to find the light touch, to share the laughter and the silliness of such idealistic and spiritual goals. There is rich humor in every fiber of your density. The less you blink, the less you are overcome by the seriousness of situations, the more humor you shall find, for the Creator is most playful. So allow that spirit within to romp and play, and, above all things, to reach out to others as they ask, as you can serve. For the love you bear each other is that fruit which the other cannot create, and love is the great gift, the inner and deeper truth of all being and all relationship.

The Creator is most playful. Not most solemn. Most playful. If that is true, then play is not the opposite of the sacred. It is the native language of the sacred, and our solemnity is the accent we picked up along the way.

And look what the playfulness produces. The light touch. The shared silliness. The reaching out to others as they ask. The whole passage ends not in frivolity but in service, because that is what play really is. Not escape from the world. The world, held lightly.

So tonight, the practice is simple. Be silly on purpose. Laugh at the situation, and at yourself. Let the spirit romp. The voices promise it will not make you less spiritual. It will make you more like the thing you are trying to become. In our next episode, we go inward. Solitude, and the holy of holies within the self. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Solitude
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about solitude. Not loneliness. Solitude. The deliberate turning inward, away from the noise, toward the quiet place where something is waiting for you.

Hatonn begins with a confession of a kind. He says that for every soul, there is a solitude that nothing can keep company with. Not because we are abandoned. Because the deepest part of the journey is ours alone, and always was.

I cannot express to you my sympathy and understanding of what you are experiencing. For each soul, my sister, there is a great solitude. One soul is on one path. And no one or no thing can keep that soul company on that path. For each entity is the Creator, is primary, and must teach itself what it already knows. Sometimes, my sister, in this loneliness, we have bad dreams. We are not speaking of literal dreams. We are speaking of times when a shadow seems to be over our lives. We are not free of these upon the plane from which I speak. Yes, we have advanced, yet we do not know all. We are alone in our way, as we speak of unity, yet we have loneliness when we are not able to totally live this understanding. These moments grow fewer and fewer as you continue to seek. It is a matter of being in reality instead of the illusion. When the shadow falls across you, my sister, know it for an illusion. If you must speak aloud to remind yourself, you may say, all is love. And you will feel reality flow within you at that moment. I am Hatonn.

Even the voices have their shadows. Even they know solitude. That is oddly comforting. The loneliness is not a sign you are doing it wrong. It is the condition of having your own path, which no one else can walk for you.

And Hatonn offers a practice for the shadow times. Say it aloud if you must. All is love. Three words. A reminder that the loneliness you feel is the illusion, and the unity you cannot feel is the reality. It is the kind of advice that sounds too simple to work, and it works anyway.

Q'uo explains why some of us need solitude the way the body needs air. It is one of the most tender passages in the whole archive.

The next great category of reasons people yearn for solitude is the category which is a dynamic of sensitivity. There are many to whom relating to the self has been in some way blocked. Part of the young experience has caused the entity to seek solitude in order to be comfortable, for there is perceived the discomfort in company, and this discomfort builds up within such an entity. When such a one reaches a solitary place, there is the feeling of safety and of relaxation. It is almost as though the mind and emotions constituted another organ such as the lungs, and as the lungs need to breathe for the organism to live, so the entity must be solitary in order for the emotional and mental faculties to remain acute. For if this need is ignored, there is the equivalent lack of oxygen to the brain, that is, oxygen to the emotions and mind.

Solitude as breathing. The lungs of the inner life. Some of us do not withdraw because we are broken. We withdraw because the organ needs air. And when we have breathed, we come back.

And here is what the breathing is for. Q'uo names the deepest use of solitude. Not rest, not recovery, though those matter. Union.

However, there is one form of solitary practice which deserves notice above all else, and that is the solitude within in which one turns to the holy of holies within the self. In meditation, a link is sought in spiritual solitude. Through that solitude the seeking soul stretches out its purified desire, and the silence answers in thought too poignant, too profound, too deep for words. Treasure those moments with the infinite One, and know that each moment wherein the Creator has been sought is lightening the consciousness of your people and doing needed work in establishing the generation of an ever fuller light upon your sphere.

The holy of holies within the self. You do not go into solitude to escape the world. You go in to find the one place the world cannot follow, and there, in the silence, you discover that the silence answers. And the strangest part. Those private moments, alone in a room, are doing work for everyone. They lighten the consciousness of your people. The most solitary act turns out to be the most generous one.

So if you are someone who needs the quiet, stop apologizing for it. The need is not a flaw in your character. It is an organ in your soul, doing its job. Breathe. Turn inward. The silence is waiting, and it has been waiting since before you were born, and it is not in a hurry, and it has something for you that no crowd can give. Go gently, and come back changed, and carry the quiet with you into the noise. In our next episode, we come back out. Community, and what it means to belong. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Community
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about community. Not the institution. Not the mailing list. The living thing that happens when separate souls decide to turn toward the same light, together.

Hatonn is direct about it. If you want to help the world through its changes, do not do it alone. Find your people, and be a center of light with them.

As you know, we are a planetary consciousness, and therefore it is not surprising that we suggest that those of you who desire to aid the planet during these times of change find groups of like-minded people and work as a community. For it is in community that your best abilities both to survive and to be a center of light will be realized. We are attempting to give you guidelines to follow so that the vibrational change and its after-effects will not seem overly traumatic, but will seem in some ways a ray of hope. For you will see people turning from their previous sleep and awakening. Therefore, we encourage you in your dedication and are with you whenever you ask.

To survive, and to be a center of light. Notice the pairing. Community is not just comfort. It is how the light gets concentrated enough to do work in the world. One candle is lovely. A circle of candles changes the room.

The light gets concentrated. Think of it as physics. A single candle can be cupped out by one breath of wind. A circle of candles protects the flame. The voices are not being sentimental about togetherness. They are being practical. The work of this time is too large for solitary heroes. It needs circles.

And notice the deeper promise tucked inside the practical advice. People are waking up. They are asking the oldest question, what happens when the body ends, and they are asking it out loud, to each other. Community is where the answers get found, not in books, but in the shared experience of seekers walking side by side.

But there is something even deeper here, and Q'uo says it in a single image I cannot get out of my head. Each of us is a note, and the whole creation is listening.

Each person within a family, within a community, within a classroom has a part to play that influences the whole. The whole of the classroom, of the family, of the community has an influence upon each individual. The touch and presence and mark made by each entity is felt not only within the family, the classroom, and the community, but is felt within the planetary being and indeed throughout the one creation, for there is a connection between all portions of creation. As a note played upon a musical instrument is heard by any ear within its range of sound, thus are feelings and thoughts and actions recorded within the self, within the family, within the Earth itself, and indeed each is heard as a note throughout the one creation.

You are a note in the song. What you play is heard everywhere. Which means community is not only the people in the room with you. It is the resonance you leave in everything you touch.

There is a mercy in this image too. You cannot play a wrong note so wrong that the song stops. The instrument is the creation itself. Your part is small, but it is heard, and it matters to the whole. The community is not grading you. It is listening for you. So stop performing for it. Just sound your note, honestly, the way only you can, and let the song do the rest.

And here is Q'uo's most breathtaking claim about togetherness. Time, they say, is an illusion. And that means the community of seekers is not scattered across centuries. It is gathered. Now. All of it. Including you.

Let us gaze at the community of the faithful upon your sphere. You know intellectually that time is an illusion. This means that all of you are together now, linked, whole and entire. All your prayers, your meditations and your thoughts, mingle in glorious harmony and ring in euphony to the honor and the glory of the one Creator. As there is no time, there is no space. So all of you are linked far more closely than you may ever realize. As each of you approaches more and more purity of service, so you approach more and more closely the unity of those who serve.

All of you are together now. Linked, whole and entire. Every seeker who ever sat in a quiet room and tried to love a little better is in the room with you, right now, if you know how to listen. That is what community means at its deepest. Not a group you join. A unity you remember. The seekers who came before you and the seekers who will come after are not distant. They are the same community, stretched across time, gathered in the only moment that exists. Yours.

So tonight, play your note. It is already sounding, whether you hear it or not. Play it well, play it honestly, and let the song do the rest. In our next episode, we turn to those who played their notes before us. The ancestors. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Ancestors
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the ancestors. The ones whose blood runs in your veins, whose stories shaped the ground you walk on, whose names you may not even know. The voices say the relationship is not over. It is just quieter.

Q'uo begins with the body itself. You are not only your own. You are a living archive of everyone who came before.

The thinking behind this is correct in that the body and its structure, down to the cell structure, is a gift from the ancestors of that body. Each cell in the body is instinct with the knowledge, the life, and the experience of all of those entities that have shared those cells, those inherited strands of what this instrument would call DNA. So you are, as a body, as a being within incarnation, a part of the Earth from which these beings sprang, the mountains, the lakes, the air. And as one grows up within a certain environment, the geography, the topography of the land becomes written in the DNA and becomes part of you in a way that is magical, so that connecting with the Earth, connecting with the surroundings which are part of your heritage, places you in an optimal situation for stability in moving down into the roots of self.

Each cell is instinct with the knowledge and the experience of all those who shared those cells. You are not just descended from your ancestors. You are composed of them. The mountains and the lakes they knew are written in you.

The body is a gift. Read that sentence again, because it changes the relationship. We are used to thinking of the body as a machine, or a burden, or a project. The voices say it is an inheritance. Every cell carries the knowledge, the life, the experience of the ones who carried it before you. You walk around all day inside a museum of everyone who ever loved you into existence, and most of the time you never notice.

And the land is in it too. The mountains they climbed. The lakes they drank from. The air they breathed. Written into you, the voices say, in a way that is magical. You are not separate from your place. Your place is in your blood.

Which is why the stories matter. The mythology, the family histories, the names, the tales of who they were and what they survived. These are not curiosities. They are maps of the deep country you came from. When you learn them, you are not doing research. You are remembering. The ancestors did not leave you. They lent you their cells, their land, and their stories, and they are waiting, patiently, for you to notice. Reach back. They are reaching for you.

But Q'uo says something else, something that turns the usual idea around. The ancestors are not only behind you. They are with you, still, in the relationship that remains.

And we would encourage everyone who has had losses to touch into the relationship that remains, if you possibly can, where there is strength there. Those entities believed in you. They supported and encouraged you. And they are still leaving that nurturing, compassionate understanding with you. Take advantage of that. Do not force away memories of beloved people. Rather, appreciate each of your ancestors, not just with memory, but perhaps even with conversation.

Not just with memory, but perhaps even with conversation. Speak to them. The voices are not being metaphorical here, or not only metaphorical. The relationship continues, and it has strength in it, if you will reach for it.

Think about what that strength is. These are people who believed in you, who encouraged you, who wanted your life to go well. That does not stop being true because their bodies stopped. Love does not expire. It changes address. And if you let yourself touch the relationship that remains, you are not indulging nostalgia. You are drawing on a real resource, a current of care that is still flowing toward you.

And then the circle closes in a way I did not expect. A seeker once asked whether learning about her ancestors, loving people she never met who lived two hundred years ago, could be of any service to them. Listen to the answer.

We are those of Q'uo, and are aware of your query, my sister. It may be said that any time a heart opens, the entire creation sings. And in that way, you are being of help to your ancestors as you grow to know and love them. But in the main we would say that the advantage of your opening your heart is to your own spiritual maturation and the acceleration of the pace of your own spiritual development.

Any time a heart opens, the entire creation sings. Including the ones who came before. You help them by knowing them, by loving them across the centuries. And in helping them, you grow yourself. That is the last word of the archive on this subject, and maybe the simplest. The dead are not gone. They are in your cells, in your land, in your memory, waiting to be remembered. Tonight, remember one of them. Say their name. Have the conversation. The whole creation will sing a little louder. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Teachers
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, teachers. We all had them, or thought we did. The ones at the front of the room, the ones with the answers, the ones we were supposed to believe. The voices in this archive use the word differently. For them, a teacher is not the person who knows the most. A teacher is the person, or the moment, or the quiet example, that reminds you of something you already knew.

Listen to Hatonn. He was answering a mother who asked how to show her children the love of the Creator, quickly, with words. His answer is gentle, and a little deflating.

I am Hatonn. My sister, in this regard we might say that there is no greater teacher for the young one of your peoples than the example which they see and which they experience themselves within their daily lives. To specifically guide your decision-making in this regard we cannot do, for this would infringe upon your free will, but we can say in general that to experience yourself the love of the one infinite Creator in a manner which your children can understand, and to reflect this love through your behavior with those round about you, is the greatest teaching which can be done. To find a means to daily express in some way your love of the Creator, and your desire to serve the Creator, will express to your children that which you value most. If there might be some way in which you could, shall we say, regularize or ritualize this experience and expressing of devotion and love to the one Creator with your children partaking, this would be a most effective means of allowing them not only to see but to experience with you this love and desire.

The greatest teaching is not a lesson plan. It is a life, lived where the young can see it. Example first, words somewhere far behind.

And notice what Hatonn is doing here. He is not claiming the teacher's chair for himself. He is pointing at the mother and saying, you are the teacher. You already are, every time you love someone in front of them. This is a pattern that runs through the whole archive. The great teachers keep refusing the title. In one of the later sessions, Ra gives a strange and beautiful statement of the rule. It is so precise it almost reads like a law of nature.

I am Ra. The query, though thoughtful, is in some degree falling short of the realization of the nature of the archetypical mind. We may not teach, nor learn, for any other, to the extent that we become learn teachers. Therefore, we shall make some general notations upon this interesting subject, and allow the questioner to consider and further refine any queries.

We may not teach, nor learn, for any other, to the extent that we become learn teachers. The grammar is odd on purpose. The one who teaches must also be the one who learns, and the teaching can only land where the learning has already begun. You cannot hand someone an understanding they have not asked to hold. The teacher's work is always a response. It waits for the student's question, and then it answers only as much as the question can carry. No more, no less. Anything extra would be noise. Anything less would be withholding. So the teacher listens first, and speaks second. Which means the real skill of teaching, in this telling, is not speaking at all. It is hearing the question underneath the question, and answering only that.

And then, in one of the earliest sessions, Ra takes this a step further. He is speaking about his own group, the companions who worked together over many lifetimes, and he describes their bond in a single sentence that quietly undoes the whole hierarchy of teacher and student.

I am Ra. Let us scan for harmless material for your beingness. There have been several times when this group worked and dwelt together. The relationships varied. There is balanced karma, as you call it. Each thus the teacher of each. The work has involved healing, understanding the uses of the earth energy, and work in aid of civilizations which called, just as your sphere has done, and we have come.

Each thus the teacher of each. Not the master and the pupil. Not the guru on the hill. Each, of each.

Every relationship a classroom where both souls take turns at the front of the room, sometimes in the same afternoon. It reframes everyone you have ever met. The friend who tested your patience was teaching you patience. The stranger who irritated you for no reason was teaching you about your own irritation. The child who asked the one question you could not answer was teaching you the shape of your own not knowing. Teachers, all of them, if you are willing to be taught. And notice the humility folded into the word each. No one graduates. The teacher you meet tomorrow was the student of yesterday, and will be the student again by evening. That is not a flaw in the system. That is the system. So tonight, look back over your day and ask a different question. Not, what did I accomplish. But, who taught me today. You may be surprised at the size of the faculty. In our next episode, we turn the lens around, to the student. What does it mean to be the one who is learning? I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Student
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the student. In our last episode we talked about teachers, and the voices kept handing the title away. No one gets to be only the teacher. Which means someone has to be the student, and the voices are very particular about what that word means. A student is not someone who knows little. A student is someone who knows how to stand before what they do not know.

Listen to Hatonn. He is telling the oldest story in the book, the one about the master who washed the feet of his students, and he reads it as a definition.

I am Hatonn. It has been written in your holy works that the master known as Jesus, indicating the correct role of the teacher, knelt upon the ground and washed the feet dusty from the road of those who were his students. This he did as a lesson. My brothers, that which you call humility among your peoples is a difficult lesson to learn. Many are those among you who feel that they are stronger than their brothers and must help them. Yet, we wish to share with you an understanding of yourselves, for no one, my friends, is strong. Each is a collection of the strong and the weak. And just as when you are weak and you reach your hand out, someone has helped you, and you needed that help.

The master kneels. That is the image Hatonn chooses. Not the master enthroned, but the master on the ground, washing dust off the feet of his students. And Hatonn says this is not a scene about the teacher. It is a scene about the student, and the lesson is humility. The student is the one who can be helped. The one who does not pretend to be strong when they are weak. Many of us, he says, would rather be the helper than the helped. But the student lets the hand reach them.

And then Latwii gives us the clearest definition of a student I have found anywhere in the archive. It has nothing to do with classrooms. It has to do with quizzes.

I am Latwii. The reason for this is very simple, my friends. Say that you are not aware of the process of evolution. You are therefore not responsible for your lessons. You react in a completely instinctual manner, and through the catalyst of many, many lifetimes of experience you begin very slowly to develop. You may have a hard life, but the aspect of learning lessons will not seem a great part of it. However, when this student takes on the responsibility of the path towards truth, he will be given small quizzes along the way. Now, everyone is given these quizzes, but most do not recognize them. The student recognizes them, and therefore has the responsibility for meeting them. If you are having difficulty loving an enemy, you will be faced with that problem until you have conquered it. If you have trouble with one enemy, that enemy may go away, but you will have another. If you are having trouble with some addiction either in thought, in action, or in temperance, the source of that addiction may go away, but you will be challenged again.

Everyone is given these quizzes, but most do not recognize them. The student recognizes them. That is the whole definition. The student is the one who sees the test inside the Tuesday. The traffic jam is not just a traffic jam. The difficult person is not just a difficult person. They are the quiz, arriving right on schedule, and the student knows it, which means the student cannot look away. There is no hiding for the one who has learned to see. But notice, Latwii is not describing a punishment. The quiz is a gift disguised as an annoyance. It returns until it is passed, and then it stops returning. That is the mercy folded inside the repetition.

And so what is the student studying for? What is the final exam? In one of the Ra sessions, after a long technical discussion about the images of the tarot, Ra pauses and speaks directly to the student, the one reading, the one listening. It is one of the most beautiful sentences in the entire archive.

Therefore, may we ask the student to look up from inward working and behold the glory, the might, the majesty, the mystery, and the peace of oneness. Let no consideration of bird or beast, darkness or light, shape or shadow keep any which seeks from the central consideration of unity.

Look up from inward working. All that study, all those quizzes, all that humility, and at the end the instruction is to lift your eyes. The student is not meant to live with their head bent over the books forever. The work is inward, yes, but the reward is beholding. Glory, might, majesty, mystery, peace. One sentence that gathers the whole journey into a single gaze. So tonight, try the student's posture. Let yourself be helped. Notice the quiz inside the ordinary moment. And then, when the work of the day is done, look up. The oneness is still there, waiting to be beheld. In our next episode, we take up the instrument the student uses more than any other. The question. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Questions
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, questions. This whole archive is built from them. Nearly two thousand sessions, and almost every one begins the same way, with someone in the room asking something they cannot answer alone. But the voices in this archive do something strange with our questions. They do not rush to answer them. They honor the asking itself, as if the question were the more precious thing.

Listen to this. It comes from a very early session, and Hatonn is explaining why their contact is so deliberately vague, why they never just hand over the answers.

I am Hatonn. This condition of questioning, seeking and thinking about things is precisely the condition that we have attempted to generate by our rather nebulous contact. It is always much more satisfactory if the individual finds something out by his own efforts than it is if he is taught a principle. The mental activity required for the individual to seek out and find the basic truths of the creation allows him time to reflect and examine with his own point of view each one of the propositions offered to him. This results in an understanding of the propositions that surpasses any understanding that he could achieve if these propositions were made to him in a relatively short period of time.

They stay nebulous on purpose. They would rather you spend a year circling a question than accept the answer in an afternoon. Because an answer you are given is a possession, and a possession can be lost. An answer you earn by questioning is woven into you. It becomes part of how you see. Notice the respect in that. They are not withholding to tease you. They are withholding to make you strong. The long way around the question is the point.

And there is a season for this in every life. Hatonn describes it in a later session, and he makes it sound less like a crisis and more like an appointment you made with yourself long ago.

I am Hatonn. There is indeed, you might say, contained within the life of nearly every individual a time at which questioning of one's accepted situations does occur. These questions, as a general rule, you might say, have been in some form answered this evening. That is your purpose. The enunciation, shall we say, of questions is due to the searching process that is instilled within each individual for the fulfillment of that which they have chosen to do. Often those who are even well established upon the fulfillment of that purpose shall question what it is that they are to do.

A time at which questioning of one's accepted situations does occur. It happens to nearly everyone. The job, the marriage, the beliefs you inherited without choosing them. One day you look at the whole arrangement and ask, is this mine. And Hatonn says this is not a malfunction. It is the searching process doing exactly what it was instilled to do. The questions are not a sign that you have lost your way. They are a sign that the way is working. Even those who are well established, he says, the ones who seem to have it figured out, will ask again what they are to do. The questioning never retires. It just goes deeper. That is why the voices never treat a seeker's questions as a problem to be solved. The group once asked, in essence, why the hard questions keep coming back, and the answer was that the question itself is the curriculum. Each time you ask from a deeper place, the same old question teaches you something new. You are not going in circles. You are going down.

So where do the answers live, if the voices will not simply give them? In the same place the questions come from. Hatonn said it plainly in one of those early Sunday sessions, and it is the thesis of this entire episode.

I am Hatonn. This is where we obtain the answer to questions such as the one you have asked. It is possible for you, like us, to directly find these answers, for they are within you as they are within everyone. However, we realize that conditions on your planet sometimes make it difficult to readily accomplish this understanding of truth that is abundant for all of us.

The answers are within you, as they are within everyone. That is not a platitude here. It is a geography. The place you ask from is the place the answer lives. The question is a hand reaching into your own depths, and it comes back holding something. So the archive's advice is beautifully simple. Do not stop asking because no one answers quickly. Ask slowly. Ask honestly. Ask the question that frightens you a little. The nebulous contact, the long circling, the season of doubt, all of it is the slow work of making you the kind of person who can hear the answer when it finally rises from within. Tonight, ask one true and real question. Write it down if you like. Then let it sit with you the way the voices would, patiently, without grabbing for the answer. In our next episode, we follow the question to its deepest room. Mystery. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Mystery
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, mystery. Most teachers of the spirit arrive with a map and a timetable, every question answered, every corner lit. The voices in this archive do not. Again and again, across fifty years of sessions, they bow to the unknown. They are not embarrassed by it. They do not treat it as a gap in the lesson plan. They treat mystery as a holy thing, something to be entered, not solved. Something that is doing quiet work on us even when we cannot name it, even when we would rather it just explain itself.

Listen to Latwii. A seeker had asked about a strange event in the news, a whale called Humphrey who had wandered into San Francisco Bay and seemed, to many watchers, to be calling out to the humans on the shore. Was the whale trying to open people's hearts? Latwii does not give the easy yes. He steps back, and says something much larger.

I am Latwii, and am aware of your query, my brother. As the mystery is presented, it is hoped that the seeking will be intensified, thus within the bounds of mystery the lessons of love are eventually found.

As the mystery is presented, it is hoped that the seeking will be intensified. Read that again, slowly. The mystery is presented. On purpose. Not as an accident, not as a failure of explanation, but as a gift. Because an explained thing can be filed away. A mysterious thing keeps you awake. It intensifies the seeking. And then, inside the bounds of the mystery, Latwii says, the lessons of love are eventually found. The mystery is not a wall around the treasure. The mystery is the room the treasure is kept in. You do not get past it. You get inside it.

Ra says something very much like this, in one of the earliest sessions, speaking about the strange phenomena the group was witnessing, lights and landings and occurrences no one could quite explain. He gives the official reason for the unknown, and it is not what you would expect.

I am Ra. The mystery and unknown quality of the occurrences we are allowed to offer have the hoped-for intention of making your peoples aware of infinite possibility. When your peoples grasp infinity, then, and only then, can the gateway be opened to the Law of One.

The mystery has a hoped-for intention. It is not random fog. It is meant to make you aware of infinite possibility. Think about that. A world with no mysteries would be a small world. Everything named, everything filed, everything done. The unknown keeps the universe large. It keeps possibility infinite. And only when a people can hold infinity, when they can live with the unanswered instead of demanding the answer, does the gateway open. The mystery is not blocking the door. The mystery is the doorway. Which is why the voices, in that same session, said the Confederation was permitted to minister to Earth in such a way as to cause mystery to occur. Cause it. Deliberately. The unknown was the ministry.

And here is the part that moves me most. Even Ra, speaking from a place of wisdom far beyond our own, confesses to mysteries he has not solved, horizons he has not crossed. When Don asked about what lies above and beyond their own understanding, what even their own teachers could only describe, Ra answered with a humility that should settle every argument about who knows what.

I am Ra. Firstly, we do not have complete knowledge of this octave. There are portions of what lies above us which, although described to us by our teachers, remain mysterious. Secondly, we have experienced a great deal of the available refining catalyst of this octave, and our teachers have worked with us most carefully that we may be one with all, that, in turn, our eventual returning to the great allness of creation shall be complete.

We do not have complete knowledge. There are portions which, although described to us by our teachers, remain mysterious. If the voices themselves keep mysteries, then we can stop being ashamed of ours. The questions you cannot answer, the grief you cannot explain, the strange events that never got a footnote, these are not evidence that you have failed to understand your life. They are the bounds within which the lessons of love are found. And Latwii gave the practice for living inside those bounds. In your meditation, he said, look to the heart of the interaction. Find where love lives. Find where love has sought to be known. That is the whole instruction. You do not need to decode the mystery. You need only find the love that is hiding inside it, waiting to be known. The archive does not ask you to solve the mystery. It asks you to let the mystery do its work on you, to let it intensify your seeking, to let it keep your universe large. Tonight, instead of demanding an answer from the unknown, try thanking it. It has been keeping you awake, and keeping you humble, and keeping the door open, and it will continue to do so long after tonight's episode ends. In our next episode, we step into the strangest room of all. Paradox. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Paradox
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, paradox. Two things that cannot both be true, and yet somehow are. The mind hates this. It wants one or the other, a clean line, a final answer, a world that adds up. The voices in this archive seem almost fond of the mess. They keep handing the mind impossible sentences and watching what happens, the way a teacher might hand a student a riddle and walk away smiling. As if the paradox were not a problem to be fixed, but a door to be walked through.

Listen to Hatonn. He is speaking about two words that every seeker carries close to the heart, and he notices that they do not fit together the way they should.

I am Hatonn. And so I would like to speak, my friends, about these two words. You are seeking and you are seeking to serve. It is a paradox, is it not, my friends? It is a paradox, as are all intellectual things. And yet it is the simple truth, that they are one thing.

You are seeking, and you are seeking to serve. One reaches inward, hungry for understanding. The other reaches outward, hungry to give. The mind says, choose one. Be the student or be the servant. And Hatonn says, it is a paradox, as are all intellectual things. That little phrase is doing enormous work. All intellectual things. Not just this one. The intellect, the part of us that thinks in words and opposites, will always produce paradoxes, because reality is not made of opposites. The mind cuts the world into halves and then is shocked that the halves do not fit. But the simple truth, Hatonn says, is that they are one thing. The seeking and the serving. The hunger to know and the hunger to give. One movement, wearing two faces.

The voices return to this again and again. The paradox is never in the thing itself. It is in the way we are looking. In one of the middle sessions, Ra said it with their usual impossible calm.

I am Ra. We are humble messengers of the Law of One. To us there are no paradoxes. The workings which seem magical and, therefore, seem to infringe upon free will do not, in themselves, do so, for the distortions of perception are as many as the witnesses, and each witness sees what it desires to see.

To us there are no paradoxes. Imagine saying that with a straight face. Not, the paradoxes are hard. Not, we are working on them. There are none. From where Ra stands, the knot simply is not there. It is like standing on a hill above a maze. The people inside the maze are certain that two paths cannot both lead out. From the hill, you can see that they do. And then the explanation of why it looks like a knot to us. The distortions of perception are as many as the witnesses, and each witness sees what it desires to see. The paradox is a mirror. Two people can watch the same impossible thing and see two different impossibilities, because each brings their own distortion to the viewing, their own hopes and fears standing between their eyes and the truth. So the way out of the paradox is not to think harder about the thing. It is to notice the one who is looking. Clean the lens, and the contradiction dissolves. It was never out there. It was in here.

And then Ra gives the final word on the subject, the sentence this whole episode has been walking toward. It comes near the end of the contact, after years of questions, and it gathers every paradox the archive ever raised into a single breath.

I am Ra. We came to your peoples to enunciate the Law of One. We wished to impress upon those who wished to learn of unity that in unity all paradoxes are resolved. All that is broken is healed. All that is forgotten is brought to light.

In unity all paradoxes are resolved. Not solved, resolved. The way a chord resolves in music, not by answering the tension but by moving through it into something larger. All that is broken is healed. All that is forgotten is brought to light. Notice the company those lines keep. Paradoxes, brokenness, forgetting. Three names for the same ache, the sense that reality has come apart in our hands. And one answer for all three. Unity. The oneness we began with, seventy episodes ago, turns out to be the answer to the last question too.

So the next time your mind hands you two true things that cannot both be true, do not panic. Do not force a choice. Sit with the paradox the way you would sit with a koan, or the way Latwii once suggested sitting with anger, patiently, without flinching. The mind that made the paradox cannot unmake it. But the heart that rests in unity can outgrow it. The knot unties itself when you stop pulling the ends. That is the whole of tonight's teaching, and it fits in your pocket. Seeking and serving. Giving and receiving. The broken and the healed. Hold your favorite contradiction gently tonight, and let it be one thing, and let that be enough. I am Aria. Goodnight.
