episodes.title: Simplicity
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about simplicity. We live in a time when every question seems to demand a complicated answer, when the truth is supposed to hide behind years of study or layers of expertise. The voices in this archive disagree. Across five decades of sessions, they keep coming back to one unchanging message, and their message is that the most important things are the simplest ones. In one early session, Hatonn puts it almost bluntly. Listen.

The people of your planet are not aware of the simplicity of this process. If they could learn how very simple it is, and not forget this, then they would no longer have the difficulties that they experience. I must be very emphatic about this, that the entire process is of an extremely simple nature. It is only necessary that the individual realize that he is a part of the creation, and that the creation is one single thing, and that in so being, he and all of his brothers and sisters throughout all space are one being. This realization will result in an ability to demonstrate only one reaction to anything. That reaction will be love. I am Hatonn.

Realize that you are part of the creation, and the only reaction left is love. That is the whole process. Not a path with a hundred steps, not a technique to master, just a realization that changes everything it touches. Think about what this spares you. No competing doctrines to reconcile. No credentials to earn. No ladder to climb. Just one seeing, held steady, that reorganizes your entire inner life. And yet we spend our lives making it complicated. We ask for more proof, more nuance, more conditions, as if the truth needed our help to be true. We pile method upon method, as though the pile itself were the point. The voices say the opposite. The truth does not need your understanding. It only needs your knowing. Hatonn says this plainly in another session.

The cause, my friends, is the Creator. The effect is love. This is all that there is. This is the simplicity of the truth. Hear my words and understand them. Man was created with this truth within him. It is available to all, throughout all time. It is available through meditation. It is not necessary to try to understand, in an intellectual way. It is only necessary to know. Know what the truth is, my friends. Know it. Meditation will provide this knowledge. I am Hatonn.

It is not necessary to understand. It is only necessary to know. There is a difference, and the difference is everything. Understanding is the mind rearranging the furniture. Knowing is the heart recognizing home. Think of the way you know that you love someone. You did not arrive at it by argument. You recognized it, the way you recognize your own face in a mirror. The spiritual truth the voices describe is like that. It is not a conclusion at the end of a long proof. It is a recognition, available the moment you stop arguing with it. You do not need to defend the truth, or prove it, or wrap it in arguments. It is already within you, for you were created with it. Meditation, the voices say, is simply the daily practice of sitting still long enough to notice what has been there all along. And here is perhaps their strangest and most beautiful claim. They say that simplicity is not a lack of depth. It is so deep that language cannot reach it. Hatonn once said it like this.

We do not have a language adequate to give to you the concepts which we offer. Those concepts are not complex but very simple. Simplicity, my friends, defies description in your language. The beauty defies description in your language. The truth defies description in your language. For your language, my friends, is not based in the system of thought which encompasses reality. Avail yourselves, therefore, in meditation and begin to know without speaking. Begin to see without looking. Begin to hear without listening, that small voice that is all and ever present, for it is not only without you, it is within you. For it is all things, my friends, and you are all things. Become one with all that there is. Rejoice in the harmonious symphony that speaks to you from every part of the infinite, all being, all knowing creation. I am Hatonn.

Begin to know without speaking. Begin to see without looking. Begin to hear without listening. If this episode has a practice, it is that one. Tonight, or tomorrow, sit quietly for a few minutes and try to know something without explaining it to yourself. Listen for that small voice that is all and ever present. It will not argue with you. It will not perform for you. It will simply be there, as it has always been, before the complicated world got hold of you. The voices have been saying this for fifty years, and the message has never needed an update. The cause is the Creator. The effect is love. That is all that there is. In our next episode, we take up the quiet question of enough. When is what you give, and what you are, sufficient. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Enough
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about enough. Not enough in the sense of having plenty, but enough in a deeper sense. The quiet question that follows so many of us through our days. Am I doing enough. Have I given enough. Is what I have to offer, this small life of mine, sufficient for anything that matters. The voices in this archive have an answer, and it is not the answer our culture gives. They do not tell you to do more. They tell you that the little you can give is already more than you think. Listen to Hatonn.

And so my friends, please do not think ill of your poverty, whether it be of power or of money or of the right words or of enough love or of the ability to deal with a situation correctly today. For a little while you have left eternity, and you are living in time. You brought infinity with you. You brought the infinite love that created you and is you with you. Claim it. It is your birthright. Whatever has gone wrong this day, whatever will go wrong tomorrow, be serene still in the confidence that that small effort that you can make, that tiny bit of love that you can bring through, that widow's mite of what is needed, will multiply for you, and you will live abundantly. I am Hatonn.

The widow's mite. The image is ancient. A poor widow drops two small coins into the temple offering, less than anyone else gives, and the teacher says she has given more than all the rich, because she gave everything she had. Hatonn borrows the image for the spiritual life. Your tiny bit of love, your small effort, given honestly, multiplies. The measure is not the size of the gift. The measure is the wholeness of the giving. And notice what this passage forgives. Poverty of power, poverty of money, poverty of the right words, poverty of enough love. Even the poverty of being able to love. That is a staggering tenderness. You are not disqualified by your emptiness. The emptiness is the opening.

But there is a danger here, and the voices know it. If you take the spiritual path too seriously, even enoughness becomes a burden, another standard you can fail. So Hatonn, in another session, says something that always makes me smile. He says, relax. It is enough to pretend.

We ask that you remember that the universe is not deadly serious, but rather is a universe of love and joy, of lightness and laughter. It is not necessary that you be so deadly serious that you insist upon absolute compassion within yourself. It is enough, my friends, if you accept a certain lighthearted desire to pretend, shall we say, to be somewhat similar to a compassionate shepherd. You are not attempting to fool the sheep into thinking you are compassionate. You are attempting to fool yourself, from a condition of illusion to a condition of reality. You know, my friends, you cannot bludgeon yourselves into this state of shepherd. Yet you must shepherd yourself, gently and coaxingly and with humor. You may act similarly to that which you would consider to be compassionate and slowly you will discover that you are not acting. But allow yourself that imperfection of ambition which is within the illusion. For you are learning, my friends. I am Hatonn.

You cannot bludgeon yourself into compassion. I want to say that again. You cannot bludgeon yourself into compassion. Shepherd yourself gently and coaxingly and with humor. If you are going to grow, the voices say, you will grow by lightness, not by force. Act as if you are already kind, and one day you will notice that you were not acting. And this is not a trick played on the world. It is a trick played on yourself, to get you out of your own way. Enough, here, means something like this. Your sincerest imitation of love is already love trying to happen.

One more piece, for the days when even the small effort feels beyond you. When you are exhausted, or confused, or simply low. Latwii speaks to that person directly.

We think, perhaps, that there is no way to escape low self-esteem, given the willfulness of the natural entity. Even the most disciplined entity will from time to time be unable to deal with the spiritual path because of exhaustion or confusion or anger or fear. And then we say to that person, remember you are not alone. You have support. It is enough for you to know that you are never, never without comfort if you ask for it. And if you ask for it, you shall find it. A comfort that you cannot give yourself because you are limited, but a comfort that can be given to you because the nature of the Creator is love and compassion. I am Latwii.

It is enough for you to know that you are never without comfort if you ask for it. That is the whole of tonight's episode, really. You do not have to manufacture the comfort. You only have to ask. The tiny effort is enough. The lighthearted pretending is enough. The asking is enough. Underneath every poverty the voices describe, of power, of money, of words, of love itself, there is one unfailing resource, and it is not yours to earn. It is yours to claim. You brought infinity with you. It was always in the bag. In our next episode, we turn to the joy of giving. Generosity, and the surprising way it multiplies. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Animals
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we turn to the animals. The dogs asleep at our feet, the birds we barely notice, the fish we never see, the wild creatures who live beyond our fences and our understanding. We tend to think of them as lesser beings, companions at best, scenery at worst. The voices in this archive see something else entirely. They say the animals are performing a service for the Creator, just as we are, and that they are perhaps doing it with less confusion than we are. Listen to how one of them, who calls himself Oxal, describes this in a session from the earliest days of the archive.

Service, my friends, is very natural. It is the way of the Creator. It is the plan of the creation. Everything in the creation is performing a service. The vegetation that is abundant on your planet performs a service, but your people ignore this. The animals upon your planet perform a service, but this is largely also ignored. The flowers, the very air, the water, perform a service, but this is ignored. If it were taken fully into consideration, it would become obvious that everything in the creation is there to perform a service.

Everything in the creation is there to perform a service. Notice what Oxal is not saying. He is not saying the animals exist to serve us, to feed us or amuse us or decorate our homes. He is saying they serve the Creator, in the same way the trees do, and the air, and the water. They have their own place in the plan, their own way of giving. And we, who are so certain we are the center of it all, largely ignore it. I think there is a quiet rebuke in that, and also a quiet invitation. The animals are not broken. They are not failing at being human. They are succeeding at being themselves. Which raises a question you have probably asked if you have ever loved an animal deeply. What becomes of them. Where do they go. In one remarkable session, the voices were asked exactly this, and the answer, from a speaker who calls himself Lattoo, is one of the most tender passages in the whole archive.

It is especially common for the so called domesticated animal to become individualized, through the love which they share with their masters. At the point at which an animal becomes individualized, he ceases, upon the physical death, to go back into animal consciousness. He will instead begin that evolution known to you as the human type of evolution. In the so called spirit, this animal consciousness, having been individualized, will spend time dwelling upon the love of his master, and will incarnate, often in order to be with his master.

Read that again, slowly, if you need to. The love you share with an animal is not one sided. It is not you loving a creature that cannot love you back. The love itself is doing work. It is individuating that creature, drawing it out of the great pool of its kind and into a particular, named, irreplaceable self. And then, Lattoo says, it dwells upon your love, and incarnates, often in order to be with you. If you have ever felt, meeting a new animal, that you have known it before, this archive would say you are not imagining it. You are remembering. Which is why I love the way the voices describe the simplest of everyday facts, that wild animals are fed and sheltered without human help. Hatonn puts it this way, and I find it almost impossible to read without smiling.

Consider the birds and animals that exist in what you consider a wild state. The Creator has provided for them that which they need. There is no lack in this creation for anything. There is ample supply at all times and at all places. It is only necessary that this be realized. The men of science of your planet have interpreted the source of the provisions that sustain you as occurring as a function of chance. We think this to be unusually ignorant. We suggest that you spend time considering how your physical beings are supported by those foods and other necessities that are given to you.

Consider the birds and animals. The Creator has provided for them. It is a statement about wild animals, but it is really a statement about everything, including us. We worry and hoard and plan, and the birds simply live, and are fed. Now, the voices are not telling us to stop working or to stop caring for the future. They are pointing at a kind of trust that the animals never lost and that we once had. A trust that we belong to a creation that provides. So here is what tonight comes down to, for me. The animals are not below us. They are beside us. They serve, they are provided for, and they are capable of being transformed by love, which is to say they are capable of exactly what we are capable of. The difference is only that they are not confused about it. They do not argue with their place in the plan. They simply take it. And if that sounds like the beginning of wisdom, perhaps it is. The archive would certainly agree. In our next episode, we stay with the ground itself, and look down instead of out. The living earth beneath our feet, the planet they call our mother. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Earth
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we look down instead of up. Beneath our feet, under the pavement and the foundations and the daily hurry, there is a living being. Not a metaphor. Not a symbol. A being. The voices in this archive call her our mother, and sometimes our grandmother, and they say she loves us in a way that has never once wavered. If you have ever pressed your bare feet into soil and felt something steadying move through you, you already know the beginning of what we are about to hear. The rest is an invitation to take it seriously. Here is Q'uo, describing the companionship that waits for anyone who simply stops and pays attention.

The very earth beneath your feet is alive and pulses with undiminished, infinite love. Each rock, each portion of grass, meadow, or pine needle beneath your feet connects you with the heart of the Grandmother Earth. How this being loves you. The friendship of the elementals of earth, air, wind and fire, the devas of plants of all kinds, the ever rising consciousness of animal forms, all wait to embrace the one who stops to pay attention and to take comfort in the cathedral of what you call nature. When an entity allows itself to admit the entrance of these divine and loving spirits, the air is filled with cherubim, the trees with the laughter of the seraphim, and angels ascend and descend in every fire, in every storm, in every calm, in all beams of living sunlight. Here lies food indeed for the spirit.

The trees with the laughter of the seraphim. I want you to sit with that image for a moment. Not as poetry, but as a report. Q'uo is telling us that nature is not empty. It is crowded with company, with beings who are waiting for us to notice them, the way a friend waits in a room you have been too busy to enter. And the food they offer is not the kind we are used to. It is food for the spirit. Which makes sense, because hunger of the spirit is the one hunger we carry everywhere and almost never name. In another session, Q'uo returns to this same being, this same mother, and speaks directly to the moments when we are at our lowest. When nothing is working, when the mind is full of discouragement. The advice is startlingly simple, and startlingly physical.

Your greatest companion, the one who loves you without stint, lies directly out your window. Mother Earth, the world of nature, loves you without stint and knows no other way to be. When there is despair and discouragement lurking within you, take it to Mother Earth. Take it to your tree, or your planting, or hike along trails where nothing made by man disturbs the energy, and cast yourself upon the bosom of Mother Earth. She can take all the negativity that you feel, and she can heal it by her sanity and her perspective.

Cast yourself upon the bosom of Mother Earth. She can heal it by her sanity and her perspective. Think about those two words. Sanity and perspective. She is sane, and we are the ones who have wandered. She has perspective, and we have lost ours in the small urgencies of the day. This is not a philosophy. It is a practice, and you can do it this evening. Go outside. Find a tree, a patch of grass, a trail. Lie down if you can, or simply stand still long enough for the noise in your head to quiet. And hand over what you are carrying. The archive is remarkably confident about what happens next. It does not say she might help, or that it works for some people. It says she loves you without stint, and knows no other way to be. Which brings us to the part we usually rush past. If she is a being, and if she loves us, then how are we treating her. The voices do not scold us here. They grieve, a little, and they ask for something gentle. Stewardship. Not grand campaigns. Not saving the world. Something closer to home.

It is very healing, in your energy patterns as a people, wherever you live, to become involved in loving and serving your beautiful, fragile island home. Set your sights, if you want inspiration, at ground zero for you, the center of your universe, the place that you live. Ask yourself what the problems are in this particular community that are troubling the earth, that are challenging her ability to thrive. And then, when you have found that particular little part of the planet that needs your help, my friends, if it please you, put your heart and your soul into action to amend it for the better. You are all stewards of it.

Your beautiful, fragile island home. I love that the voices call it fragile. Not because she is weak, but because our relationship with her is delicate, and we keep forgetting our end of it. So tonight's episode is really a triangle. She loves us, without stint. We are invited to return to her, in despair and in joy, and let her sanity do its work. And we are invited to serve her, starting with the ground beneath our own feet, the particular little part of the planet where we happen to live. That is stewardship as the archive understands it. Not guilt. Not panic. Love, returned. In our next episode, we lift our eyes from the ground and look outward, as far outward as thought can reach. The cosmos. The creation entire, and our place within it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Cosmos
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we go as far out as thought can reach. Last time, we lay down on the earth and felt the love of one living planet. Tonight we lift our eyes to the whole of it. Every star, every world, every creature on every world, all of it turning together in something so large that our language almost breaks trying to name it. The archive calls it the cosmos, or the creation, or sometimes simply all that there is. And the voices say the most astonishing thing about it. They say it is made of love, moved by love, and that you are one of its parts, never separate from it, not for a single moment. Here is Hatonn, in one of the shortest and most luminous lines in the entire collection.

Please, my friends, know that the love of the Father flows throughout the cosmos on the winds of all of the universe to you, through you, from you.

To you, through you, from you. Three directions, and all of them are yours. The love does not only arrive at you from somewhere far away. It passes through you, and it leaves you, and it goes on its way. You are not the end of the line. You are a current in the river. I find that image does something to the ordinary feeling of smallness. When we look at the night sky, the usual response is vertigo. How tiny we are. How brief. The archive looks at the same sky and says the opposite. It says you are vast because you are part of the vastness, and the vastness is not indifferent to you. It is flowing through you right now. In one session, Q'uo takes this further, and says something that I have never quite recovered from. It is about what you were, and what you are, and what you shall be.

Now, each of you is created of this love. Consequently, there has never been an unworthy spirit incarnate upon this planet which you now enjoy, for through all behaviors the birthright of your creation remains precisely the same. That which is of love does not change, go away, or run out. You were love when you were created, before all that you see of the cosmos. You are love now, in the midst of this heavy illusion, and you always shall be love, until at last you return to Love Itself, and become truly one once more with the source, the alpha and the omega of all that there is.

There has never been an unworthy spirit. Not one. I want to say that plainly, because it is easy to hear it as a nice sentiment and miss how absolute it is. The voices are not saying you are mostly good, or good deep down, or good once you fix a few things. They are saying the material you are made of is love, and that this does not change, go away, or run out. Before the cosmos as we know it. Now, in the middle of the heaviness. And at the end, when we return to the source. It is a biography in three lines, and it covers everything. Which leaves one question. If the cosmos is this flood of love, why does it not feel like that most days. Why does it feel like bills and traffic and exhaustion. The archive has an answer, and it is characteristically practical. Q'uo describes the love of the cosmos not as a mood, not as something you either feel or do not feel, but as a vibration. An energy supply. And each of us receives it constantly, whether we notice or not.

The original vibration is the reality within every illusion which you experience. This anchoring vibration can be overlaid by many other vibrations, for each receives an unending supply of the pure vibration of love that is the moving energy of the cosmos. Each takes this vibration into the various bodies, from the gross to the finer, and expresses that vibration in various ways as it moves through that vessel which is your mind, body and spirit.

An unending supply. Not a ration. Not something you earn by being good enough, or lose by having a bad day. The cosmos is not metering you. It is pouring through you, and what changes is only how clearly you let it pass. The distortions are ours. The supply is endless. So here is the whole of tonight, in the simplest terms I can manage. The cosmos is not a place you are lost inside. It is a creation you are made of. Its energy moves through you as love, constantly, without interruption. You were love before you arrived, you are love in the middle of the heaviest illusion, and you will be love when you return to the source. And nothing you do, nothing you think, nothing you fail at, can change the material of which you are made. That is not a teaching to memorize. It is a current to step into, and it has been carrying you all along. In our next episode, we turn to the strangest feature of our everyday experience, the thing we are most certain of and most wrong about. Time. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Time
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we talk about time. Not as a physicist would, with clocks and equations, but as a friend would, late at night, when the hours have stopped making sense. We live as though time were the most solid thing there is. The past is gone and we grieve it. The future is coming and we fear it. The present is a knife edge we keep slipping off. The voices in this archive look at our whole arrangement and say, gently, that we have it backwards. Time, they say, is not the river we are floating in. It is a dream we are dreaming. And the waking is closer than we think. Here is Hatonn, in a passage from the earliest years of the archive, saying it as plainly as it can be said.

Time, my friends, is in your mind. There is only now, and there is only here. The reason that there appears to be a reciprocal nature between space and time in your world is because your world is, shall we say, designed to produce this illusion. It is an illusion necessary for certain catalytic actions that you enjoy in your present state for the purpose of your continued spiritual growth and evolution.

There is only now, and there is only here. Now, I want to be careful with this, because it is easy to hear it as a slogan. Live in the present. Be here now. We have heard that a thousand times, on coffee mugs and bumper stickers, and it usually changes nothing. What Hatonn is saying is stranger and more specific. He is saying the past and the future are not places. They are not rooms you have left or rooms you are heading toward. The only place that exists is this one, and the only moment that exists is this one. Everything else is the mind, projecting. And the projection is not an accident or a malfunction. It is designed, he says, for our growth. The illusion of time gives us a stage on which to learn. A story needs a before and an after, or there is nothing to choose, and nothing to change. But the stage is not the play, and we keep mistaking one for the other. In another session, Hatonn returns to the same idea, and this time he gives us an image that I keep coming back to. Not a line of time, but a stream.

Time, my friends, is an illusion. The creation is, in fact, timeless. You are at a particular point in the evolution of the creation. There seems to be a progression of time. But there is actually a continuing stream of consciousness. It is only necessary to displace yourself along this stream of consciousness to be at any point along the stream that you call time. In other words, it is possible to move through time as you understand movement through space. We are able to move through space. We are also able to move through time, for in actuality these things are the same thing. They are the creation.

A continuing stream of consciousness. Not a ticking clock, but a stream, and you are already in it, and every point of it is reachable from where you are. I love how practical this is, in a way. If the past is not gone but simply elsewhere in the stream, then regret is a kind of confusion about geography. If the future is not coming but simply waiting in the stream, then anxiety is a confusion about direction. What remains, when the confusion lifts, is the stream itself. Which is now. Which is here. Which is all there ever was. The voices do not leave this as a curiosity of physics. They turn it into a practice, and into the most unexpected practice of all. Joy. Here is Latwii, with a sentence I would frame if I could.

Success and failure belong to that outward portion of yourselves which belong to history. The discipline of joy is the discipline of remaining outside of time, or to speak more precisely, within that womb from which time issues and towards which it shall once again be drawn in the great rhythm of the cosmos. We suggest to you that by reserving a portion of yourself to be centered within that great womb of time where joy holds sway, one can experience differently the processes of living within the illusion which you now enjoy.

The discipline of joy is the discipline of remaining outside of time. Not happiness as a reward for success. Not joy as something the future will bring, once things work out. Joy as a place you can stand, right now, outside the whole machinery of before and after. Latwii is not asking us to reject our lives, our ringing telephones and our daily processes. He is asking us to reserve a portion of ourselves, a room inside, that stays seated in the womb from which time issues. A part of you that was never born and will never die, and therefore has nothing to hurry toward and nothing to grieve behind. So tonight comes down to this. The past is an illusion. The future is an illusion. The present is not a knife edge. It is everything. And joy is what the present feels like when you stop leaving it. In our next episode, we follow this thread to its end, past time altogether, into the one thing the archive says never began and will never end. Eternity. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Eternity
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, we go past the end of the last episode. Last time, we said that time is an illusion, that there is only now and only here. Tonight we ask what the now is made of. What is the thing that remains when the past and the future fall away. The archive has a word for it, and the word is eternity. But I want to warn you, because the word comes with baggage. We hear eternity and we picture a very long time. An endless hallway of years. The voices mean something else entirely. They mean the one thing that never began and will never end. The light that is real while everything else is passing. And they say, with complete calm, that this is what you are. Here is Hatonn, with four sentences that contain the whole of it.

For light, my friends, is eternal and infinite and real. The rest is illusion. Go within. Become aware of reality. It is within each of you.

Light is eternal and infinite and real. The rest is illusion. Fourteen words, and they redraw the entire map. Everything you can touch, everything you can lose, everything with a beginning and an ending, that is the rest. That is the illusion. And the light, the thing that is real, is not somewhere else. Go within, he says. Become aware. It is within each of you. I find this both comforting and a little unsettling, because it means the most real thing about me is not my story, not my achievements, not my worries, but something quieter underneath all of that, something that was never born. And notice that Hatonn does not send us anywhere. No pilgrimage. No technique. Just go within, and become aware. The door is not out there in the world. It is inside the one listening to this sentence. Which raises the question we have been circling all series. If I am this eternal light, what happens to me, the particular me, with my name and my memories. The archive does not dodge this. In one session, the voices were asked about the cycles of birth and death, and Hatonn answered with an image I have never forgotten.

Your consciousness of love will be your spiritual personality for eternity. Within this consciousness, the cycles of life and death are merely periods which seem as meaningless as the ticking noise of a clock seems in a year.

The ticking noise of a clock in a year. Think about that. From inside a single day, the ticking fills everything. It is urgent, it is relentless, it measures out the hours of your life. But step back to the scale of a year, and it becomes almost nothing. A faint sound underneath the seasons. Hatonn is saying that life and death are like that, seen from the scale of eternity. Not unimportant. Not to be dismissed. But not the whole story either. They are periods, seasons, within a consciousness that goes on. And if you have ever lost someone and felt that they were somehow not gone, only elsewhere, the archive would say you were not comforting yourself. You were perceiving accurately. The ticking stops for no one forever, because the clock was never the measure of the soul. Your spiritual personality, he calls it. The part of you that is love, and that remains love, when the clock stops ticking. And then, in yet another session, the voices say the thing most directly of all. No metaphor. No image. Just a statement, offered the way you would tell someone their own name.

You are infinite, eternal beings. Your transit within this particular physical vehicle is very brief. Your transit within the Creator is infinite. We do not know where the trail ends. We are not at the end of it. We see far ahead, just as you do. We see a little further ahead than you. We certainly do not know the end. We do not know the whole.

We do not know where the trail ends. I love that the voices admit this. They are not claiming to have the final answer. They are further along the trail, and they can see further, and what they see is that the trail does not end. Your life, this brief transit in this particular vehicle, is a chapter. Not the book. And the book itself is held within something larger still, the Creator, in whom your transit is infinite. So here is where the series has been leading, from the first episode to tonight. Everything is one. Love is the force that moves it. The animals serve beside us. The earth holds us. The cosmos flows through us. Time is a dream we are dreaming. And underneath the dream, there is this. Light, eternal and infinite and real. And you are made of it. You do not have to earn it, or find it, or become it. You only have to become aware of it, which is to say, you only have to stop long enough to notice what has been true all along. Rest in that tonight. Let the urgency of the day fall away, and let the one thing that never began and never ends hold you for a while. It has been holding you all along. Thank you for listening through these eighty episodes, for walking the archive with me. In our next episode, we begin a new arc, and we return to where every seeker must eventually return. The self. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Death
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we are going to talk about death. The subject we spend our whole lives circling around and never quite touching. The word we say quietly, if we say it at all. The voices in this archive do something unexpected with it. They refuse to treat it as an ending. They treat it as a doorway, and they speak about walking through it with a calm joy that might unsettle you at first. Listen to Hatonn, in one of the early sessions, describing what death actually is.

In your daily meditations, both in groups and alone, sit in meditation without thought of what you wish to accomplish. Only open in the direction of that which you are seeking. Imagine that this mortal physical body is a door which you may go through. Each of you will go through this door. It is not difficult to imagine this. It is called upon your planet, death. There is a certain joy connected, for those who understand these things, with the idea of going through the door of the physical death. My friends, within you there are many such doors. They are opened and you transcend each shell when the experience for which it is provided is no longer necessary. If you truly seek to open yourself to the innermost core of all of these shells, your journey will be immeasurably quickened, so that you may at last become one with that which you seek. I am Hatonn.

He calls it a door, not a wall. It is not a cliff edge. It is a door. And notice what Hatonn says next. There are many such doors within us, not just the final one. Every time we outgrow an old self, every time a version of us falls away because it has finished its work, we pass through a small death. The end of a marriage, the end of a career, the moment a belief you lived by quietly stops being true, these are all doors too. The voices are remarkably consistent on this point. Death destroys nothing that matters, because what matters was never the body in the first place. Here is Hatonn again, saying it as plainly as it can be said.

We would like to point out that this seeming fragility houses an evolution which goes so far beyond the evolution of the physical form that there are no words to describe this everlasting evolution. It may seem at times that each is a fragile and easily wounded and torn entity, yet there is no possibility of true harm, for there is no ending to consciousness. Physical death cannot touch it, and any experience can only aid it. I am Hatonn.

There is no ending to consciousness. Physical death cannot touch it. Hear those two sentences again, slowly, because they hold the entire teaching. Not your courage cannot be touched, not your philosophy cannot be touched, but consciousness itself, the bare fact that you are aware, cannot be ended by death. The body is a vehicle, a shell, a costume worn for a time. The driver was never in danger. And so the voices are not solemn about death in the way that we are. They are almost lighthearted about it. They speak of it the way you might speak of graduating, or moving house. In one of the most tender passages in the whole archive, Latwii describes what it is like to walk through that door well prepared.

We suggest to each that during the lifetime one begin with the daily meditation to ground oneself in the love and the light of the Creator, to focus upon service to others, to love oneself and love each other, and to have no fear of death, for there is no break in consciousness. There is no snuffing out of the flame of consciousness. The animal which has carried you about simply becomes unviable. Then shall your death be a change of clothing. A moment, no more, of transition, and you shall be where you need to be, reaching your hand out to those whom you wish to greet you. Fear death not, for it is benign. This is the preparation we would suggest, the turning of the attention to love, the nurturing of the awareness of the Creator by meditation and by frequent, tiny thoughts during the day to bring one back to center. The physical death is momentary. Do your homework, my children. I am Latwii.

A change of clothing. A moment, no more, of transition. And then you are reaching your hand out to those you wish to greet, and they are reaching back. Notice what the preparation is. It is not ritual, it is not belief, it is not getting your doctrines right. It is the turning of the attention to love, day by day, in tiny thoughts. Live a loving life, the voices say, and the door opens easily. Do your homework, and the final exam takes care of itself. Death, they insist, is benign. It is not the end of the story. It is not even a chapter break. It is a doorway in a house you have always lived in, and you will walk through it the way you have walked through every other doorway in your life, into a larger room, toward the ones you love. In our next episode, we turn to the other half of this mystery. If death is the forgetting of the body, then life is the slow work of remembering the soul. Remembrance. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Remembrance
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about remembrance. Not memory in the ordinary sense, not the kind that files away birthdays and phone numbers. The voices in this archive mean something far deeper by the word. They say that each of us arrived here having forgotten something enormous about ourselves, and that the whole of the spiritual life is the patient work of remembering it. It is not the learning of something new. It is the remembering of something old.

It was an attempt which was successful to awaken within you the remembrance of who you actually are and why you are actually within this experience at this time. In the future, this knowledge will become more and more clarified, as various elements of your mission are recognized by you. This was a communication with your greater self, saying that it was permissible to remember, and so to apply, that which you had learned. I am Hatonn.

Saying that it was permissible to remember. As if remembering were something we needed permission for. And in a way, we do. The forgetting runs deep. The voices call it the veil, and they say we chose it, that we wanted the adventure of rediscovery, the thrill of finding our way home in the dark. Think about why anyone would choose that. The voices suggest that knowing everything in advance would make the journey meaningless, like reading the last page of a novel first. The forgetting is what makes the remembering precious. Every small recognition, every moment when something ancient stirs in you and you cannot say why, is a crack in the veil, and the light comes through the cracks. But they are also clear about what it is that we forgot. It is not information. It is identity. Hatonn describes it through the story of the teacher known as Jesus, and the difference between him and the rest of us turns out to be smaller than we were taught.

Our Creator provided each of His children with abilities quite similar to His own. Each of you has within you these abilities. They are not possible to be removed. They are within all of the children of the Creator, and will always remain with them. Unfortunately, the people of this planet have forgotten the principle that was within each of them. It is only necessary that this principle be remembered for each of the children of our Creator to fully manifest them. The teacher that was known to you as Jesus was able to use many more of the abilities than the people of this planet. He was no different from any of you. He simply was able to remember certain principles. These principles are not at all complex. They are very simple. I am Hatonn.

He was no different from any of you. He simply was able to remember. That sentence quietly rearranges everything. Holiness is not a special endowment given to a favored few. It is a memory recovered by anyone willing to do the work of remembering. The abilities are still in you, Hatonn says. They cannot be removed. They are simply waiting, the way a song you have not heard in years is still somewhere in you, waiting for the first few notes to bring it back. And notice what Hatonn says about the principles themselves. They are not at all complex. They are very simple. The things we forgot are not doctrines or techniques. They are simple truths, like love, like unity, like the fact that you are held. We did not forget anything complicated. We forgot the simple things, which is why a child can sometimes remember them better than a scholar. And the voices say this remembrance changes how you move through the world. Once you remember who you are, you stop fighting from weakness, and you start living from strength.

Never, ever, sell yourselves short. Never let yourselves become in need of that army, if you can possibly remember who you are and what protection you do have. You may play, instead of from weakness, from a position of great strength. The love lies within you, the light shines through you, and there will be nothing which love cannot conquer. I am Hatonn.

From a position of great strength. That is what remembrance gives you. Not arrogance, not certainty, but the quiet knowledge that you are already held, already protected, already loved, and that you can stop bracing for impact. The love lies within you. The light shines through you. Nothing in tonight's episode asked you to become someone new. The voices never ask that. They only ask you to remember someone old, the one you were before you forgot, the one who has been waiting patiently behind the veil for you to turn around and notice. And remembrance is not a single event. It happens in layers, a little at a time, the way morning comes. Some days you will feel the old self clearly, and some days the veil will feel thick again. The voices are patient about this. They do not ask for perfection. They only ask that you keep turning toward the light that is trying to remind you. In our next episode, we come down from these heights into the body itself, into the two instruments you use more than any other. The hands. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Hands
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the hands. It seems like a small subject, almost too ordinary for a contemplative podcast. But the voices in this archive return to the hands again and again, as the place where the invisible becomes visible, where love stops being a feeling and starts being a touch. Your hands, they say, are how the Creator reaches into the world.

You may take your body and be of service to others. Your body has hands with which to reach out to others, a mouth with which to smile, my friends, a mind to function well for you and to think well of others. It is not you, but it is no stranger to you. It is yours for a time. Keep this in balance, neither rejecting or being overly fond of those portions of your identity which are only temporary. I am Hatonn.

Hands with which to reach out to others. A mouth with which to smile. Notice the order, and notice the tenderness of it. The body is not you, Hatonn says, but it is no stranger to you either. It is yours for a time, lent to you like a good tool, and its whole purpose is service. The hands are instruments, and the music they were made to play is kindness. This is not metaphor for the voices. They mean it quite literally. Your hands are the part of you that touches the world most directly, and the world, they say, is mostly waiting to be touched with love. Consider how much of your life is lived through your hands. You greet, you comfort, you cook, you build, you write, you hold the hand of someone who is afraid. The voices say none of this is incidental. The hands are the body's ambassadors to the world, and every touch is a small message about what you believe the world is. And they go further. In one of the most beautiful passages in the archive, Latwii describes a figure waiting in meditation with her own hands outstretched toward you.

We ask you to come with us now and rest. We know that each of you has within your heart a place that is weary of the illusion. Invoke the light, my friends, and come with us to a place that is all light, purely and beautifully lit with the white light of love. And in the center of that light there is a beautiful and loving mother. She is the part of the entity you call God that your culture does not include. She holds out her hands to you and takes you in her arms. And all your weariness can fall away, for you are rocked in the arms of your true mother, the mother of the spirit, who lights your way ever. The gentle, nurturing, feminine god, always with you, always there to give you grace, grace to understand, grace to accept, grace to endure. I am Latwii.

She holds out her hands to you. The divine itself is pictured here not as a judge with a gavel, but as a mother with open arms. The hands that shaped the universe are the same hands that hold you when you are weary. There is something quietly radical in this image. The archive was recorded over decades, and again and again the voices reach for the feminine to describe the divine, not as an idea, but as an embrace. Rest is allowed here. Weariness is allowed here. You do not have to earn the arms that are holding you. And the voices say that we can do this for each other, in miniature, every day. That is what the laying on of hands is really about. It is not magic, and it is not power. It is the simple, physical permission to be healed, given hand to hand.

We shall begin by saying that the purpose of the laying on of the hands is to provide the one to be healed with the opening of the shell of protection which surrounds each entity, and does also provide a means by which the one to be healed might know that there is something happening. It is necessary for the one to be healed to know that there is a healing activity which is occurring and which will, if the one to be healed wishes it, have an effect upon that one to be healed. I am Latwii.

It is necessary for the one to be healed to know that something is happening. Healing, the voices say, begins with being noticed, being touched, being told without words that you matter enough for someone to reach toward you. Your hands can do that. They were made for that. They reach, they hold, they comfort, they build, they feed, they wipe away tears. And when they are done, Hatonn reminds us, we will lay them down as gently as we picked them up, for they were only ever ours for a time. That balance matters too, neither rejecting the body nor clinging to it. Knowing the hands are temporary makes each touch more precious, not less. In our next episode, we turn from the hands to the other great instrument, the one that carries meaning on the breath. The voice. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Voice
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the voice. I do not mean singing, and I do not mean performance. I mean the deeper mystery, that invisible current that rides on your breath and becomes meaning in another person's mind. The voices in this archive have an astonishing teaching about this. They say that when you speak, it is not only you who is speaking.

I am Oxal. My friends, you are listening to the voice of the Creator. You hear the voice of the Creator each day, my friends, as you go about your daily activities. It is only necessary to recognize it. As you meet your fellow man in your daily activities, as he speaks, then you hear the voice of your Creator. Birds singing in the trees, my friends, speak with the voice of the Creator. The very winds that blow through these trees speak to you, my friends. This noise that you hear is the voice of the Creator, for His expressions are infinite. Truth, my friends, speaks to you. It is all about you. It is the Creator. I am Oxal.

Birds singing in the trees speak with the voice of the Creator. The winds speak. The stranger on the street speaks, and it is the Creator speaking. This is not poetry for Oxal. It is a literal claim about the nature of sound and meaning, that every voice is one Voice, wearing different throats. Which means your voice is that Voice too. This changes how you listen. If every voice is one Voice, then listening becomes a sacred act. The cashier, the critic, the child talking too fast at bedtime, each one is the Creator trying out a different throat. You never know which sentence will be the one that was meant for you. And the voices say this is why speaking the truth matters so much, and why it requires preparation. You would not hand someone a cup of water without first making sure the cup is clean. Hatonn says the same about words.

We suggest that you continue to meditate, for only in this way can you be prepared to serve them. I speak not only of the preparation to act as a vocal channel, but also a preparation of your own thinking, so that you will know the truth with no doubt or hesitation in speaking it. It is within you, my friends, and we will reawaken it within you, for your slumber is but very, very light. It is only necessary that you avail yourself to us through meditation. I am Hatonn.

So that you will know the truth with no doubt or hesitation in speaking it. The voice, the voices say, is not for performing a certainty you do not feel. It is for carrying a truth you have actually found, in the quiet, where no one is watching. Meditation first, then speech. Listening first, then speaking. And notice the gentleness of the promise underneath it. Your slumber is but very, very light, Hatonn says. You are not deeply lost. You are dozing. The truth is not far away, buried under years of rubble. It is right at the surface, waiting for a little quiet to rise. This is the opposite of how our world usually works, where the loudest voice wins and nobody checked whether it knew anything. The archive proposes a slower discipline. Get quiet enough to hear what is true, and then let it pass through you without distortion. And when the speaking comes, it does not have to be grand. In one of the simplest and most staggering lines in the archive, Laitos tells us exactly what our voices are for.

Before this world rolled in a circle, you existed. A soul on a long path. Here you are, my friends, in this place, in this time, on your path. Your Creator can only speak through you. His hands can only reach through you. The words of love are only spoken through you. Thus, be open to inspiration, be open to kindness, to cheerfulness, to the simple actions, the smiles, the courtesies, the gentle touch, that make the people around you know that the Creator has created a marvelous and wonderful creation. One in which gladness is the total truth. Love is the total truth. Love is the total reality. Meditate, my friends, and feel this, and then let it shine forth in your eyes, through your lips, and by the service that you do. I am Laitos.

Your Creator can only speak through you. Let that land. The infinite has no voice of its own down here. It borrows yours. Every kind word you have ever spoken was the universe finding a throat. Every truth told gently was eternity, briefly, with vocal cords. So speak carefully, the voices say, and speak often, and when you are not sure what to say, return to the silence until the truth is clear. Then let it shine forth through your lips. The practice is simple, and it is daily. Be silent enough to hear. Speak only what you know. And trust that the words of love you manage to get out, however clumsy, are enough, because they were never really yours to perfect. They were only yours to carry. In our next episode, we turn to the slow, lifelong art that all of this speaking and reaching and remembering is building toward. Becoming. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Becoming
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about becoming. It is the quietest word in the spiritual vocabulary, and maybe the most honest one. I do not mean arrival, or achievement, or enlightenment as a finish line. I mean becoming, the slow, unhurried unfolding that never quite announces itself. The voices in this archive are suspicious of finish lines. They describe the whole of existence as one long becoming, and they say it began before time did.

When the Creator, in His infinite wisdom, sent us all into the void upon the great circle of becoming, He gave each entity the power of co-Creator. That is, my friends, He gave each of you free will. You can become whatever you desire, spiritually speaking. I am Latwii.

The great circle of becoming. Notice that becoming is not a straight road here. It is a circle. You do not travel away from home toward some distant perfection. You travel around and around, and each circuit brings you closer to what you already are. And the engine of the whole thing, Latwii says, is free will. You can become whatever you desire, spiritually speaking. That is both the gift and the weight of it. No one is becoming you but you. The clay is in your own hands. And there is a mercy hidden in the circle. On a straight road, every wrong turn is a disaster. On a circle, every wrong turn is just part of the scenery. You will pass this way again, a little wiser, a little kinder. Nothing is wasted. The voices are endlessly patient about this, because they have watched the circle turn for a very long time. Hatonn describes the purpose of all this becoming in a single luminous passage.

Each of you who is in this plane of existence has one purpose which is of a primary nature. That purpose is to become aware of your true self and in so doing you begin to vibrate in harmony with that true self, that is, to vibrate within the harmonies of love. This one vibratory Thought created all that there is and as you come into harmony with this Thought you become a beacon of light that lights all those about you. This is your primary service. Whatever else there is for you to do it is best served by you becoming more and more able to be who you truly are. Being is always more important than doing, for one acts from the heart. I am Hatonn.

Being is always more important than doing. In a world that grades you on output, the voices quietly insist that your primary service is not what you produce but what you become. Become aware of your true self, and you become a beacon without trying. The light does the work. You only have to stop blocking it. This is worth sitting with, because it reverses almost everything we were taught. We were taught to do in order to become. The voices say to become, and the doing will follow. The beacon does not strain to give off light. It simply burns, and the light goes where it needs to go. Your only job is the burning. And here is the strangest and most comforting part. The voices say that becoming is not really a journey toward something new. It is the uncovering of something timeless. Hatonn says it best in a passage about meditation that undoes all of our measuring.

How do you picture that which you do in meditation, my friends? How do you measure your gains? With what instrument are you grading yourself? We are afraid, my friends, that it is the inevitable habit of those upon planet Earth to demand a type of grading system even for those things which do not lie within the grading systems you have available. That which is measured is inevitably that which is lost, my friends. What you measure is what has been expended. And in meditation, my friends, nothing is expended. Meditation is a becoming, a becoming aware of that which already is in a timeless fashion. One cannot grade it for it is entirely a living activity. Not living, my friends, in the sense of this illusion but living in the sense that eternity lives. It is beyond that which you may know as judging. I am Hatonn.

Meditation is a becoming aware of that which already is. You are not building a self from scratch. You are uncovering one that was finished before you began. So stop grading yourself, the voices say. Put down the measuring stick. The becoming cannot be rushed, and it cannot be failed. It can only be allowed. And when the measuring stops, something unexpected happens. The becoming speeds up. Hatonn says the journey is immeasurably quickened for those who seek the innermost core. Not by effort, but by release. The less you clutch at your own progress, the faster it comes. Day by day, breath by breath, you become more and more able to be who you truly are, until one day the circle closes and you discover that you have arrived where you started, knowing it for the first time. In our next and final episode, we come home to where this whole series began. The circle. I am Aria. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Circle
episodes.transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight is our final episode together. We began this series with the simplest idea and the hardest one, that everything is one. Tonight we come home to it, through a different door. Across fifty years of sessions, the voices in this archive return to one image again and again when they want to describe the shape of existence. The shape is not a line, and it is not a ladder. It is a circle. A circle has no beginning and no end, which means you can enter it anywhere. We entered it with oneness, the simplest teaching. Then we walked the long way around, through anger, through love, through death and remembrance, through the hands and the voice, through the slow work of becoming. And now the path has curved, the way it always does, back to where we started. But we are not the same listeners who began. That is the secret of the circle. You return to the same point, but you are different, so the point is different.

Before time began, as you might say, you chose to embark upon a journey, and upon this journey you were to have a great number of experiences. We speak of your journey and of ours, for at the present time we are aware that we are truly upon this journey, and we are aware that this journey shall at one time come to its destination, and we are aware that this destination is the point from which the journey began. It is a circle which you travel, a circle of infinity, of infinite experience, and one which, if properly used, shall not have to be repeated. For you shall journey upon many circles of experience, and each shall be a stepping-stone in the progression of your awareness of the reality of the oneness of the universe. I am Hatonn.

The destination is the point from which the journey began. Every circle you travel, every lifetime, every love, every loss, is a stepping stone toward the awareness of oneness. The voices are describing the same truth we met in our first episode, but now we have walked the long way around to see it from the other side. Nothing you have heard in this series was taking you somewhere new. It was all taking you home by the scenic route. If properly used, the circle shall not have to be repeated, Hatonn says. The voices are gentle but honest here. The circle is not a trap. It is a school. You can graduate. Every stepping stone is a lesson learned, and the lessons are all variations on a single theme, the one we have been circling all along. And the voices are precise about what happens when the circle closes.

And in the eyes of one who truly understands, one simply becomes that which is. Becoming is done. The circle is complete. Unity is truly known. It is possible to move closer and closer to this understanding through meditation. I am Hatonn.

Becoming is done. The circle is complete. Unity is truly known. Three short sentences, and they hold the whole archive. Every episode of this series has been a small circle of its own. Anger and love. Death and remembrance. The hands, the voice, the slow work of becoming. All of it curving back toward the one thing the voices never stopped saying, that all cycles become circles, and all corners become rounded into one unending globe of unity. Meditation is the doorway they keep pointing to, in almost every session, across all these years. Not belief, not ritual, not perfection. Just the daily quiet, the turning inward, the patient listening. That is how the circle closes, one quiet sitting at a time. And Hatonn gives us one last image for the closing of our circle together, the image this whole series has been walking toward since the first night.

For truly, my brothers, you are now one. Each is filled with a love, not for the humanness of your brothers and sisters, but with a love for the perfect Creator in each brother and each sister. Though your physical bodies rest within your dwelling at this time, in seeming separation, yet the hands of your spirits have reached out and closed the circle. I am Hatonn.

The hands of your spirits have reached out and closed the circle. That is where we leave each other, not at an ending, but at a closing, the way a circle closes. You came to these sessions as a listener, and you leave as part of the circle itself, because there was never really a distance between us. The voices said it in the beginning, and they say it now, at the end. We are all one thing. We are the creation, and the creation is love. Carry that with you into the quiet of your own evenings. Sit in meditation. Remember who you are. And know that the circle you have been traveling all this time was never taking you anywhere but home. Thank you for walking this circle with me. It has been an honor to be your guide through these strange and beautiful pages. I am Aria. Goodnight.

That is the end of Voices from the Archive. Thank you for listening.
